docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, item):

Description: Executes LLM extraction on a single batch of files. Parses and validates candidate abstractions, ensuring returned file indices map correctly to integers.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): Batch descriptor dictionary from prep().

Returns:

  • list[dict]: List of validated abstraction objects containing name, description, and files (sorted list of integer indices).

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def exec(self, item):
        batch_index = item["batch_index"]
        files = item["files"]
        emit("LLM_CALL_MAP_ABSTRACTIONS", batch_index=batch_index, file_count=len(files))

        context = "".join(f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n" for i, path, content in files)
        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("map_abstractions", mode=item.get("mode", "tutorial"))
        # ... format prompt with language hints and context ...
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="map_abstractions"
        )
        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
        validated_abstractions = []
        if isinstance(abstractions, list):
            for obj in abstractions:
                if isinstance(obj, dict) and "name" in obj and "description" in obj and "file_indices" in obj:
                    validated_indices = [idx for e in obj["file_indices"] if (idx := parse_file_index(e)) is not None]
                    if validated_indices:
                        validated_abstractions.append(
                            {"name": obj["name"], "description": obj["description"], "files": sorted(set(validated_indices))}
                        )
        return validated_abstractions

The method concatenates batch files into a unified context block, builds the prompt from the mode-specific map_abstractions template, and dispatches to call_llm. It parses the resulting YAML and validates each abstraction item, discarding any entries without resolvable integer file indices.

Description: Executes repository crawling by calling crawl_github_files for remote targets or crawl_local_files for local directories.

Parameters:

Returns:

Raises:

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        source = prep_res["repo_url"] or prep_res["local_dir"]
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE EXEC | node=FetchRepo | action=crawl_files | source={source}", dest="LOG")

        if prep_res["repo_url"]:
            emit("CRAWL_REPOSITORY", url=prep_res["repo_url"])
            result = crawl_github_files(
                repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
                token=prep_res["token"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],

        else:
            emit("CRAWL_DIRECTORY", path=prep_res["local_dir"])
            result = crawl_local_files(
                directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )

        files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
        if len(files_list) == 0:
            raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")
        return files_list

The method branches on prep_res["repo_url"], executing remote Git/REST ingestion or local filesystem directory walking. It converts the resulting {path: content} dictionary into a list of tuples, raising a ValueError if all files were excluded or missing.

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Compiles source code context up to the input safety limit, generates the directory tree, and packages execution parameters.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central workflow state dictionary.

Returns:

  • tuple: A 12-element tuple providing context, directory tree, total file counts, localization options, reasoning levels, and token measurements.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "identify_abstractions")

        def create_llm_context(files_data):
            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
            safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level)
            context = ""
            current_tokens = 0
            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)
                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    emit("WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED", index=i, path=path, limit=safety_limit)
                    break
                context += entry
                current_tokens += entry_tokens
            return context, current_tokens

        context, context_tokens = create_llm_context(files_data)
        directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
        return (
            context,
            directory_tree,
            len(files_data),
            project_name,
            language,
            use_cache,
            max_abstraction_num,
            thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
            shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
            context_tokens,
        )

The method employs an internal closure create_llm_context to concatenate files up to safety_limit, warning if files must be truncated. It pairs the concatenated content with the directory tree and returns a 12-element parameter tuple.

Returns:

    @safe_exec

            context, directory_tree, total_files_count, project_name,
            language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level,
            _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode, context_tokens,
        ) = prep_res

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_abstractions", mode=mode)
        # ... prompt interpolation with language instructions ...
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="identify_abstractions")
        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
        if not isinstance(abstractions, list):
            raise ValueError("LLM Output is not a list")

        validated_abstractions = []
        for item in abstractions:
            if not isinstance(item, dict) or not all(k in item for k in ["name", "description", "file_indices"]):

            item["files"] = sorted(set(validated_indices))
            validated_abstractions.append({"name": item["name"], "description": item["description"], "files": item["files"]})
        return validated_abstractions

The method formats the template, monitors token estimation, and calls call_llm. It verifies that the parsed YAML is a list of well-formed dictionaries, expands index range expressions ("0-3"), bounds indices to valid repository files, and returns validated abstraction models.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class AnalyzeRelationships(Node):

Description: Evaluates dependencies, conceptual interactions, and data flow across discovered abstractions. Implements dynamic token budgeting to include as many source code snippets as possible per abstraction without starving any single abstraction, then prompts an LLM to generate architectural relationship edges and a high-level project summary.

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Implements a two-pass token allocation algorithm across abstractions. First distributes available token budget equally across all abstractions; then redistributes unused budget from smaller abstractions to larger ones before serializing file contexts.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central workflow state dictionary.

Returns:

  • tuple: A 10-element configuration tuple containing serialized contexts, abstraction listings, abstraction counts, localization notes, and reasoning controls.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "analyze_relationships")
        num_abstractions = len(abstractions)

        # Build initial abstraction listings...
        # ... token budgeting and pre-computation ...
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        abstr_results = []  # list of (included_files, remaining_files, unused_budget)

        for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files, remaining_files = [], []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        # ... redistribution loop ...
        return (context, "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt), num_abstractions, project_name, language, use_cache, thinking_level, shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000), shared.get("mode", "tutorial"))

The method calculates file sizes across each abstraction, sorting files largest-first. In Pass 1, each abstraction receives an equal share (per_abstr_budget). In Pass 2, any unspent budget is pooled and allocated to abstractions that still have pending files. The final context is constructed with full source snippets for included files and path-only listings for omitted files.

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Dispatches the relationship analysis prompt to the LLM, validates the output schema, and normalizes directional abstraction edges (from, to, label). Wrapped with @safe_exec.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (tuple): The 10-element tuple returned by prep().

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing:
    • "summary" (str): High-level architectural overview.
    • "details" (list[dict]): Edge definitions with keys from (int), to (int), and label (str).

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the LLM output is not a dict, is missing "summary" or "relationships", or if individual edges lack required fields.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        (
            context, abstraction_listing, num_abstractions, project_name,
            language, use_cache, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode,
        ) = prep_res

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_relationships", mode=mode)
        # ... prompt interpolation with language instructions ...
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="analyze_relationships")
        relationships_data = parse_yaml_response(response)

        if not isinstance(relationships_data, dict) or not all(k in relationships_data for k in ["summary", "relationships"]):
            raise ValueError("LLM output is not a dict or missing keys ('summary', 'relationships')")

        validated_relationships = []
        for rel in relationships_data["relationships"]:
            if not isinstance(rel, dict) or not all(k in rel for k in ["from_abstraction", "to_abstraction", "label"]):
                raise ValueError(f"Missing keys (expected from_abstraction, to_abstraction, label) in relationship item: {rel}")
            # ... parse indices using regex \d+ and bounds check 0 <= idx < num_abstractions ...
            validated_relationships.append({"from": from_idx, "to": to_idx, "label": rel["label"]})

        emit("DONE_RELATIONSHIPS")
        return {"summary": relationships_data["summary"], "details": validated_relationships}

The method posts the prompt and validates the resulting YAML. It uses regular expressions to extract integer abstraction IDs from from_abstraction and to_abstraction, checks bounds against num_abstractions, and returns the validated summary and edge dictionary.

docs.title: OrderChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Invokes the LLM to order the abstractions, parsing and validating that the output contains every abstraction index exactly once. Wrapped with @safe_exec.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (tuple): The 10-element tuple returned by prep().

Returns:

  • list[int]: Ordered list of integer abstraction indices representing chapter sequence.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the output is not a list, contains invalid or duplicate indices, or omits any abstraction index.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        (
            abstraction_listing, context, num_abstractions, project_name,
            list_lang_note, use_cache, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode,
        ) = prep_res

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("order_chapters", mode=mode)
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            project_name=project_name, list_lang_note=list_lang_note, abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing, context=context
        )
        emit("LLM_CALL_ORDER_CHAPTERS")
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="order_chapters")
        ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)

        if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
            raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

        ordered_indices = []
        seen_indices = set()
        for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
            # Parse integer, handle '# ' comments
            idx = int(entry.split("#")[0].strip()) if isinstance(entry, str) and "#" in entry else int(str(entry).strip())
            if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list. Max index is {num_abstractions - 1}.")
            if idx in seen_indices:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
            ordered_indices.append(idx)
            seen_indices.add(idx)

        if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
            raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length does not match number of abstractions. Missing: {set(range(num_abstractions)) - seen_indices}")

        emit("DONE_CHAPTER_ORDER", indices=ordered_indices)
        return ordered_indices

The method executes the prompt and parses the YAML integer list. It enforces strict permutation validity: every index from 0 to num_abstractions - 1 must appear exactly once without duplicates, raising a ValueError if any index is missing or out of bounds.

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, item):

Description: Synthesizes or retrieves a single documentation chapter. Handles incremental cache manifest lookups, trims prior chapter summaries to stay within the 50% context limit, calls the LLM, validates output headers, generates a technical summary of the new chapter, and updates instance context. Wrapped with @safe_exec.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): The chapter task descriptor from prep().

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing:
    • "content" (str): The drafted Markdown chapter text.
    • "hash" (str | None): The MD5 cache signature (or None if truncated or generated via fallback).
    • "name" (str): The abstraction name.
    • "cache_key" (str): The manifest cache key identifier.
    • "filename" (str): The destination file path.
    • "summary" (str): The technical summary of this chapter.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the LLM returns an empty completion.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, item):
        # ... extract item parameters and assemble file_context_str ...
        # Incremental Caching Logic:
        current_hash = None
        if incremental and output_dir:
            hasher = hashlib.md5()
            hasher.update(item.get("generation_signature", "").encode("utf-8"))
            hasher.update(file_context_str.encode("utf-8"))
            hasher.update(item.get("verified_facts", "").encode("utf-8"))
            current_hash = hasher.hexdigest()
            # ... inspect manifest and read cached file if current_hash matches ...

        # Context Window Windowing:
        prev_chapters_budget = int(max_tokens * 0.50)
        # ... trim older summaries from self.chapter_summaries ...

        # LLM Synthesis:
        prompt = prompt_template.format(...)
        chapter_content = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="write_chapters")
        if not chapter_content.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"Empty chapter response for '{abstraction_name.strip()}'")

        # Summarization Step:
        summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, chapter_content, language)
        chapter_summary = call_llm(summary_prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=summary_thinking_level, step="chapter_summary")
        summary_entry = f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}"
        self.chapter_summaries.append(summary_entry)

        return {"content": chapter_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name, "cache_key": cache_key, "filename": filename, "summary": summary_entry}

The method evaluates incremental cache status against the manifest file on disk. On a cache miss, it caps accumulated chapter summaries at 50% of the context budget, renders the draft_chapters prompt template, calls call_llm, ensures the title matches the expected chapter number, and invokes an internal summarization call via build_chapter_summary_prompt to provide context for downstream chapters.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):

Description: Graceful degradation handler invoked when chapter drafting exhausts all retries. Injects a placeholder page and placeholder summary into context, ensuring subsequent chapters continue uninterrupted and maintaining alignment in the chapter summary queue.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): The failed chapter descriptor item.
  • exc (Exception): The exception causing fatal failure.

Returns:

  • dict: A placeholder dictionary containing fallback Markdown, an unassigned hash (None), and an unavailable notice summary.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):
        name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
        chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
        emit("WARN_CHAPTER_FALLBACK", chapter_num=chapter_num, name=name.strip(), error=exc)
        notice = get("UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE")
        summary = f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {name.strip()}:\n{notice}"
        self.chapter_summaries.append(summary)
        return {"content": f"# {name.strip()}\n\n{notice}\n", "hash": None, "name": name, "summary": summary}

The fallback emits a warning, appends an unavailable notice to self.chapter_summaries, and returns a placeholder document with hash: None. This omitted hash ensures the missing chapter will be re-attempted on subsequent incremental runs rather than treated as cached.

Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):

Description: Gathers all generated chapters, builds the pending cache manifest in shared, copies summaries to shared["chapter_summaries"], and emits step usage subtotals.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central workflow state dictionary.
  • prep_res (list[dict]): The item task list prepared in prep().

Returns:

Raises:

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

        if shared.get("incremental"):
            shared["pending_manifest"] = {
                res.get("cache_key") or res["name"]: {"hash": res["hash"], "summary": res.get("summary", ""), "filename": res.get("filename")}
                for res in exec_res_list

        shared["chapter_summaries"] = list(self.chapter_summaries)
        del self.chapters_written_so_far

        emit_step_subtotals("write_chapters", "chapter_summary")

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Renders the architectural Mermaid flowchart, resolves UI strings for localization, injects YAML frontmatter (for MkDocs mode), builds navigation configurations, and initializes source verification contexts via utils.chapter_check.source_context.

Parameters:

Returns:

Raises:

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        output_base_dir = shared.get("output_dir", "output")
        output_path = os.path.join(output_base_dir, project_name)
        repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")

        relationships_data = shared["relationships"]
        chapter_order = shared["chapter_order"]
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        chapters_content = shared["chapters"]

        # Generate Mermaid Diagram
        mermaid_lines = ["flowchart TD"]
        for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
            sanitized_name = abstr["name"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ").strip()
            mermaid_lines.append(f'    A{i}("{sanitized_name}")')
        for rel in relationships_data["details"]:
            edge_label = rel["label"].replace('"', "").replace("\n", " ")
            if len(edge_label) > 30:
                edge_label = edge_label[:27] + "..."
            mermaid_lines.append(f'    A{rel["from"]} -- "{edge_label}" --> A{rel["to"]}')
        # Highlight high-indegree foundation nodes...
        # ... Assemble overview, nav snippet, and chapter frontmatter ...
        return prep_result_dict

The method builds a Mermaid flowchart diagram with high-indegree foundation nodes highlighted using the red entryNode class. For MkDocs output, it adds YAML frontmatter (title, sidebar_position) to each chapter and constructs directory-based navigation trees. For standalone output, it prepares an index table of contents linked to full_content.md.

docs.title: CombineTutorial.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Creates output directories and delegates static site or standalone package generation to utils.mkdocs.write_mkdocs_output or utils.mkdocs.write_standalone_output. Wrapped with @safe_exec.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (dict): The render preparation dictionary returned by prep().

Returns:

  • str: The verified absolute or relative path to the generated output directory.

Raises:

  • Exception: Any file system, rendering, or IO error raised during writing.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        output_path = prep_res["output_path"]
        is_mkdocs = prep_res["is_mkdocs"]
        chapter_files = prep_res["chapter_files"]
        ui = prep_res["ui"]

        emit_raw(
            "DEBUG",
            f"NODE EXEC | node=CombineTutorial | action=write_output | output={output_path} | chapters={len(chapter_files)} | mkdocs={is_mkdocs}",
            dest="LOG",
        )
        emit("COMBINE_WRITING_OUTPUT", path=output_path)
        os.makedirs(output_path, exist_ok=True)

        if is_mkdocs:
            write_mkdocs_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files)
        else:
            write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui)

        return output_path

The method ensures the output path exists via os.makedirs. It branches on prep_res["is_mkdocs"], invoking write_mkdocs_output to create static site trees, configuration files (mkdocs.yml), and diagrams, or calling write_standalone_output to generate flat Markdown directories.

docs.title: CombineTutorial.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

Description: Records the final output path in shared["final_output_dir"]. Atomically commits shared["pending_manifest"] to disk as .doc_cache_manifest.json using a temporary file swap to guarantee cache consistency.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central workflow state dictionary.
  • prep_res (dict): Parameter dictionary from prep().
  • exec_res (str): Final output directory path from exec().

Returns:

  • None.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        shared["final_output_dir"] = exec_res

        # Save the incremental manifest only now that the pages it describes are on disk: saved earlier,
        # an interrupted run left new hashes next to old pages, which later runs served as cache hits.
        manifest = shared.get("pending_manifest")
        if shared.get("incremental") and manifest is not None:
            manifest_path = os.path.join(exec_res, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            tmp_path = f"{manifest_path}.tmp"
            with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)
            os.replace(tmp_path, manifest_path)

        emit("GEN_COMPLETE", path=exec_res)

The method assigns shared["final_output_dir"]. If incremental compilation is enabled and pending manifest entries exist, it writes the manifest to a .tmp file and atomically replaces .doc_cache_manifest.json via os.replace, ensuring crash-safe disk state.

docs.title: ExtractFacts._exec_manifest()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _exec_manifest(self, item):

Description: Specialized extraction helper for build manifests (e.g., package.json, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml). Invokes the LLM using the extract_manifest.md template to identify package names, external dependencies, and path aliases. Validates that output conforms to valid YAML against MANIFEST_KEYS.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): Manifest task payload item prepared in ExtractFacts.prep().

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary structured as:
    • "kind" (str): "manifest".
    • "path" (str): Relative file path.
    • "facts_hash" (str | None): The MD5 cache hash, set to None if syntax errors occurred.
    • "claims" (dict): Parsed manifest claims mapping package declarations and path aliases.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if parsed manifest items contain invalid YAML and remaining retry attempts exist.

Example:

    def _exec_manifest(self, item):
        """Declared package names and path aliases of one manifest (prompts/common/extract_manifest.md). A reply
        with items that do not parse is retried uncached; on the last attempt its readable items are kept
        without a facts hash, so the next run asks again."""
        if item["cached_claims"] is not None:
            emit("FACTS_CACHE_HIT", name=item["path"])
            return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": item["cached_claims"]}
        prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"])
        emit("LLM_CALL_EXTRACT_MANIFEST", name=item["path"])
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="extract_facts"
        )
        claims = parse_facts_response(response, MANIFEST_KEYS)
        if claims["unparsed"] and self.cur_retry < self.max_retries - 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{claims['unparsed']} manifest items are not valid YAML")
        facts_hash = None if claims["unparsed"] else item["facts_hash"]
        return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": facts_hash, "claims": claims}

The method checks the item cache before executing call_llm. It parses the response using parse_facts_response bounded to MANIFEST_KEYS. If unparsed items are detected prior to the final retry, it raises a ValueError to trigger an uncached retry. On the final retry, it strips the cache hash to force re-extraction on subsequent runs while keeping the usable items.

docs.title: ExtractFacts._follow_up()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _follow_up(self, item, claims, asked=()):

Description: Multi-turn follow-up extraction coordinator. Evaluates source code line coverage using utils.facts.completeness_hints. If declaration-like or import-like lines remain omitted from claims, it prompts the LLM specifically on those lines (up to FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT lines per turn) for up to FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS iterations, merging the new claims into the accumulated claim set.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): File task specification dictionary.
  • claims (dict): Current claim dictionary extracted during initial passes.
  • asked (tuple | list, optional): Sequence of 1-based line numbers already submitted in earlier follow-up rounds. Defaults to ().

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, dict, int]: A 3-element tuple comprising:
    1. claims: Updated claims dictionary merged with verified follow-up claims.
    2. followup_status: Metadata dictionary containing "status" ("done", "failed", or "none") and "asked" line lists.
    3. calls: Total count of follow-up network calls dispatched.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def _follow_up(self, item, claims, asked=()):
        asked, calls, lines = list(asked), 0, split_lines(item["content"])
        for _round in range(self.FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS):
            hints = completeness_hints(item["content"], verify_file_claims(claims, item["content"]), claims)
            already = set(asked)
            pending = [number for number in hints["uncovered"] if number not in already]
            if not pending:
                break
            note = build_facts_focus_note([(number, lines[number - 1]) for number in pending])
            prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"], focus_note=note)
            emit("FACTS_FOLLOWUP", name=item["path"], count=len(pending))
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
            answer = None
            for attempt in range(2):
                calls += 1
                try:
                    response = call_llm(
                        prompt,
                        use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0 and attempt == 0),
                        thinking_level=item["thinking_level"],
                        step="extract_facts",
                    )
                    answer = parse_facts_response(response)
                    break
                except Exception as e:
                    emit_raw("WARNING", f"FACTS FOLLOW-UP FAILED | {item['path']} | attempt {attempt + 1} | {e}", dest="LOG")
            if answer is None:
                return claims, {"status": "failed", "asked": asked}, calls
            claims = merge_claims(claims, answer)
            asked += pending[:FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT]
        return claims, {"status": "done" if asked else "none", "asked": asked}, calls

The method loops up to FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS times, calling completeness_hints to identify uncovered lines that look like declarations or imports. It constructs a focused prompt with line snippets via build_facts_focus_note. If an attempt fails, it retries once before marking the status as "failed" and preserving all claims collected so far. Verified claims are merged using merge_claims.

docs.title: Shared Store Schema
docs.text:
The centralized mutable dictionary (shared) passed across all nodes throughout the workflow pipeline.

Key Type Description files list[tuple[str, str]] Repository files as (relative_path, content) pairs populated by FetchRepo. project_name str Normalized project name derived from Git URLs, local paths, or CLI inputs. max_tokens int Context window ceiling resolved from model configuration. directory_tree str ASCII representation of repository directory hierarchy. manifest_files list[int] Indices of detected build manifest files in files. abstractions list[dict] Core abstractions with keys name, description, and files (file indices). mapped_abstractions list[dict] Intermediate un-reduced abstractions gathered across batches by MapAbstractions. file_batches list[list[tuple]] Grouped file batches assembled by ContextRouter during "batch" routing. relationships dict High-level system overview summary and list of directional inter-abstraction edges. chapter_order list[int] Validated permutation of abstraction indices defining documentation sequence. module_facts dict[str, dict] Verified per-file facts indexed by path, populated by ExtractFacts. chapters list[str] Generated Markdown chapter documents produced by WriteChapters. chapter_summaries list[str] Compact technical summaries of generated chapters used for cross-chapter context. pending_manifest dict[str, dict] Cache manifest entries waiting to be committed to disk upon generation completion. final_output_dir str Path to the directory containing written Markdown pages or the MkDocs site.

docs.title: Module Facts Entry
docs.text:
Structured fact metadata compiled per module by ExtractFacts and stored in shared["module_facts"] and facts.json.

Field Type Description source_sha256 str SHA-256 digest of raw module source text. lines int Physical line count of the source file. symbols list[dict] Verified exported functions, classes, and methods. depends_on list[dict] Outgoing dependencies with target modules and symbol evidence. used_by list[str] Inverse dependency edges listing modules that import this file. external list[str] Third-party dependencies and system libraries. config list[dict] Environment variables and configuration options read. errors list[dict] Raised, caught, or mentioned exceptions. coverage dict Ratio dictionary with integer keys "claimed" and "verified". completeness dict \| None Line analysis with keys "import_lines", "declaration_lines", "unreported_lines", and "declined_lines". rejected list[dict] Unverified claims where quotes could not be located in source text. missed_imports list[str] Syntactic imports detected in source that were omitted from model claims. unexplained_names list[str] Identifiers referenced in code without local declarations or imports. facts_hash str \| None MD5 signature over inputs; None if parsing failed or was truncated. claims dict \| None Raw parsed claims object extracted from LLM response.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements layered fault tolerance to survive network failures, token exhaustion, and non-deterministic model completions without aborting documentation generation:

  • Centralized Node Interception (@safe_exec): Every node's exec implementation is decorated with safe_exec(). Any unhandled runtime exception triggers an immediate NODE_RETRY_ERROR event via utils.output.emit, formats and records the full stack trace to the log file, and re-raises the exception so PocketFlow can manage retry limits and backoff schedules.
  • Low Coverage Re-Prompting (ExtractFacts.exec): Hallucinated or paraphrased quotes that cannot be found verbatim in source text are tracked by verify_file_claims. If a module generates four or more claims but fewer than 50% can be verified against physical source lines (checked["found"] * 2 < checked["claimed"]), the node raises a ValueError prior to its final retry, forcing an uncached retry to request verbatim quotes.
  • Batch Fallback Mechanisms (exec_fallback): Both ExtractFacts and WriteChapters implement exec_fallback(). If a file or chapter fails across all retry attempts:
    • ExtractFacts retains the best parsed claims from earlier attempts (with "status": "failed") or returns an empty claim set without an MD5 hash.
    • WriteChapters returns a placeholder Markdown document (UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE) with hash: None and inserts a placeholder summary into the context queue. Because failed items have their hash set to None, they are omitted from .doc_cache_manifest.json, ensuring they will be re-attempted on subsequent incremental runs.
  • Non-Blocking Follow-Up Failures (ExtractFacts._follow_up): Network drops or parsing errors during multi-turn follow-up passes are logged as warnings without raising exceptions, returning accumulated base claims with "status": "failed" so the pipeline can proceed safely.
  • Crash-Resilient Manifest Commits (CombineTutorial.post): Incremental manifest files are written to a .tmp file and committed atomically using os.replace. This prevents corrupt manifests if execution is interrupted mid-write.

docs.title: call_llm.py
docs.text: Source: utils/call_llm.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/call_llm.py serves as the primary inference gateway and orchestration module for all Large Language Model (LLM) communications within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder repository. It provides a unified entry point, call_llm(), which abstracts provider-specific connection protocols, client implementations, request and response normalizations, and authentication subtleties. Downstream workflow nodes invoke this unified function without needing direct coupling to the underlying vendor interfaces, whether interacting with Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as Ollama.

The architecture emphasizes cost-efficiency, operational idempotency, and fine-grained observability. Disk caching is implemented through an in-memory singleton backed by a JSON file (llm_cache_v2.json). Cached entries are keyed by a SHA-256 hash combining the provider, model, thinking level, and prompt text. Cache updates use atomic filesystem operations (writing to a temporary file before renaming) to ensure process interruptions never leave corrupt or truncated states on disk. Additionally, the module integrates with a ledger system defined in utils/llm_common.py that intercepts unretryable provider refusals (preventing redundant billed retries on subsequent node cycles) and tracks token consumption, reasoning tokens, cache read rates, and monetary costs.

The execution lifecycle of a language model invocation through this module proceeds through cache lookup, refusal ledger validation, provider-specific routing, token usage recording, and cache serialization:

flowchart TD subgraph Preflight["Preflight and Cache Verification"] startNode["Receive Prompt and Parameters"] checkCache{"Cache Enabled?"} calcHash["Compute SHA-256 Cache Key"] checkMemCache{"Key in Cache?"} returnCache["Return Cached Response"] checkRefusal{"Prior Unretryable Refusal?"} raiseRefusal["Re-raise Cached LLMRefusalError"] end subgraph Routing["Provider Routing and Invocation"] routeDispatch{"Determine Provider"} callGemini["_call_llm_gemini"] callAnthropic["_call_llm_anthropic"] callOpenRouter["_call_llm_openrouter"] callGeneric["_call_llm_provider"] end subgraph Telemetry["Telemetry and Persistence"] measureDelta["Calculate Usage Delta"] emitTelemetry["_emit_call_usage"] validateResponse{"Valid and Untruncated?"} persistCache["save_cache atomically"] returnResponse["Return Generated Text"] end startNode --> checkCache checkCache -->|Yes| calcHash checkCache -->|No| checkRefusal calcHash --> checkMemCache checkMemCache -->|Hit| returnCache checkMemCache -->|Miss| checkRefusal checkRefusal -->|Yes| raiseRefusal checkRefusal -->|No| routeDispatch routeDispatch -->|GEMINI| callGemini routeDispatch -->|ANTHROPIC| callAnthropic routeDispatch -->|OPENROUTER| callOpenRouter routeDispatch -->|Generic / OLLAMA| callGeneric callGemini --> measureDelta callAnthropic --> measureDelta callOpenRouter --> measureDelta callGeneric --> measureDelta measureDelta --> emitTelemetry emitTelemetry --> validateResponse validateResponse -->|Yes| persistCache validateResponse -->|No| returnResponse persistCache --> returnResponse classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class startNode,routeDispatch,measureDelta entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: cache_file
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: cache_file = "llm_cache_v2.json"

Description: The active on-disk filename where the v2 LLM response cache is serialized and stored in JSON format. Responses stored in this file are scoped to individual SHA-256 digests calculated across provider names, model IDs, thinking levels, and the prompt text.

docs.title: LEGACY_CACHE_FILE
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: LEGACY_CACHE_FILE = "llm_cache.json"

Description: The legacy v1 cache file path. Pre-v2 caches keyed responses purely on prompt content without scoping to provider or model parameters. This file is no longer read or written by the runtime, but its presence is checked at startup so users can be alerted to clean up obsolete disk usage.

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def load_cache():

Description: Loads the disk cache into the in-memory singleton _cache. If the in-memory dictionary is already populated, it returns immediately without disk access. If the file is not found, an empty dictionary is initialized. If decoding fails due to an invalid JSON structure or an operating system error, an alert is emitted via utils.output and an empty cache is returned to prevent blocking operations.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • dict: The global cache dictionary mapping hashed cache keys to string completions.

Raises:

None internally; all FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, and OSError exceptions are caught and handled defensively.

Example:

cache = load_cache()
if key in cache:
    cached_response = cache[key]
    emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
    record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)

The function checks the module-level _cache variable and deserializes the JSON cache file upon first call. If a corrupted file is encountered, warnings are dispatched through the centralized event-emitting system while ensuring runtime execution continues uninterrupted with a clean, in-memory dictionary.

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def save_cache(cache):

Description: Synchronizes the current in-memory cache to the filesystem. To prevent data corruption from ungraceful process terminations, the function employs atomic file replacement: it dumps the JSON payload into a temporary file named llm_cache_v2.json.tmp and executes os.replace to atomically overwrite the destination cache file.

Parameters:

  • cache (dict): The dictionary of cache keys and string responses to persist.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

None internally; caught OSError and TypeError events trigger an error emit rather than crashing the pipeline.

Example:

if use_cache and response_text and not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False):
    cache = load_cache()
    cache[key] = response_text
    save_cache(cache)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

This write strategy guarantees that even if a pipeline run is cancelled or terminated mid-write, the existing cache file remains intact. Any failure in serializing or writing to the disk results in a warning log event (WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL), keeping the process alive.

docs.title: notice_legacy_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:

Description: Scans the working directory for the existence of the legacy llm_cache.json file. If located, it calculates the file size in megabytes and emits a CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND event to prompt the user to purge obsolete cache files that consume unnecessary disk space.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

None internally; OSError exceptions triggered during os.path.getsize are silently ignored.

Example:

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from utils.llm_config import check_llm_auth
    from utils.output import emit
    from utils.output import init as init_output

    init_output(language="english", use_cache=False)
    if not check_llm_auth():
        sys.exit(1)
    notice_legacy_cache()

The notice routine serves an administrative role during preflight checks. It calculates disk usage by converting bytes to megabytes and notifies users via output channels, ensuring developers are aware of abandoned v1 cache artifacts.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None, step: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The central public dispatch interface used throughout the codebase to submit a prompt to the configured LLM provider. It resolves the active provider configuration, inspects local caches, checks for previous refusal records, delegates execution to provider subroutines, captures telemetry and usage deltas, and updates the cache.

docs.title: Phase 1: Parameter Normalization and Telemetry Initialization
docs.text:
step = step or "other"
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"{'=' * 80}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}", dest="LOG")

The routine defaults the node execution step to "other" if unspecified. It resolves the active provider and model via resolve_llm_settings(), calculates prompt token metrics using memoized estimation utilities, and logs structured debug entries.

docs.title: Phase 2: Cache Inspection
docs.text:
# Check cache if enabled
    key = _cache_key(prompt, provider, model, thinking_level)
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if key in cache:
            cached_response = cache[key]
            emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)
            emit("LLM_CALL_CACHED", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}", dest="LOG")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit", dest="LOG")
            return cached_response
        emit("CACHE_MISS")

When caching is requested (use_cache=True), the function derives the SHA-256 hash key across the prompt and runtime settings. Upon a cache hit, token estimation metrics are updated, telemetry events are emitted, and the cached response string is returned immediately, bypassing external network overhead.

docs.title: Phase 3: Prior Refusal Verification
docs.text:
# A request the provider already declined this run is declined again: do not re-send it on
    # node retries (rate limits, billed partial output). The node retry still sees the error.
    refusal_key = request_key(provider, model, thinking_level, prompt)
    refused = previous_refusal(refusal_key)
    if refused is not None:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=refused_before (not re-sent)", dest="LOG")
        raise refused

Before dispatching expensive or blocked API calls, the function evaluates whether an identical prompt and parameter combination was previously rejected during this pipeline execution. If an unretryable refusal is on record, the stored exception is re-raised immediately to prevent wasted billing and repeated rate-limit violations.

docs.title: Phase 4: Provider Dispatch and Ledger Tracking
docs.text:
# Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...", dest="LOG")

    # Usage of this call = ledger delta for the provider: it includes every billed request the call
    # made (Anthropic truncation retry, resend after fallbacks were disabled), even when it raises.
    before = usage_snapshot(provider)
    returned = False
    try:
        with usage_step(step):
            if provider == "GEMINI":
                response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "ANTHROPIC":
                response_text = _call_llm_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "OPENROUTER":
                response_text = _call_llm_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
                response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
        returned = True
    except LLMRefusalError as e:
        if not e.retryable:
            remember_refusal(refusal_key, e)
        raise
    finally:
        call_usage = usage_delta(before, usage_snapshot(provider))
        measured = call_usage["calls"] - call_usage["unmeasured_calls"]
        if measured:
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens * measured)
            _emit_call_usage(step, prompt_tokens, call_usage, measured)
        elif returned:  # answered, but the provider reported no usage
            emit("LLM_CALL_USAGE_MISSING", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")

The function captures a baseline usage snapshot from the ledger and routes the prompt within a usage_step context manager to the appropriate provider handler. If an LLMRefusalError occurs and is marked non-retryable, it is recorded in the refusal registry. The finally block computes the ledger delta to ensure that token metrics and request costs are accounted for, even if underlying operations fail.

docs.title: Phase 5: Response Finalization and Atomic Cache Write
docs.text:
elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}", dest="LOG")

    # Update cache if enabled. Empty and truncated responses (llm_common.TruncatedResponse)
    # are never cached — they would be replayed on every later run.
    if use_cache and response_text and not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False):
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[key] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s", dest="LOG")
    return response_text

Elapsed time and completed responses are written to debug logs. If caching is enabled and the response text is non-empty and not flagged as truncated (via TruncatedResponse), the new output is written to the cache and flushed atomically to disk.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The complete prompt text to submit to the model.
  • use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to inspect or populate the response cache. Defaults to True.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Model-specific reasoning budget or level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.
  • step (str | None, optional): Name of the executing workflow node, mapped against NODE_KEYS for token ledger attribution. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The text generated by the model.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: Re-raised or newly raised if the provider rejects the prompt or content filtering blocks completion.
  • ValueError: Raised if the provider configuration is missing required environment variables or returns malformed JSON.
  • RuntimeError: Raised if the provider API response is missing completion choices.
  • Exception: Raised on network failures, timeouts, or unexpected API errors.

Example:

test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

emit("SELFTEST_LLM_CALL")
response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
emit("SELFTEST_LLM_RESPONSE", response=response1)

docs.title: _cache_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:

Description: Constructs an immutable SHA-256 hash identifying an LLM invocation. Scopes the hash to the provider name, model identifier, normalized thinking level, and prompt body to prevent cache cross-contamination across differing configurations.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The prompt string.
  • provider (str): The provider identifier (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI", "OLLAMA").
  • model (str): The specific model name.
  • thinking_level (str | None): The assigned reasoning effort level, or None.

Returns:

  • str: The hexadecimal SHA-256 digest string representing the cache entry.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The function builds a scoping prefix incorporating provider, model, and thinking level parameters followed by a newline, appends the prompt text, encodes the concatenated string to UTF-8, and calculates the SHA-256 digest. This prevents identical prompts run against different models or reasoning budgets from colliding.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches chat completion calls to generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints (used primarily for local engines such as Ollama). It parses environment configurations, configures HTTP headers, applies reasoning effort parameters, validates HTTP responses, parses usage metrics, and returns the completion content.

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment Resolution and Validation
docs.text:
# Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    # Read the provider-specific variables
    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")  # API key is optional, default to empty string

    # Validate required variables
    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    # Append the endpoint to the base URL
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"

The method resolves provider configuration via get_llm_provider(), dynamically references provider-specific environment variables (<PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL, and <PROVIDER>_API_KEY), validates their existence, and constructs the target /v1/chat/completions endpoint URL.

docs.title: Phase 2: Payload Construction and Sampling Adjustment
docs.text:
# Configure headers and payload based on provider
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
    if api_key:  # Only add Authorization header if API key is provided
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        # Ollama reasoning models accept low/medium/high; xhigh/max clamp to high.
        # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
        effort = _clamp_level(thinking_level.lower(), ["low", "medium", "high"]) or "medium"
        payload["think"] = effort
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = effort
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    if rejects_sampling_params(model):
        # Claude Opus 4.7+ / Opus 5.x / Sonnet 5 / Fable reject sampling parameters (400).
        payload.pop("temperature", None)

The payload is initialized with the target model, user message, and default temperature (0.7). If the provider is "OLLAMA" and thinking levels are configured, the effort is clamped to valid boundaries (low, medium, high) and assigned to both think and reasoning_effort keys. If the model rejects sampling parameters (evaluated by rejects_sampling_params), the temperature parameter is stripped.

docs.title: Phase 3: Request Dispatch and Response Extraction
docs.text:
try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        response.raise_for_status()  # HTTP status first: an HTML 502 page must not look like a JSON bug
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            from utils.output import emit

            emit(
                "WARN_INVALID_JSON",
                status_code=response.status_code,
                preview=response.text[:200].strip(),
            )
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None

        # Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            from utils.output import emit

            emit("WARN_API_NO_CHOICES", detail=str(error_detail))
            raise RuntimeError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")
        # ...

The HTTP POST request is submitted with a connect timeout of 10 seconds and a read timeout of 300 seconds. HTTP errors trigger status verification before JSON decoding to prevent masking gateway errors. The parsed JSON structure is checked for completion choices.

docs.title: Phase 4: Usage Recording and Truncation Checks
docs.text:
# ...
        usage = response_json.get("usage") or {}
        from utils.llm_common import record_usage
        from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, observe_prompt_tokens

        prompt_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
        record_usage(
            provider,
            model,
            input_tokens=prompt_tokens,
            output_tokens=usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0,
            thinking_tokens=(usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0,
            cache_read=(usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens") or 0,
            cost=None,
            measured=bool(usage),
        )
        if usage:
            observe_prompt_tokens(provider, model, count_tokens_raw(prompt), prompt_tokens)
        choice = response_json["choices"][0]
        text = (choice.get("message") or {}).get("content") or ""
        if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length":
            from utils.llm_common import TruncatedResponse

            return TruncatedResponse(text)
        return text
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

Token consumption metrics (prompt, completion, reasoning, and cached tokens) are extracted and recorded in the common ledger via record_usage(). If the completion was terminated due to token length limits (finish_reason == "length"), the response text is returned wrapped in a TruncatedResponse object. Exception handlers catch HTTP errors, connection drops, and timeouts, converting them into standardized exceptions.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The prompt string.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The completion text, or an instance of TruncatedResponse if terminated early.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Missing environment settings or non-JSON HTTP responses.
  • RuntimeError: Successful HTTP responses that lack the choices attribute.
  • Exception: Network timeouts, connection drops, or HTTP status failures.

docs.title: _emit_call_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:

Description: Formats and emits a single-line console telemetry summary for an LLM call. Calculates percentage deviations between estimated prompt tokens and actual billed input tokens, incorporates output and reasoning metrics, logs cached token counts, and formats overall estimated monetary cost.

Parameters:

  • step (str): The pipeline step name associated with the execution.
  • estimate (int): The estimated prompt token count calculated prior to network dispatch.
  • usage (dict): The dictionary of usage metrics returned by the ledger delta.
  • measured (int): The count of completed requests that reported valid usage metrics.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:
    """One console line per LLM call: billed input vs the estimate, output (thinking), cached, cost.
    `measured` = requests with provider-reported usage (the deviation is per measured request)."""
    from utils.output import emit, get
    from utils.token_utils import format_cost

    per_request = usage["input"] / measured
    deviation = f"{(per_request - estimate) / estimate:+.0%}" if estimate else get("CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN")
    emit(
        "LLM_CALL_USAGE",
        step=step,
        input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
        estimate=f"{estimate:,}",
        deviation=deviation,
        requests=get("LLM_CALL_REQUESTS", count=measured) if measured > 1 else "",
        output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
        thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
        cached=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
        cost=format_cost(usage),
    )

The helper determines input consumption per request, computes the variance against initial estimates, and emits the LLM_CALL_USAGE event with formatted token counts and costs.

docs.title: In-Memory Cache Store
docs.text:
The module stores responses in a flat dictionary mapping SHA-256 hash digests to response strings.

Field Type Description key str A 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 hash calculated over the provider, model, thinking level, and prompt. value str The completion text returned by the model for that exact query configuration.

Example structure: 

{
  "c54d32a93b482...": "Response text generated by the model..."
}

docs.title: Usage Delta Dictionary
docs.text:
Captured via usage_delta(before, usage_snapshot(provider)) and passed into _emit_call_usage().

Field Type Description input int Number of billed input tokens consumed across the call. output int Number of completion tokens generated by the provider. thinking int Reasoning or thinking tokens generated during inference. cache_read int Number of tokens read from the provider's prompt cache. cost float \| None Calculated monetary expense in USD based on provider pricing tables. calls int Total count of low-level HTTP/SDK requests executed. unmeasured_calls int Count of requests where the provider omitted usage data.

docs.title: Generic OpenAI-Compatible Request Payload
docs.text:
Constructed inside _call_llm_provider() when dispatching requests to endpoints like Ollama.

Field Type Description model str Model identifier string (e.g., qwen2.5:32b). messages list[dict[str, str]] Ordered message history list; contains a single user prompt object. temperature float Sampling temperature (0.7 by default; 1.0 if reasoning effort is active; omitted if unsupported). think str (optional) Reasoning effort (low, medium, or high) passed to Ollama thinking variants. reasoning_effort str (optional) Standardized reasoning effort parameter matching the think value.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive error handling across filesystem operations, network transport, response serialization, and provider-specific error states:

  • Filesystem & Cache Resiliency: If llm_cache_v2.json is missing, load_cache() treats it as an empty cache without failing. If corrupted or unreadable, json.JSONDecodeError and OSError exceptions are caught, an alert event is logged, and an empty dictionary is returned. Cache writes are committed to a temporary file (.tmp) before atomic replacement via os.replace to prevent corrupted files if interrupted.
  • Network & Gateway Faults: In _call_llm_provider(), network requests are bounded by timeouts ((10, 300)). Specific exceptions (requests.exceptions.HTTPError, ConnectionError, Timeout, and RequestException) are caught and re-raised as standardized Exception types containing diagnostic details.
  • Malformed Provider Outputs: If an HTTP 200 response contains non-JSON text or HTML (such as error pages from reverse proxies), the JSON parser failure raises a ValueError with a response preview. If the response JSON lacks the expected choices array, a RuntimeError is raised.
  • Truncated Completions: When a provider stops generation early due to token limits (finish_reason == "length"), the completion is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse. These responses are explicitly excluded from disk caching so subsequent pipeline executions retry the query rather than replaying truncated text.
  • Non-Retryable Refusal Memory: When an LLMRefusalError is caught during provider execution, its retryable status is evaluated. If non-retryable, the refusal is recorded in a run-scoped registry (remember_refusal). Subsequent attempts with the same parameters are aborted early via previous_refusal, avoiding redundant billing.
  • Missing Optional Dependencies: Provider delegators (_call_llm_anthropic, _call_llm_gemini) catch ImportError exceptions when external SDKs (anthropic, google-genai) are not installed, providing explicit installation instructions.

docs.title: chapter_check.py
docs.text: Source: utils/chapter_check.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/chapter_check.py provides deterministic quality assurance and linting for generated Markdown chapters. Operating without Large Language Model (LLM) calls, it inspects written documentation pages strictly through regular expressions, AST/token analysis, and pipeline-accurate rendering tests. The module functions as a verification gate at the end of the documentation build pipeline, outputting a consolidated diagnostic report to chapter_check.json and emitting structured telemetry via utils.output.emit.

The verification architecture operates across three distinct evaluation layers. First, structural checks analyze CommonMark syntax compliance across every page, identifying unclosed code fences, broken internal hyperlinks, and syntactic defects in Mermaid diagram blocks that would cause client-side rendering crashes. Second, markup fidelity checks evaluate site renderer compatibility by injecting non-rendering Unicode Private Use Area (PUA) markers into Markdown construct boundaries, rendering the marked text through the MkDocs renderer, and comparing the resulting HTML tag hierarchies against CommonMark baseline expectations. Third, factual conformance checks validate the content of API reference pages against verified source facts, detecting omitted symbols, mutated signatures, nonexistent type names in headings, and broken or superfluous cross-references.

docs.title: parse_page()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def parse_page(markdown: str) -> dict:

Description: Parses raw Markdown text into structured components without executing external rendering engines. It reads the source line-by-line following GitHub CommonMark conventions to identify code fences, separating fenced blocks from prose and cataloging all headings along with their nesting levels. Any code block opener that remains unclosed at the end of the document is reclassified as prose, and its line number is tracked in the unclosed list.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): The raw Markdown text content of a documentation chapter.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing parsed page structures:
    • "prose": List of (line_number, text) tuples for lines outside code blocks.
    • "blocks": List of dictionary records for closed code blocks (lang, start, end, text).
    • "headings": List of (line_number, level, text) tuples for Markdown headings.
    • "unclosed": List of 1-based line numbers for unclosed opening code fences.

Example:

lines = markdown.split("\n")
prose, blocks, headings, unclosed = [], [], [], []
number = 0
while number < len(lines):
    line = lines[number]
    opener = _FENCE_RE.match(line)
    if opener and opener.group(2)[0] == "`" and "`" in line[opener.end(2) :]:  # ```mermaid``` in prose: inline code
        opener = None
    if opener:
        indent, fence = len(opener.group(1)), opener.group(2)
        for end in range(number + 1, len(lines)):
            closer = _FENCE_RE.match(lines[end])
            if (
                closer
                and closer.group(2)[0] == fence[0]
                and len(closer.group(2)) >= len(fence)
                and not lines[end][closer.end(2) :].strip()
                and len(closer.group(1)) <= indent + 3
            ):
                blocks.append({"lang": opener.group(3).lower(), "start": number + 1, "end": end + 1, "text": "\n".join(lines[number + 1 : end])})
                number = end + 1
                break
        else:
            unclosed.append(number + 1)
            prose.append((number + 1, line))
            number += 1
        continue
    prose.append((number + 1, line))
    heading = _HEADING_RE.match(line)
    if heading:
        headings.append((number + 1, len(heading.group(1)), heading.group(2)))
    number += 1

The parsing loop uses _FENCE_RE to distinguish valid code fence delimiters (triple backticks or tildes). It explicitly guards against inline code spans such as ```mermaid``` appearing in prose. When a fence opener is encountered, the inner loop searches ahead for a matching closer with identical or greater delimiter length and an indentation within 3 spaces of the opener; if found, the intermediate text is recorded as a code block. If the inner search reaches the end of the file without finding a matching delimiter, the opening line is appended to unclosed and treated as prose.

docs.title: resolve_link()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_link(page: str, target: str) -> str | None:

Description: Resolves a relative Markdown link target against the site-relative path of the source page, returning a normalized POSIX path. Protocol links (https:, mailto:), root-relative links starting with /, and in-page anchor links starting with # are ignored, returning None. URL query strings and fragment identifiers are stripped, and percent-encoded escapes are decoded.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The site-relative file path of the page containing the link (e.g., "api/index.md").
  • target (str): The raw hyperlink target attribute extracted from the Markdown link.

Returns:

  • str | None: The normalized site-relative path to the target file, or None if the target is external or an anchor.

Example:

if re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z][\w+.-]*:", target) or target.startswith(("#", "/")):
    return None
path = unquote(target.split("#", 1)[0].split("?", 1)[0])
return posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(page), path)) if path else None

The function first checks the target against a URI scheme regex and leading # or / prefixes, immediately returning None for external or non-relative references. For candidate relative paths, query strings and anchors are discarded using string splits, and urllib.parse.unquote resolves any URL-encoded characters. The resulting path is joined with the source page's directory name using posixpath.join and normalized with posixpath.normpath.

docs.text:
