docs.title: DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1_048_576 # 1 MB

Description: The fallback maximum byte threshold allowed per file during repository traversal. Any source file exceeding 1,048,576 bytes is excluded from ingestion to prevent memory bloating and pipeline stalls during tokenization and AST parsing.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def crawl_github_files( repo_url, token=None, max_file_size: int = DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None, )

Description: Orchestrates the retrieval of source files from a remote GitHub repository at a target branch, commit ref, or subdirectory. It routes requests through GitPython for SSH-based protocols or recursive GitHub REST API v3 queries for standard URLs. It enforces file-level exclusion patterns, applies repository .gitignore rules, discards binary payloads, and computes execution summary metrics.

Parameters:

  • repo_url (str): Full GitHub repository URL, optionally containing commit or branch references and subdirectory paths (e.g., https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/e45a15766746d95f8cfaaa705b0371267bec812e/python/packages/autogen-core/src/autogen_core) or an SSH git locator (e.g., git@github.com:owner/repo.git).
  • token (str | None): GitHub personal access token used for API authentication and rate-limit mitigation. If not passed, defaults to None and attempts fallback to unauthenticated public requests or reads from environment variables at caller sites.
  • max_file_size (int): Ceiling on ingested file sizes in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are recorded in skipped statistics and omitted from the returned content map. Defaults to 1_048_576 (1 MB).
  • use_relative_paths (bool): When True, strips the leading target subdirectory path from the keys in the output dictionary, anchoring file paths directly to the target subfolder. Defaults to False.
  • include_patterns (str | set[str] | None): Filename glob patterns (e.g., *.py) required for inclusion. If None, all encountered files are candidates for ingestion.
  • exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None): Path or filename glob patterns to filter out (e.g., */tests/*). Takes precedence over inclusion matches. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • dict: Ingestion payload containing a files dictionary mapping repository-relative file paths to UTF-8 decoded content strings, and a stats dictionary containing ingestion metrics.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised when repo_url does not conform to standard GitHub repository paths (fewer than two path components representing owner and repository).
  • Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits are encountered on unauthenticated connections.

docs.title: Phase 1: Input Pattern Normalization
docs.text:
# Convert single pattern to set
    if include_patterns and isinstance(include_patterns, str):
        include_patterns = {include_patterns}
    if exclude_patterns and isinstance(exclude_patterns, str):
        exclude_patterns = {exclude_patterns}

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

During initialization, scalar string arguments for include_patterns and exclude_patterns are coerced into sets for uniform iteration. The inner helper should_include_file defines the core evaluation hierarchy: filename inclusion matching is executed first, followed by path matching against the compiled gitignore_spec, and finally pattern matching against custom exclude_patterns. Any positive match against .gitignore or exclusion patterns drops the candidate file immediately.

docs.title: Phase 2: SSH Protocol Ingestion and Clone Management
docs.text:
# Detect SSH URL (git@ or .git suffix)
    is_ssh_url = repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git")

    if is_ssh_url:
        # Clone repo via SSH to temp dir
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
            emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
            try:
                repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
            except Exception as e:
                emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
                return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

            # ... Directory traversal and summary logic ...

If the URL matches an SSH signature (starting with git@ or terminating with .git), the crawler branches out of the HTTP API workflow into an isolated clone lifecycle. It provisions a temporary directory via tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and uses git.Repo.clone_from to perform a full local checkout. If the clone operation fails due to network failure, key rejection, or invalid repository coordinates, the error is intercepted, logged to telemetry, and an empty file dictionary with error metadata is returned immediately.

docs.title: Phase 3: Repository Traversal and Local File Ingestion (SSH)
docs.text:
# --- Load .gitignore ---
            gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
            gitignore_spec = None
            if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
                try:
                    with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                        gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
                    emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository")
                except Exception:
                    pass

            for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
                # Filter directories
                excluded_dirs = set()
                for d in sorted(dirs):
                    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
                    reason = None
                    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                        reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
                    elif exclude_patterns:
                        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                            dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                                reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                                break

                    if reason:
                        excluded_dirs.add(d)
                        entry_num += 1
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

                for d in dirs.copy():
                    if d in excluded_dirs:
                        dirs.remove(d)

                # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
                dirs.sort()

                for filename in sorted(filenames):
                    abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
                    rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
                    entry_num += 1

                    # Check include/exclude patterns
                    if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        continue

                    # Check file size
                    try:
                        file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
                    except OSError:
                        continue

                    if file_size > max_file_size:
                        count_size_limit += 1
                        skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = file_size / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    # Read content
                    try:
                        with open(abs_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                            content = f.read()
                        files[rel_path] = content
                        count_processed += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except Exception as e:
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, error=e)

The SSH execution path compiles a PathSpec model from the root .gitignore file and walks the temporary directory using os.walk. Pruning of directories occurs dynamically in-place within dirs before traversing subdirectories, avoiding unnecessary disk reads in ignored branches. Files are validated against max_file_size, and content is decoded via utf-8-sig to gracefully strip byte order marks. Binary files, decoding failures, and unexpected file-system errors are caught, counted as non-text, and emitted to telemetry channels.

docs.title: Phase 4: GitHub URL Decomposition and Remote Target Resolution
docs.text:
# Parse GitHub URL to extract owner, repo, commit/branch, and path
    parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)
    path_parts = parsed_url.path.strip("/").split("/")

    if len(path_parts) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub URL: {repo_url}")

    # Extract the basic components
    owner = path_parts[0]
    repo = path_parts[1]

    # Setup for GitHub API
    headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"}
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"token {token}"

    # ... Helper declarations fetch_branches, check_tree ...

    # Check if URL contains a specific branch/commit
    if len(path_parts) > 3 and path_parts[2] == "tree":

        def join_parts(i):
            return "/".join(path_parts[i:])

        branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
        branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

        # Fetching branches was not successful
        if len(branches) == 0:
            return None

        # Check branch name
        relevant_path = join_parts(3)

        # Find a match with relevant path and get the branch name
        filter_gen = (name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name))
        ref = next(filter_gen, None)

        # If match is not found, check for is it a tree
        if ref is None:
            tree = path_parts[3]
            ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None

        # If it is neither a tree nor a branch name
        if ref is None:
            emit_raw("ERROR", "The given path does not match with any branch and any tree in the repository.\nPlease verify the path is exists.")
            return None

        # Combine all parts after the ref as the path
        part_index = 5 if "/" in ref else 4
        specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
    else:
        # Don't put the ref param in query
        # and let Github decide default branch
        ref = None
        specific_path = ""

For standard HTTPS requests, the URL is decomposed into owner, repo, git ref (commit SHA, branch, or tag), and an optional subdirectory path specific_path. When a /tree/ segment is present, the crawler fetches repository branches and disambiguates multi-slash branch names (such as feature/auth) against target directory paths using relevant_path.startswith(name). If no named branch matches, it verifies whether the identifier corresponds to a valid Git tree or commit SHA via check_tree. If verification fails, the crawler terminates with an error message; otherwise, it assigns ref and sets specific_path to index into the targeted subfolder.

docs.title: Phase 5: Remote Gitignore Discovery and Ingestion
docs.text:
# --- Try to fetch .gitignore ---
    gitignore_spec = None
    try:
        gi_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore"
        gi_params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
        gi_resp = requests.get(gi_url, headers=headers, params=gi_params, timeout=(10, 10))
        if gi_resp.status_code == 200:
            gi_data = gi_resp.json()
            if "content" in gi_data and gi_data.get("encoding") == "base64":
                gi_content = base64.b64decode(gi_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gi_content.splitlines())
                emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository (API)")
    except Exception:
        pass

Before traversing remote tree hierarchies via the GitHub REST API, the crawler requests the repository's root .gitignore file using the target ref. If returned as Base64-encoded content, it decodes the payload to standard UTF-8 text and instantiates a pathspec.PathSpec matcher configured with the gitwildmatch rule set. Network timeouts and non-200 HTTP codes (e.g., absent .gitignore) are safely ignored, allowing crawling to continue without gitignore filtering.

docs.title: Phase 6: Recursive Contents Retrieval via REST API
docs.text:
def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        # ... Status code validation, directory parsing, and file content dispatch ...

The recursive fetch_contents helper queries the GitHub contents endpoint at the specified path. It inspects response headers and status codes to detect rate limits. When a rate limit is exceeded on an authenticated connection, it sleeps until the timestamp specified in X-RateLimit-Reset and retries the request; on unauthenticated connections, it raises an exception. Received directory entries are filtered against .gitignore and exclude_patterns to prevent descending into ignored subtrees. For files, payloads are downloaded using download_url or through the REST contents API using Base64 decoding, with file size limits enforced before and after transfer.

docs.text:
# Start crawling from the specified path
    fetch_contents(specific_path)

    # --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = api_counters["processed"] + api_counters["excluded"] + api_counters["size_limit"] + api_counters["non_text"]
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=api_counters["processed"])
    if api_counters["excluded"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=api_counters["excluded"])
    if api_counters["size_limit"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=api_counters["size_limit"])
        for sf in api_skipped_size:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=sf)
    if api_counters["non_text"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=api_counters["non_text"])
        for sf in api_skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=sf)

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": 0,
            "skipped_files": [],
            "base_path": specific_path if use_relative_paths else None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
        },
    }

Once all recursive calls terminate, the function aggregates telemetry counters covering processed files, pattern-excluded files, files exceeding size caps, and non-text artifacts. It publishes these metrics through emit and formats the final return structure containing the complete in-memory dictionary of files alongside operational statistics.

Example:

    repo_url = "https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/6c38dc93f40a47f4d1350adca9ec0d72502e223f/pydantic"

    # Example: Get Python and Markdown files, but exclude test files
    result = crawl_github_files(
        repo_url,
        token=github_token,
        max_file_size=1 * 1024 * 1024,  # 1 MB in bytes
        use_relative_paths=True,  # Enable relative paths
        include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},  # Include Python and Markdown files
    )

    files = result["files"]
    stats = result["stats"]

docs.title: should_include_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested within crawl_github_files)

Signature: def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool

Description: Determines whether a given candidate file should be ingested based on glob patterns and Git wildcard specifications. The inclusion logic checks whether file_name matches any configured pattern in include_patterns. If accepted, it evaluates file_path against gitignore_spec.match_file(). If the file is not ignored, it checks file_path against exclude_patterns.

Parameters:

  • file_path (str): Repository-relative or directory-relative path of the file.
  • file_name (str): Basename of the file (e.g., main.py).
  • gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None): Compiled PathSpec instance representing active .gitignore rules, or None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the file passes all criteria and should be downloaded/read; False if it should be excluded.

Example:

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The function prioritizes positive filtering: when include_patterns is provided, any file whose name does not match at least one pattern is dropped immediately. Files that survive inclusion matching are checked against gitignore_spec and exclude_patterns, returning False if any exclusion rule matches.

docs.title: fetch_branches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested within crawl_github_files)

Signature: def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str)

Description: Queries the GitHub REST API to list all branches in the specified repository. This list is used to parse branch names that contain slashes (e.g., feature/v2) out of ambiguous URL path segments.

Parameters:

  • owner (str): GitHub account or organization name.
  • repo (str): GitHub repository name.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: List of branch representation dictionaries returned by the GitHub API. Returns an empty list ([]) if the repository is not found, permissions are insufficient, or a non-200 status code occurs.

Raises:

  • Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits (HTTP 403 or 429) are encountered without an authentication token.

Example:

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get branches of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
                )
            else:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository.",
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function executes a synchronized HTTP GET against /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches with a 30-second timeout. It checks for rate-limiting status codes and differentiates unauthenticated from authenticated 404 responses via emit_raw, guiding the user on how to configure access tokens when a repository cannot be reached.

Signature: def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str)

Description: Verifies whether a given identifier represents a valid Git tree or commit SHA in the remote repository by querying the GitHub Git Trees API endpoint.

Parameters:

  • owner (str): GitHub account or organization name.
  • repo (str): GitHub repository name.
  • tree (str): Git SHA or tree identifier extracted from the URL path.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the tree or commit exists in the repository (HTTP 200); False otherwise.

Raises:

  • Exception: Raised when a rate limit (HTTP 403 or 429) is hit on an unauthenticated connection.

Example:

    def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str):
        """Check the repository has the given tree"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"check_tree | ref='{tree}' for {owner}/{repo} -> exists={response.status_code == 200}", dest="LOG")

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        return response.status_code == 200

The function sends an HTTP GET request to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}. It logs the existence check to the debug channel via emit_raw, evaluates the response code against 200, and ensures rate-limit errors on unauthenticated runs are raised as explicit exceptions.

Visibility: Private (nested within crawl_github_files)

Signature: def fetch_contents(path)

Description: Core recursive traversal routine for the GitHub REST API workflow. Fetches the metadata and content of files and subdirectories located at path. Handles directory pruning, rate-limit backoff, file size enforcement, and decoding of Base64 or raw payloads.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Repository-relative subdirectory or file path to inspect.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates the parent scope files dictionary and api_counters maps in-place.

Raises:

  • Exception: Raised when rate limits are exceeded on unauthenticated connections.

docs.title: Phase 1: Request Dispatch and Rate Limit Handling
docs.text:
def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
                )
            elif not path and ref == "main":
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found. Check if the default branch is not 'main'\n"
                    "Try adding branch name to the request i.e. python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo/tree/master",
                )
            else:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    f"Error 404: Path '{path}' not found in repository or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    f"Please verify the token has access to this repository and the path exists.",
                )
            return None

        if response.status_code != 200:
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching {path}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return None

The helper issues an HTTP GET to /contents/{path} with the active commit or branch reference in params. If a 403 or 429 status code indicates rate limiting, the function checks for a token; if missing, it terminates by raising an Exception. If a token is present, it extracts the epoch reset timestamp from X-RateLimit-Reset, sleeps for the required interval, and retries the call. 404 responses are caught and logged with troubleshooting instructions before returning None.

            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]

            # Calculate relative path if requested
            if use_relative_paths and specific_path:
                # Make sure the path is relative to the specified subdirectory
                if item_path.startswith(specific_path):
                    rel_path = item_path[len(specific_path) :].lstrip("/")
                else:
                    rel_path = item_path
            else:
                rel_path = item_path

            if item["type"] == "file":
                api_counters["entry"] += 1
                entry_num = api_counters["entry"]

                # Check if file should be included based on patterns
                if not should_include_file(rel_path, item["name"], gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    continue

                # Check file size if available
                file_size = item.get("size", 0)
                if file_size > max_file_size:
                    api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                    api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                    size_kb = file_size / 1024
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                    continue

                # For files, get raw content
                if item.get("download_url"):
                    file_url = item["download_url"]
                    file_response = requests.get(file_url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

                    # Final size check in case content-length header is available but differs from metadata
                    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get("content-length", 0))
                    if content_length > max_file_size:
                        api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                        api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = content_length / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    if file_response.status_code == 200:
                        files[rel_path] = file_response.text
                        api_counters["processed"] += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    else:
                        api_counters["non_text"] += 1
                        api_skipped_non_text.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_HTTP_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, status=file_response.status_code)
                else:
                    # Alternative method if download_url is not available
                    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
                    if content_response.status_code == 200:
                        content_data = content_response.json()
                        if content_data.get("encoding") == "base64" and "content" in content_data:
                            # Check size of base64 content before decoding
                            if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size calculation
                                estimated_size = int(len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75)
                                api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                                api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                                size_kb = estimated_size / 1024
                                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                                continue

                            file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                            files[rel_path] = file_content
                            api_counters["processed"] += 1
                            emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        else:
                            api_counters["non_text"] += 1
                            api_skipped_non_text.append(rel_path)
                            emit("CRAWL_FILE_UNEXPECTED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    else:
                        api_counters["non_text"] += 1
                        api_skipped_non_text.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_HTTP_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, status=content_response.status_code)

The response JSON array (or single dictionary) is processed sequentially. For each file item, relative paths are computed if use_relative_paths is enabled. If the item passes pattern and size checks, the file content is retrieved. If download_url is provided, a direct GET request downloads the text; otherwise, the function queries the API item URL, checks that the payload is Base64 encoded, approximates the decoded byte size (len * 0.75), and decodes the string into files[rel_path].

docs.title: Phase 3: Directory Filtering and Recursion
docs.text:
elif item["type"] == "dir":
                # Check if directory should be excluded before recursing
                dir_excluded = False
                dir_reason = None

                if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(rel_path):
                    dir_excluded = True
                    dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")

                if not dir_excluded and exclude_patterns:
                    dir_name = item["name"]  # basename of the directory
                    for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                        dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                        if (
                            fnmatch.fnmatch(item_path, dir_pattern)
                            or fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, dir_pattern)
                            or fnmatch.fnmatch(dir_name, dir_pattern)
                        ):
                            dir_excluded = True
                            dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                            break

                if dir_excluded:
                    api_counters["entry"] += 1
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=api_counters["entry"], path=rel_path, reason=dir_reason)
                    continue

                # Only recurse if directory is not excluded
                fetch_contents(item_path)

        return None

When an item's type is "dir", the function determines whether the directory is ignored by the compiled gitignore_spec or matches any pattern in exclude_patterns. Patterns ending with /* have that suffix stripped using .removesuffix("/*"), and are compared against the full path, relative path, and directory basename. If the directory is marked for exclusion, traversal skips the entire subtree; otherwise, it recursively invokes fetch_contents(item_path).

docs.title: Crawled Repository Result
docs.text:
The top-level dictionary structure returned by crawl_github_files() containing ingested source files and operation statistics.

Field Type Description files dict[str, str] Mapping of file paths (either repository-relative or anchored to the subpath) to their UTF-8 decoded text content. stats dict[str, any] Key-value pairs documenting traversal results, filter definitions, and base path configuration.

docs.title: Crawling Statistics
docs.text:
The schema of the stats dictionary embedded within the result structure.

Field Type Description downloaded_count int Total count of files downloaded and stored in the files dictionary. skipped_count int Count of skipped files recorded in the returned statistics structure. skipped_files list List tracking skipped filenames. base_path str \| None Subdirectory path used to compute relative paths if use_relative_paths was True; otherwise None. include_patterns set[str] \| None Set of inclusion patterns used to filter files. exclude_patterns set[str] \| None Set of exclusion patterns used to filter files. source str (Optional) Added during SSH clone operations with the literal value "ssh_clone". error str (Optional) Error message string populated if an SSH clone operation fails.

Example structure returned during an HTTPS crawl:

{
    "files": {
        "pydantic/main.py": "from __future__ import annotations...",
        "pydantic/types.py": "import typing..."
    },
    "stats": {
        "downloaded_count": 2,
        "skipped_count": 0,
        "skipped_files": [],
        "base_path": "pydantic",
        "include_patterns": {"*.py", "*.md"},
        "exclude_patterns": None
    }
}

docs.title: Internal API Traversal Telemetry
docs.text:
Internal integer tracking schema maintained in the api_counters dictionary during remote REST traversal.

Field Type Description processed int Number of files retrieved and stored in files. excluded int Number of files and directories excluded by patterns or .gitignore. size_limit int Number of files skipped because they exceeded max_file_size. non_text int Number of files skipped due to HTTP failures or non-text content. entry int Monotonically increasing counter assigned to each processed directory entry for progress reporting.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module handles errors defensive at multiple layers to prevent incomplete crawls and unhandled exceptions:

  • URL Parsing Validation: The function parses repo_url using urllib.parse.urlparse. If the path segments contain fewer than two elements (owner and repo name), it raises a ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub URL: {repo_url}").
  • API Rate Limiting: REST requests check for HTTP status codes 403 and 429. If rate limits are encountered on an unauthenticated connection, the crawler raises an Exception notifying the user to set GITHUB_TOKEN. On authenticated connections, it reads the X-RateLimit-Reset header, logs a warning message, and sleeps until the limit window resets before retrying.
  • Missing or Private Repositories (HTTP 404): When handling 404 status codes, the crawler inspects the authentication state. For unauthenticated calls, it notifies the user that the repository may be private and requires a token. When a specific branch (such as main) returns 404, it suggests specifying an alternate branch (such as master).
  • SSH Clone Resilience: Failures during git.Repo.clone_from are caught within a general except Exception as e block. The error is emitted via emit_raw("ERROR", ...) and the function returns early with an empty files map and the exception string recorded under stats["error"].
  • Binary File Filtering: When reading local files in SSH mode, reading is wrapped in try...except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError). Non-text and binary payloads are skipped, logged via emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", ...), and tracked in the skipped_non_text_list.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
crawl_local_files.py serves as the primary local filesystem ingestion component for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. Operating as the local counterpart to crawl_github_files.py, this module scans a designated root directory on the host machine, normalizes directory hierarchies, evaluates path-filtering rules, and reads file content into memory. Downstream analysis nodes, including AST parsing routines and LLM-assisted knowledge extraction passes, depend on the resulting in-memory file dictionary to generate technical documentation without requiring external network access or Git credentials.

The crawling pipeline is implemented as a single-pass traversal built upon Python's os.walk. To optimize performance across large code repositories, the traversal implements in-place directory pruning (dirs.remove()), ensuring that entire subtrees designated as ignored—such as build directories, virtual environments, or package caches—are bypassed before entering unnecessary recursion cycles. Filtering is governed hierarchically: the module dynamically identifies, parses, and caches scoping rules from both root and nested .gitignore files using pathspec, while simultaneously evaluating explicit glob patterns (include_patterns and exclude_patterns) via fnmatch. Files exceeding a configured byte size ceiling or failing UTF-8 text decoding (such as compiled binaries or proprietary formats) are recorded and excluded.

The module integrates tightly with the runtime's central telemetry bus in utils.output. Rather than printing unformatted diagnostic text directly to stdout, the crawler emits standardized, localized event tokens (emit) along with structural counts for processed, excluded, and non-text entries. This design isolates file discovery and ingestion mechanics from presentation and report generation, maintaining structural parity with remote GitHub crawl workflows.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def crawl_local_files( directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None, max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True, ):

Description: Recursively walks the specified local directory to collect, filter, and extract file contents into a standardized dictionary structure. The function enforces root and nested .gitignore compliance, evaluates custom glob exclusion and inclusion rules, validates file sizes against byte limits, decodes text using utf-8-sig to safely strip Byte Order Marks (BOM), and emits comprehensive progress metrics.

Parameters:

  • directory (str): The target filesystem path pointing to the root directory to crawl.
  • include_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob expressions (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}) restricting the crawler strictly to matching file paths.
  • exclude_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob expressions (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.pyc"}) specifying directories and files to exclude.
  • max_file_size (int | None): Optional maximum file size threshold in bytes. Files exceeding this ceiling are excluded from ingestion.
  • use_relative_paths (bool): Flag indicating whether dictionary keys should be normalized relative to directory (defaults to True) or maintained as absolute/raw filesystem paths.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing a single "files" key mapped to an inner dictionary {filepath: content}, where each path points to its decoded UTF-8 string payload.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the target directory argument does not exist or fails os.path.isdir().

Example:

files_data = crawl_local_files(
    "..",
    exclude_patterns={
        "*.pyc",
        "__pycache__/*",
        ".venv/*",
        ".git/*",
        "docs/*",
        "output/*",
    },
)

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Validation and Gitignore Initialization
docs.text:
if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

    files_dict = {}

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_limit = []
    skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Gitignore specs: {abs_dir_path: pathspec} ---
    gitignore_specs = {}
    root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
        spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
        if spec:
            gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
            emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

    # Translated reason strings (looked up once)
    reason_excluded = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
    reason_gitignore = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")

The function begins by verifying that the target filesystem path points to an accessible directory; if not, it raises a ValueError immediately. It initializes tracking counters for crawl telemetry, empty lists for skipped items, and the main files_dict container. It then inspects the crawl root for an initial .gitignore file, parses it into a pathspec.PathSpec object mapped to the directory's absolute path, and retrieves localized rejection reason strings once via utils.output.get to avoid redundant dictionary lookups throughout the traversal.

docs.title: Phase 2: Directory Traversal and Pruning
docs.text:
# --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        abs_root = os.path.abspath(root)

        # Check for nested .gitignore in current directory (skip root, already loaded)
        if abs_root != os.path.abspath(directory):
            nested_gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
            if os.path.exists(nested_gi):
                spec = _load_gitignore(nested_gi)
                if spec:
                    gitignore_specs[abs_root] = spec

        # --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            abs_d = os.path.join(abs_root, d)
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(abs_d, directory)

            reason = None
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
                reason = reason_gitignore
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = reason_excluded
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()

The crawler initiates a single-pass os.walk through the filesystem hierarchy. At each traversed directory level, it detects and loads any nested .gitignore file into gitignore_specs to enforce scoped ignoring rules for child subtrees. Candidate child directories are evaluated against both loaded .gitignore specifications and user-supplied exclude_patterns. Any matched directory is pruned directly from dirs in-place using dirs.remove(d), which halts os.walk from descending into that entire filesystem subtree and conserves significant I/O and CPU cycles.

docs.title: Phase 3: File Filtering Chain
docs.text:
# --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            abs_filepath = os.path.abspath(filepath)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore (all levels)
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_filepath):
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                    continue

For every file located within an unpruned directory, the crawler executes an ordered filtering pipeline. Files are first matched against all active .gitignore rules across all hierarchy levels via _matches_any_gitignore(). If permitted, the relative file path is checked against the set of exclude_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch. Finally, if include_patterns were explicitly configured, the path must positively match at least one pattern, or else it is rejected and tagged with a CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED telemetry event.

docs.title: Phase 4: Content Reading and Encoding Normalization
docs.text:
# Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=relpath, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                continue

            # Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=relpath, error=e)

Files that survive the pattern filters undergo a byte-size check if max_file_size is specified; files exceeding the limit are skipped, and their size in kilobytes is reported. Surviving files are opened using utf-8-sig encoding, ensuring UTF-8 compatibility while transparently stripping leading Byte Order Marks. If the read operation triggers a UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError (indicating a binary file), or any other filesystem I/O exception, the file is safely caught, categorized as non-text, recorded in skipped_non_text, and omitted from files_dict.

docs.title: Phase 5: Telemetry Summary and Payload Return
docs.text:
# --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=count_processed)
    if count_excluded > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=count_excluded)
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=count_size_limit)
        for f in skipped_size_limit:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)
    if count_non_text > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=count_non_text)
        for f in skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)

    return {"files": files_dict}

Once os.walk finishes traversing the filesystem tree, the crawler aggregates metric totals across processed, excluded, oversized, and non-text categories. It transmits structured telemetry events to utils.output.emit, itemizing skipped oversized files and unreadable binaries for pipeline audit logs. Finally, the collected in-memory dictionary containing relative paths mapped to decoded source strings is packaged into {"files": files_dict} and returned to the caller.

docs.title: _load_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):

Description: Opens a specified .gitignore file using utf-8-sig encoding and compiles its rules into a pathspec.PathSpec instance utilizing the standard gitwildmatch pattern syntax. If the file cannot be opened or parsed due to permission errors or encoding issues, a warning log is transmitted through emit_raw, and the function returns None.

Parameters:

  • gitignore_path (str): Filesystem path pointing directly to a .gitignore file.

Returns:

  • pathspec.PathSpec | None: A compiled pattern matcher instance if successfully parsed, or None if an exception occurred.

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised directly; all read and parsing errors are caught internally.

Example:

root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
    spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
    if spec:
        gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
        emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):
    """Load a .gitignore file and return a PathSpec, or None on failure."""
    try:
        with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
            return pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Failed to load .gitignore at {gitignore_path}: {e}", dest="LOG")
        return None

The helper encapsulates file ingestion and pattern compilation for Git ignore rules. By parsing lines using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ...), it faithfully reproduces standard Git wildcard behavior (such as handling glob stars, leading slashes, and negation rules). Wrapping the entire operation in a defensive try...except block ensures that malformed or inaccessible .gitignore files log a diagnostic warning without aborting the parent crawl operation.

docs.title: _matches_any_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):

Description: Determines whether an absolute filesystem path matches any active pathspec.PathSpec rule across loaded .gitignore instances. The evaluation calculates the candidate path relative to each .gitignore's containing directory, skipping specs that do not encompass the path's subtree. For directory evaluations, it ensures a trailing slash is appended to conform to Git wildcard directory syntax.

Parameters:

  • gitignore_specs (dict): Dictionary mapping absolute directory paths to their corresponding compiled pathspec.PathSpec objects.
  • abs_path (str): The absolute path of the file or directory being evaluated.
  • is_dir (bool): Optional boolean indicating whether the target path represents a directory (defaults to False).

Returns:

  • bool: True if the path matches at least one governing .gitignore rule; otherwise False.

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised.

Example:

if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
    reason = reason_gitignore

def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):
    """Check if a path matches ANY loaded .gitignore spec.

    Each spec is checked with the path relative to its own .gitignore directory.
    For directories, a trailing '/' is appended for proper gitignore matching.

    Args:
        gitignore_specs: dict of {abs_dir_path: pathspec.PathSpec}
        abs_path: absolute path of the file or directory to check
        is_dir: True if checking a directory
    Returns:
        True if the path matches any gitignore rule
    """
    for gi_dir, spec in gitignore_specs.items():
        rel = os.path.relpath(abs_path, gi_dir)
        # Skip if the path is not under this gitignore's scope
        if rel.startswith(".."):
            continue
        match_path = rel.replace("\\", "/")
        if is_dir:
            match_path = match_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
        if spec.match_file(match_path):
            return True
    return False

This function performs multi-level Gitignore resolution across hierarchical scopes. When checking a path, it calculates the relative path from each cached .gitignore directory using os.path.relpath. Any relative path prefixed with .. indicates that the target path lies outside that specific ignore file's subtree and is skipped immediately. Windows backslashes are normalized to forward slashes to guarantee cross-platform consistency with POSIX gitwildmatch rules, and directories have trailing slashes appended so that rules targeting directories specifically (e.g., build/) match correctly.

docs.title: Local crawler file results
docs.text:
The primary dictionary returned by crawl_local_files() provides downstream nodes with immediate access to in-memory file content mapped by normalized path keys.

Field Type Description files dict[str, str] Key-value store where each key is a file path (relative to the crawled root directory when use_relative_paths=True) and each value is the raw decoded file content as a string.

Example dictionary returned by crawl_local_files():

{
    "files": {
        "main.py": "import os\n\ndef run():\n    pass\n",
        "utils/files.py": "def read_file(path):\n    return open(path).read()\n",
    }
}

docs.title: Gitignore specification mapping
docs.text:
An internal mapping constructed dynamically during filesystem traversal to track active scoping rules across directory subtrees.

Key Type Description abs_dir_path str Absolute filesystem path of the directory containing the .gitignore file. spec pathspec.PathSpec Compiled pattern matcher configured with the gitwildmatch syntax for that specific directory subtree.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Root Directory Validation (ValueError): At invocation, crawl_local_files() checks os.path.isdir(directory). If the target does not exist or points to a non-directory file, a ValueError is raised immediately with the message f"Directory does not exist: {directory}".
  • Gitignore Parsing Tolerances (Exception): Inside _load_gitignore(), all filesystem I/O and syntax parsing failures are trapped by an untyped except Exception as e: block. The error is routed to logging via emit_raw("WARNING", ..., dest="LOG"), returning None so that invalid or locked ignore files do not interrupt the broader crawl.
  • Non-Text and Encoding Errors (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError): When reading file payloads, the crawler attempts decoding using utf-8-sig. If decoding fails due to binary content, invalid UTF-8 sequences, or embedded null characters, the exception is caught, the counter count_non_text is incremented, the path is appended to skipped_non_text, and a CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT event is emitted.
  • Filesystem Read Faults (Exception): Any unexpected OS-level I/O faults during file reads (such as read permission denials or broken symlinks) are caught by an untyped except Exception as e: block. The crawler increments count_non_text, records the path, and logs the diagnostic event CRAWL_FILE_ERROR with the exception object.

docs.text: Source: utils/exclude_patterns.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/exclude_patterns.py defines the default baseline pattern set used by filesystem and repository crawling modules across the system, including crawl_local_files.py and crawl_github_files.py. The module centralizes file and directory exclusion rules into a single immutable configuration constant, DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS. During repository traversal, crawlers match discovered paths against these patterns to prevent ingestion of binary assets, compiled artifacts, third-party vendor directories, lockfiles, temporary files, and sensitive credentials.

The patterns rely on standard Unix shell-style glob syntax evaluated via fnmatch. Directory patterns terminate with a trailing wildcard suffix (/*), signaling to recursive crawlers (such as os.walk) that any directory matching the prefix should be pruned before descending into its subtree. File patterns leverage wildcard extension matching (such as *.png or *.pyc), exact basename matching (such as package-lock.json or .DS_Store), and depth-independent wildcard path prefixes (such as */.env or */id_rsa) to intercept files located at arbitrary filesystem depths.

Excluding irrelevant content at the ingestion boundary is essential for the documentation generation pipeline. Parsing binary media files or massive dependency trees (such as node_modules or Python virtual environments) causes excessive memory consumption, decoding failures, and token limit exhaustion when payloads are sent to Large Language Models (LLMs). Furthermore, the exclusion of cryptographic keys, environment variables, and SSH credentials prevents secrets from being cached on disk or transmitted across network boundaries to LLM inference providers.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS = {

Description: A module-level set of string literals containing glob patterns formatted for evaluation with fnmatch.fnmatch() or fnmatch.fnmatchcase(). The set encapsulates exclusions partitioned across seven distinct operational domains: media and static assets; build and framework distribution directories; virtual environments, dependencies, lockfiles, and secrets; language-specific compilation artifacts; operating system and version control metadata; traditional IDE settings; and modern AI assistant workspace rules.

Parameters:

  • This constant symbol does not accept parameters.

Returns:

  • set[str]: An unordered collection of unique glob pattern strings.

    "assets/*",
    "data/*",

    "static/*",

Dependency directories (such as node_modules/* and vendor/*) and generated lockfiles (such as package-lock.json and Cargo.lock) are excluded because their repetitive dependency graphs consume tens of thousands of tokens without providing high-level design insight.

Native machine objects and libraries (*.o, *.so, *.dylib, *.dll, *.exe) and mobile package directories (ios/Pods/*, android/.gradle/*) are excluded to avoid reading unparsable binary headers.

These files describe developer-specific workspaces, local SDK paths, and UI preferences rather than the shared codebase logic, and are omitted to avoid noise during architecture mapping.

Excluding these files prevents their prompt instructions from interfering with the LLM prompts executed by this knowledge extraction pipeline.

docs.title: Default exclusion pattern set
docs.text:
The file defines DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS as a standard Python set[str]. Each element in the set represents a path or file pattern evaluated using fnmatch.fnmatch(). The set adheres to three structural conventions:

Pattern Category Syntax Pattern Matching Behavior Target Scope Directory Subtree directory_name/* Trailing wildcard indicating that any directory matching the prefix should be omitted, allowing crawlers to mutate dirnames in-place and skip subtrees. Top-level or nested directories (e.g., dist/*, venv/*, node_modules/*). Glob Extension *.extension Suffix wildcard matching any filename with the specified file extension, regardless of directory location. Binary assets, media files, compiled bytecode, libraries (e.g., *.png, *.pyc, *.dll). Basename Literal filename Exact match against the file basename; applies when the filename appears in any discovered path. Environment files, lockfiles, OS files (e.g., .env, .DS_Store, package-lock.json). Arbitrary Depth Wildcard */pattern Wildcard prefix matching files or directories located inside any parent directory. Nested secrets and credentials (e.g., */.env, */id_rsa, */id_ed25519).

The breakdown of patterns across the 7 functional categories defined in DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS is summarized below:

Category Index Category Description Representative Entries Primary Rationale 1 Media, Data, & Static Assets *.png, *.jpg, *.mp4, *.pdf, *.zip, assets/* Avoid binary decoding errors and unnecessary payload volume. 2 Build, Distribution, & Caches dist/*, build/*, target/*, .next/*, *.log Eliminate minified bundles, compiler targets, and non-source logs. 3 Environments, Lockfiles, & Secrets .env, */id_rsa, *.pem, node_modules/*, *.lock Prevent secret exfiltration and eliminate redundant lockfile token load. 4 Language-Specific Artifacts __pycache__/*, *.class, *.so, *.dylib, ios/Pods/* Exclude compiled platform-specific binaries and runtime caches. 5 OS & Version Control .git/*, .github/*, .svn/*, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db Skip VCS object databases and local OS file manager metadata. 6 Classic IDEs .vscode/*, .idea/*, *.iml, .eclipse/*, .vs/* Omit developer-specific workstation and project configuration files. 7 AI Agents & AI IDEs .cursor/*, .cursorrules, .windsurf/*, .cline/* Avoid prompt pollution or conflicting instructions from other AI agent frameworks.

docs.title: facts.py
docs.text: Source: utils/facts.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/facts.py module implements deterministic, language-agnostic code fact verification across the repository. In the documentation generation pipeline, Large Language Models (LLMs) inspect repository files and emit structured assertions regarding symbols, module dependencies, configuration keys, and error conditions, accompanied by line-level quote evidence. Rather than employing language-specific Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsers, this module verifies whether LLM claims correspond verbatim to physical source lines, resolves their line boundaries, verifies lexical enclosing structures, and tracks module dependencies across multi-package projects.

Source files undergo text normalization and indexing via SourceIndex, which prepares Unicode NFC-normalized views, whitespace-collapsed single-line representations, fully squashed character offsets, and an inverted word-token line index. Quoted evidence is matched using a tiered search strategy: single-line collapsed string matching, multi-line squashed matching bounded by a line window, and ordered token subsequence searches. Symbols are bound to their declared parents by tracking hierarchical indentation blocks and container keywords across diverse programming language conventions.

For cross-module analysis, ModuleTable aggregates project manifests (such as package.json, Cargo.toml, or pom.xml), directory structures, and unique symbol ownership maps. It resolves raw import strings—including relative imports, path aliases, package barrel exports, and wildcard namespaces—against actual project files. The module enforces the strict "evidence rule": a claimed dependency is accepted only if the quoted line names the target module, references a path matching the module, or uses a symbol owned exclusively by that module.

docs.title: split_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def split_lines(content: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Splits source code into line strings matching the line numbering semantics used by text editors, GitHub, and LLMs. Unlike Python's standard str.splitlines(), which breaks on form feeds (\f), vertical tabs (\v), and Unicode line break characters (U+2028), this function splits exclusively on carriage return (\r) and newline (\n) delimiters, preserving terminal empty lines without trailing newline artifacts.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw file content string.

Returns:

  • list[str]: A list of individual line strings.

Example:

lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
view = code_view(lines)
imports = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if import_statement_like(line)} | import_block_lines(view)

The function regularizes multi-platform line breaks (\r\n, \r, \n) into a predictable list of string lines. The final empty element produced by a trailing newline is trimmed to preserve exact 1-based editor line correspondences across downstream operations.

docs.title: SourceIndex
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class SourceIndex:

Description: An in-memory search index built for a single source file. It normalizes text via Unicode NFC, maintains whitespace-collapsed and whitespace-free ("squashed") linear buffers with line-offset indexes, and indexes word tokens in an inverted map for multi-line and token-fallback matching.

docs.title: SourceIndex.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def __init__(self, content: str):

Description: Initializes the SourceIndex instance by splitting and normalizing content, calculating cumulative line offsets for exact and squashed buffers, and constructing inverted token indexes.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw source file content.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def __init__(self, content: str):
    self.lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
    self.collapsed = [_collapse(line) for line in self.lines]
    # Collapsed lines joined by "\n" (never inside a collapsed line or quote, so no match spans two lines)
    self.collapsed_text = "\n".join(self.collapsed) + "\n"
    self.collapsed_offsets = list(accumulate((len(line) + 1 for line in self.collapsed), initial=0))
    squashed = [_squash(line) for line in self.lines]
    # All lines without whitespace, back to back, with each line's start offset: one str.find per quote
    self.squashed_text = "".join(squashed)
    self.offsets = list(accumulate((len(line) for line in squashed), initial=0))
    self.words = [_words(line) for line in self.lines]
    self.word_sets = [set(words) for words in self.words]
    self.word_lines = defaultdict(list)  # word → lines it occurs on, for the token fallback
    for number, words in enumerate(self.word_sets):
        for word in words:
            self.word_lines[word].append(number)
    self._chains = None  # block_chain(), built on first use

The constructor computes cumulative length offsets using itertools.accumulate for both the whitespace-collapsed lines buffer (collapsed_offsets) and the whitespace-removed squashed buffer (offsets). It pre-tokenizes each line into word lists and populates word_lines, mapping every token to the list of line indices where it appears. Block hierarchy chains (self._chains) are initialized as None and lazily calculated when requested.

docs.title: SourceIndex.block_chain()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def block_chain(self, line: int) -> tuple:

Description: Returns the chain of enclosing lexical blocks surrounding a given line, ordered from innermost enclosing block to outermost.

Parameters:

  • line (int): 0-based index of the line.

Returns:

  • tuple: A tuple of tuples, where each entry represents (indent, text, kind, named).

Example:

def block_chain(self, line: int) -> tuple:
    """The blocks *line* sits in, innermost first: ``(indent, text, kind, named)`` per enclosing line
    (``_block_chains``)."""
    if self._chains is None:
        self._chains = _block_chains(self.lines)
    return self._chains[line]

This method delegates to _block_chains upon its first invocation to build an indentation-aware stack of enclosing scopes across all lines in the file. Results are cached on self._chains to optimize repeated lookups during parent-symbol resolution.

docs.title: SourceIndex.text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def text(self, first: int, last: int) -> str:

Description: Returns the raw source text spanning lines from first to last (inclusive), joined by newline characters.

Parameters:

  • first (int): 0-based starting line index.
  • last (int): 0-based ending line index.

Returns:

  • str: The un-collapsed, raw source lines joined by \n.

Example:

def text(self, first: int, last: int) -> str:
    return "\n".join(self.lines[first : last + 1])

The method slices the underlying pre-split self.lines list from index first through last + 1 and joins them with standard newline delimiters. It preserves original indentation and source character formatting.

docs.title: SourceIndex.locate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def locate(self, quote, start: int = 0, end: int | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:

Description: Finds 0-based line ranges matching a target quote within the line window between start and end. Executes a three-tiered fallback search: exact single-line collapsed matching, multi-line squashed matching within a sliding window, and ordered token sequence matching.

Parameters:

  • quote (Any): The search string or object convertible to string representing the quote evidence.
  • start (int): 0-based line index at which to begin searching. Defaults to 0.
  • end (int | None): 0-based line index upper boundary. Defaults to None (searches to end of file).

Returns:

  • list[tuple[int, int, str]]: A list of matches formatted as (first_line, last_line, match_mode), where match_mode is "exact", "joined", or "tokens".

Example:

end = len(self.lines) if end is None else min(end, len(self.lines))
collapsed = _collapse(quote)
if not collapsed or start >= end:
    return []
exact = []
pos = self.collapsed_text.find(collapsed, self.collapsed_offsets[start])
while 0 <= pos < self.collapsed_offsets[end]:
    line = bisect_right(self.collapsed_offsets, pos) - 1
    exact.append((line, line, "exact"))
    pos = self.collapsed_text.find(collapsed, self.collapsed_offsets[line + 1])  # next line: one hit per line
if exact:
    return exact
# ...

The matching hierarchy begins with single-line collapsed string matching against collapsed_text. Binary search via bisect_right resolves character positions to line indices. If no exact match occurs, it searches squashed_text for joined multi-line matches spanning at most window lines. If joined matching fails, it evaluates ordered word tokens using the rarest token in word_lines as a search anchor.

docs.title: SourceIndex.excerpt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def excerpt(self, first: int, last: int, quote) -> tuple[str, bool]:

Description: Extracts a representative snippet of source code spanning lines first through last, capped at _EXCERPT (300) characters. If the snippet exceeds this threshold, it centers a 300-character window around the matched quote.

Parameters:

  • first (int): 0-based starting line index.
  • last (int): 0-based ending line index.
  • quote (Any): The quote string to center around if truncation is required.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool]: A tuple containing (excerpt_text, is_truncated).

Example:

def excerpt(self, first: int, last: int, quote) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    text = self.text(first, last).strip()
    if len(text) <= _EXCERPT:
        return text, False
    flat, wanted = _collapse(text), _collapse(quote)
    pos = max(flat.find(wanted), 0)
    start = max(0, min(pos - max(0, (_EXCERPT - len(wanted)) // 2), len(flat) - _EXCERPT))
    return flat[start : start + _EXCERPT], True

The method retrieves the raw text slice between first and last. When the length is within 300 characters, it returns the text unmodified with False. For longer text, it collapses whitespace and calculates an excerpt window centered on the target quote, returning the 300-character slice marked as True for truncation.

docs.title: verify_file_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verify_file_claims(claims: dict, content: str) -> dict:

Description: Audits LLM-extracted claims for a single file against its source content. Verifies symbols, dependencies, configuration keys, and errors, calculating physical 1-based line numbers, multi-line spans, excerpt strings, and error handling roles.

docs.title: Phase 1: Symbol Verification and Top-level Resolution
docs.text:
index = SourceIndex(content)
result = {key: [] for key in CLAIM_KEYS}
rejected = []
claimed = 0
unparsed = claims.get("unparsed", 0) if isinstance(claims, dict) and isinstance(claims.get("unparsed"), int) else 0
if unparsed:
    claimed += unparsed
    rejected.extend({"kind": "unparsed", "reason": "reply item that is not valid YAML"} for _ in range(unparsed))

symbols = _claim_list(claims, "symbols")
claimed += len(symbols)
kept, symbol_rejects = _verify_symbols(symbols, index)
result["symbols"] = kept
rejected += symbol_rejects

The function constructs a SourceIndex over the file content. Any pre-flagged unparsed YAML reply items are counted toward total claims and directly appended to the rejected queue. Symbol claims are extracted and processed via _verify_symbols, which establishes parent-child relationships and checks signatures.

docs.title: Phase 2: Dependency Evidence Matching
docs.text:
for item in _claim_list(claims, "dependencies"):
    claimed += 1
    target, evidence = _as_text(item.get("target")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
    matches = index.locate(evidence) if target else []
    if not matches:
        rejected.append({"kind": "dependency", "target": target, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "evidence not in source"})
        continue
    first, last, how = matches[0]
    text, truncated = index.excerpt(first, last, evidence)
    entry = {"target": target, "line": first + 1, **_end(first, last), "evidence": text, "match": how}
    result["dependencies"].append({**entry, "truncated": True} if truncated else entry)

Each dependency claim is checked by searching for its evidence quote in the SourceIndex. If the quote cannot be located in the file, the dependency claim is rejected. When located, the entry records 1-based line numbers, matching technique (exact, joined, or tokens), and excerpted evidence text.

docs.title: Phase 3: Configuration and Error Span Extension
docs.text:
for key in ("config", "errors"):
    for item in _claim_list(claims, key):
        claimed += 1
        name, evidence = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
        matches = []
        for first, last, how in index.locate(evidence) if name else []:
            if _names_in(index.text(first, last), name):
                matches.append((first, last, how, False))
                continue
            end = _call_span(index, first, last)
            if end > last and _names_in(index.text(first, end), name):
                matches.append((first, end, how, True))
        if not matches:
            rejected.append({"kind": key, "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "name/evidence not in source"})
            continue
        roles = {m: _error_role(index, m[0], m[1], name) for m in matches} if key == "errors" else {}
        matches.sort(key=lambda m: (_ROLE_RANK.get(roles.get(m), 0), _name_rank(index.text(m[0], m[1]), name), m[3]))
        first, last, how, extended = matches[0]
        # ...

Config keys and error claims are matched against the index. If an evidence quote begins a multi-line function call (such as argparse.add_argument() but the argument name appears on a subsequent line, _call_span extends the line boundary. For error claims, _error_role inspects surrounding keywords to classify the error as raised, caught, or mentioned.

docs.title: Phase 4: Fact Deduplication and Span Narrowing
docs.text:
for key, fields in (("symbols", ("parent", "name")), ("dependencies", ("target",)), ("config", ("name",)), ("errors", ("name",))):
    seen, unique = set(), []
    for entry in result[key]:
        marker = (*(entry.get(field) for field in fields), entry["line"])
        if marker not in seen:
            seen.add(marker)
            unique.append(entry)
    if key in ("config", "errors"):
        narrow_first = sorted(unique, key=lambda e: e.get("end_line", e["line"]) - e["line"])
        kept_spans = []
        for entry in narrow_first:
            low, high = entry["line"], entry.get("end_line", entry["line"])
            if not any(other["name"] == entry["name"] and low <= other["line"] <= high for other in kept_spans):
                kept_spans.append(entry)
        unique = [entry for entry in unique if any(entry is other for other in kept_spans)]
    claimed -= len(result[key]) - len(unique)
    result[key] = unique
result["rejected"] = rejected
result["claimed"] = claimed
result["found"] = claimed - len(rejected)
return result

Duplicate claims sharing identical identities and start lines are pruned. For configuration and error items where overlapping matches occur across expanded and unexpanded spans, the narrowest line span is preserved. The final dictionary reports verified claims, rejected claims with diagnostic reasons, total claimed items, and confirmed items found.

Parameters:

  • claims (dict): Raw dictionary of claims returned by an LLM prompt.
  • content (str): Decoded source file text.

Returns:

  • dict: Verified claims dictionary structured with keys symbols, dependencies, config, errors, rejected, claimed, and found.

docs.title: code_view()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def code_view(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:

Description: Returns a sanitized view of the source lines with comments, docstrings, and multi-line string literals blanked out while preserving exact line numbers and column alignments. Skips globs such as lib/*.sh and ensures block comments are correctly paired.

Parameters:
