Strips extension and splits on /.

docs.title: _is_relative()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _is_relative(target: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether an import path begins with relative navigation prefixes (./ or ../).

Parameters:

  • target (str): Path string.

Returns:

  • bool: True if path is relative.

Example:

def _is_relative(target: str) -> bool:
    return target.replace("\\", "/").startswith(("./", "../"))

Normalizes backslashes to forward slashes before testing for relative prefixes.

docs.title: ModuleTable._suffix_hits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Identifies documented module paths whose terminal segments match tail, prioritizing exact case matches over case-folded matches.

Parameters:

  • tail (list[str]): Path segment suffix.
  • ext (str): File extension constraint.
  • source_path (str): Path of importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Matching module paths.

Example:

def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:
    for fold in (str, str.casefold):
        wanted = [fold(part) for part in tail]
        hits = [
            path
            for path in self.paths
            if path != source_path and (not ext or path.endswith(ext)) and [fold(part) for part in self.segments[path][-len(tail) :]] == wanted
        ]
        if len(hits) > 1:
            near = [path for path in hits if posixpath.dirname(path) == posixpath.dirname(source_path)]
            if len(near) == 1:
                return near
        if hits:
            return hits
    return []

Checks exact case matches first. If multiple candidates are found, it prioritizes a sibling file located in the importing module's directory before returning candidates.

docs.title: ModuleTable._index_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:

Description: Identifies an index or entrypoint file (e.g., __init__.py, index.ts, mod.rs) within a directory according to _INDEX_STEMS.

Parameters:

  • directory (str): Directory path.

Returns:

  • str | None: Path to the index file, or None.

Example:

def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:
    members = {_stem(path): path for path in self.by_dir.get(directory, [])}
    return next((members[stem] for stem in _INDEX_STEMS if stem in members), None)

Iterates over _INDEX_STEMS (mod, index, __init__, init, main, lib) and returns the first matching file present in directory.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_relative()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves relative path import specifiers (./, ../, Rust super::, Python leading dots .models) against the importing file's directory.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Specifier string.
  • source_path (str): Importing module path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing file.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str] | None: (paths, how) or None.

Example:

def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
    text = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,").replace("\\", "/")
    parent = re.match(r"^super(?:::(.*))?$", text)
    if parent:
        directory = posixpath.dirname(source_path)
        if _stem(source_path) in _INDEX_STEMS:
            directory = posixpath.dirname(directory)
        rest = [part for part in (parent.group(1) or "").split("::") if part and _SEGMENT_RE.match(part)]
        for size in range(len(rest), 0, -1):
            base = posixpath.join(directory, *rest[:size])
            hits = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and os.path.splitext(path)[0] == base]
            if len(hits) == 1:
                return hits, "path"
        index_file = self._index_file(directory)
        return ([index_file], "package") if index_file and index_file != source_path else ([], "external")
    # ...

Converts Python leading dots into relative path segments. Normalizes paths via posixpath.normpath and delegates resolution to _resolve_rooted.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_rooted()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves a project-root-relative path against known file stems and directories.

Parameters:

  • base (str): Rooted path without extension.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Importing file tokens.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str] | None: (paths, how) or None.

Example:

def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
    base = "" if base in (".", "") else base
    stem_match = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and (os.path.splitext(path)[0] == base or path == base)]
    if not stem_match:
        stem_match = [
            path
            for path in self.paths
            if path != source_path and posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.basename(path).split(".")[0]) == base
        ]
    if len(stem_match) == 1:
        return stem_match, "path"
    if not stem_match and base in self.by_dir:
        index_file = self._index_file(base)
        used = [
            path for path in self.by_dir[base] if path != source_path and (path == index_file or self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
        ]
        if used:
            return used, "package"
    return None

Matches base against files with any extension. If no exact file matches, it checks if base is a directory; if so, it returns the directory's index file and any sibling files whose symbols appear in source_words.

docs.title: ModuleTable._matches_whole()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether every segment of a target matches the terminal segments of a documented module or directory path.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Target import specifier.
  • source_path (str): Importing file path.

Returns:

  • bool: True if all segments match an internal path.

Example:

def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:
    parts, _ = self.normalize(target)
    return bool(parts) and (
        any(path != source_path and self.segments[path][-len(parts) :] == parts for path in self.paths)
        or any(d.split("/")[-len(parts) :] == parts for d in self.by_dir if d)
    )

Ensures that multi-part Java package imports (e.g., com.acme.shipping.Label) mapping cleanly to .../com/acme/shipping/Label.java are recognized.

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_in_package()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_in_package(self, package: dict, rest: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Resolves sub-paths or symbols referenced within a manifest-declared package directory.

Parameters:

  • package (dict): Package descriptor dictionary.
  • rest (list[str]): Path segments following the package name.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Words in importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Resolved module paths.

Example:

def _resolve_in_package(self, package: dict, rest: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
    directory = package["dir"]
    under = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and (not directory or path.startswith(directory + "/"))]
    root = self._package_root(package, under, source_path, source_words)
    if not rest:
        return root
    for size in range(len(rest), 0, -1):
        tail = rest[:size]
        for fold in (str, str.casefold):
            wanted = [fold(part) for part in tail]
            hits = [path for path in under if [fold(part) for part in self.segments[path][-len(tail) :]] == wanted]
            if len(hits) == 1:
                return hits
            # ...

Filters modules located under package["dir"]. If rest is empty, returns the package root. Otherwise, checks suffixes against paths and subdirectories under the package, falling back to symbols re-exported by the package root or owned by specific files.

docs.title: ModuleTable._package_root()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Locates the primary entrypoint file for a package (e.g., explicit manifest entry, index file in src or lib, or file named after the package).

Parameters:

  • package (dict): Package descriptor.
  • under (list[str]): Modules residing under the package.
  • source_path (str): Importing module path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of entrypoint module paths.

Example:

def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
    directory, entry, last = package["dir"], package["entry"], package["segments"][-1] if package["segments"] else ""
    if entry:
        hits = [path for path in under if path == entry or os.path.splitext(path)[0] == os.path.splitext(entry)[0]]
        if hits:
            return hits[:1]
    for sub in ("", "src", "lib", last, f"src/{last}"):
        index_file = self._index_file(posixpath.join(directory, sub).rstrip("/") if sub else directory)
        if index_file and index_file in under:
            return [index_file]
    # ...

Evaluates explicit manifest entries, common directory conventions (src, lib), and files matching the package name (e.g., lib/shop.rb).

docs.title: ModuleTable._corroborated()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:

Description: Confirms whether a partial path match is corroborated by aliases, namespace declarations, directory ancestry, or referenced symbol names.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Specifier string.
  • parts (list[str]): Parsed segments.
  • size (int): Matched suffix segment length.
  • path (str): Candidate module path.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing file.

Returns:

  • bool: True if corroborated.

Example:

def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:
    if size < len(parts):
        dropped = parts[: len(parts) - size]
        alias = not re.match(r"\w", dropped[0]) and not (self.packages or self.aliases)
        return alias or declares_namespace(self.contents.get(path, ""), dropped[-1]) or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
    if len(parts) == 1 and not _is_relative(target):
        directory, source_dir = posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.dirname(source_path)
        ancestor = not directory or source_dir == directory or source_dir.startswith(directory + "/")
        return ancestor or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
    return True

If leading segments were discarded (e.g., matching app/utils.py for email.utils), corroboration requires a sigil alias, a matching namespace declaration in the target, or shared symbol usage. Bare single-part names matching distant directories require directory ancestry or shared symbols.

docs.title: _names_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Verifies if name occurs in evidence as part of a path or qualified module specifier rather than a standalone identifier.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Quoted line text.
  • name (str): Stem or segment name.
  • extension (str): Target file extension.
  • extensions (set): Known project file extensions.

Returns:

  • bool: True if formatted as a path or specifier.

Example:

def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        before = evidence[match.start() - 1] if match.start() else ""
        after = evidence[match.end() :]
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", after)
        if written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension:
            continue
        if before in _QUALIFIERS or (extension and after.startswith(extension)) or (after and after[0] in _CLOSERS):
            return True
    return False

Scans occurrences of name. Checks if it is preceded by _QUALIFIERS (e.g., /, ., :, ") or followed by the expected file extension or closing delimiter.

docs.title: _plain_occurrence()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Verifies that name appears in evidence without being suffixed by a different documented extension (preventing socket.h from falsely matching socket.cpp).

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence string.
  • name (str): Base symbol or stem.
  • extension (str): Target extension.
  • extensions (set): All project extensions.

Returns:

  • bool: True if a valid plain occurrence exists.

Example:

def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", evidence[match.end() :])
        if not (written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension):
            return True
    return False

Ensures that when multiple files share a basename with different extensions, imports specifying one extension do not match the other.

docs.title: _names_directory()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines if evidence names directory via its terminal path segments.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence line text.
  • directory (str): Directory path string.

Returns:

  • bool: True if evidence names the directory path.

Example:

def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:
    tail = [re.escape(part) for part in directory.split("/")[-2:]]
    return re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + r"(?:\.|/|\\|::)".join(tail) + r"(?!\w)", evidence) is not None

Takes the last two segments of directory and checks whether they appear joined by path delimiters (/, \, ., ::) in the evidence string.

docs.title: _import_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Tests whether the first non-modifier word of evidence belongs to _IMPORT_WORDS.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Quoted line.

Returns:

  • bool: True if prefixed with an import keyword.

Example:

def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:
    words = _words(evidence.lstrip().lstrip("#@"))
    while words and words[0] in _MODIFIERS:
        words = words[1:]
    return bool(words) and words[0] in _IMPORT_WORDS

Strips annotations and access modifiers before checking the leading word against _IMPORT_WORDS.

docs.title: _without_bindings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:

Description: Strips local alias bindings introduced by imports (e.g., Python as billing, C# using Env =, JS import Foo =) from a line.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Import line string.

Returns:

  • str: Sanitized line string with aliases removed.

Example:

def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:
    line = re.sub(r"\bas\s+[\w$]+", " ", line)
    line = re.sub(r"=>\s*[\w$]+", " ", line)
    return re.sub(r"^(\s*(?:global\s+)?(?:using|import)\s+)[\w$]+\s*=(?!=)", r"\1", line)

Removes local alias names so they cannot be mistaken for imported module names or external libraries.

docs.title: _bare_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:

Description: Removes leading relative navigation slashes and dots (./, ../, /, .) from a path string.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw path string.

Returns:

  • str: Clean path without leading navigation syntax.

Example:

def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"^(?:\.{1,2}/|/|\.+)+", "", text)

Strips relative path prefixes using regex substitution.

docs.title: _imports_target()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks if evidence imports target via an import statement, a Go import block, a quoted specifier, or inline qualified code usage.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence text.
  • target (str): Target module name.

Returns:

  • bool: True if evidence imports the target.

Example:

def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:
    lines = split_lines(evidence)
    quoted = re.escape(target.strip().strip("\"'`<>"))
    if any(import_statement_like(line) or _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line) for line in lines) or re.search(rf"[\"'`<]{quoted}[\"'`>]", evidence):
        return True
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith(("//", "#", "/*", "*", "--", ";")):
            continue
        code = re.sub(r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`[^`]*`", " ", line)
        if re.search(rf"(?<![\w-]){quoted}(?:::|\.)\w", code):
            return True
    return False

Checks for import statement keywords, quoted specifiers, and qualified inline usage (e.g., shop_core::money::total(...)).

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module employs defensive error isolation patterns to prevent invalid LLM inputs or missing files from interrupting the documentation generation process:

  • Unparsed Claim Recovery: Malformed JSON/YAML blocks identified during extraction passes are passed as claims["unparsed"]. verify_file_claims increments the claimed count and adds corresponding entries to rejected with descriptive reasons rather than raising exceptions.
  • Corrupted Cache Handling: In load_facts(), file read failures (OSError) or JSON decoding errors (ValueError) are caught, returning an empty dictionary ({}). Schema version mismatches are checked silently to trigger cache invalidation.
  • Atomic File Writes: save_facts() writes JSON documents to an adjacent temporary file (f"{path}.tmp") and swaps it via os.replace(). This prevents corrupted facts files if execution terminates during disk writes.
  • Subprocess Isolation: Git command execution in source_commit() uses timeout=10 and handles OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError, returning None if the local directory lacks a Git environment or fails to respond.
  • Ambiguity Rejection: In _verify_symbols() and judge_dependency(), when an identifier matches multiple candidate lines or modules without sufficient context to differentiate them, the claim is rejected with reason "signature matches several lines" or "target matches several modules".

docs.title: files.py
docs.text: Source: utils/files.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/files.py provides lightweight, in-memory file organization and selective content retrieval utilities for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. Operating downstream from crawler modules—such as local filesystem scans and remote GitHub repository ingestors—the module processes collections of codebase files represented as sequential pairs of relative file paths and decoded text content. It addresses two core requirements in Large Language Model (LLM) codebase documentation workflows: generating a compact, token-efficient representation of the repository's directory hierarchy, and retrieving the raw source text of specific files on demand using zero-based index lookups.

The structural formatting logic is implemented in build_directory_tree(), which groups files by parent directory, sorts both directory paths and file basenames lexicographically, and annotates each filename with its integer index (idx:{i}). This formatted tree string is passed into prompt templates across multiple extraction stages—including abstraction identification, relationship mapping, and chapter compilation—enabling the LLM to understand the repository's layout and reference files by index without requiring full file contents in the initial context window. Complementing this, get_content_for_indices() extracts source text exclusively for designated file indices, constructing an indexed mapping that downstream pipeline nodes supply to targeted evaluation prompts.

The module is stateless, deterministic, and self-contained, relying exclusively on Python standard library modules (os and collections.defaultdict). It implements defensive safeguards, including out-of-bounds index suppression to prevent runtime termination and path normalization that resolves root-level files to . rather than empty directory strings. By enforcing consistent alphanumeric ordering across all directory branches and file entries, the module guarantees stable prompt payloads across executions.

docs.title: build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_directory_tree(files_data):

Description: Generates a compact, human-readable directory tree string from a sequence of file tuples. Each file is grouped under its parent directory path and labeled with its zero-based index in files_data. Directories and filenames are sorted in ascending alphanumeric order to produce deterministic output across different environments and operating systems.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): A list of two-element tuples, where each tuple contains the relative file path and its decoded string content.

Returns:

  • str: A formatted multi-line string representing the directory tree, with directories suffixed by / and indented filenames annotated with (idx:{i}).

Raises:

  • None: The function handles empty inputs and missing parent directories without raising exceptions.

Example:

def build_directory_tree(files_data):
    """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples.

    Groups files by directory and formats as a hierarchical tree with file indices.
    Used by ContextRouter, IdentifyAbstractions, MapAbstractions, and CombineTutorial
    to give LLMs structural context about the project layout.
    """
    dir_files = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
        basename = os.path.basename(path)
        dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

    lines = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
        lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
        lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))
    return "\n".join(lines)

The function iterates over files_data using enumerate to preserve the original integer index of each file record. For every file, os.path.dirname(path) determines the parent directory; if the path resides at the repository root, os.path.dirname yields an empty string, which the fallback or "." normalizes to the current directory identifier. The basename is formatted into a descriptor string "{basename} (idx:{i})" and appended to the directory's list in a collections.defaultdict. Once all entries are aggregated, the directory keys are sorted lexicographically, and each directory is rendered as a header line ending with / followed by two-space indented, sorted file entries. This structure minimizes token overhead when passed to language models while retaining index coordinates for downstream content retrieval.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):

Description: Retrieves the text content of specific files from files_data matching the provided collection of integer indices. It constructs a dictionary mapping contextual composite keys ("{index} # {path}") to their corresponding source file contents, safely skipping any indices that fall outside valid list bounds.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): The master list of (path, content) tuples representing the ingested codebase files.
  • indices (Iterable[int]): An iterable collection of integer indices designating which files to extract.

Returns:

  • dict[str, str]: A dictionary where each key is formatted as "{index} # {path}" and each value is the corresponding raw file content string.

Raises:

  • None: Out-of-bounds or negative indices are silently ignored via guard conditions.

Example:

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    """Get file content for specific indices from files_data list."""
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

The function initializes an empty dictionary content_map and iterates through the provided indices sequence. For each candidate index i, it executes a bounds-checking guard condition 0 <= i < len(files_data) to prevent IndexError exceptions caused by hallucinated or invalid LLM index references. Valid entries are unpacked into path and content variables and inserted into the dictionary using the composite key template f"{i} # {path}". Including both the numerical index and the file path in the key provides contextual anchoring for downstream LLM prompts, ensuring that the model maintains awareness of which specific repository path each code block represents.

docs.text:

Element Type Description path str Normalized relative file path within the target repository (e.g., utils/files.py or main.py). content str Complete decoded UTF-8 string content of the source file. 
# Example representation of files_data
[
    ("main.py", "import sys\n..."),
    ("utils/files.py", "import os\n..."),
    ("utils/output.py", "def emit(event):\n...")
]

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/files.py adopts a non-raising, defensive design pattern across its functions:

  • Index Bounds Guarding: In get_content_for_indices(), the index validation expression 0 <= i < len(files_data) protects against negative integers and indices exceeding the list length. Rather than raising IndexError, out-of-range indices are skipped, allowing execution to continue when an LLM requests non-existent file indices.
  • Root Path Normalization: In build_directory_tree(), calling os.path.dirname(path) on top-level paths (such as main.py or README.md) returns an empty string "". The expression os.path.dirname(path) or "." ensures top-level files are organized under the explicit directory key . instead of producing invalid or missing directory headers.
  • Deterministic Output: Directory paths and filenames are sorted using Python's built-in sorted() before formatting, preventing variation in prompt strings across runs caused by non-deterministic dictionary key ordering.

docs.title: i18n.py
docs.text: Source: utils/i18n.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/i18n.py provides the internationalization (i18n) and automated translation subsystem for user interface strings within the repository. Originally factored out of utils/output.py, this module breaks a circular dependency cycle (output.py → call_llm.py → token_utils.py → output.py). By isolating the inference dependencies required for string localization into a dedicated component, output.py can delegate translation jobs to i18n.py without coupling itself directly to LLM orchestration infrastructure.

The module inspects the localized string registry (strings.csv), identifies entries missing translations for a requested target language, and compiles missing key-value pairs into a structured translation payload. It dynamically loads the translation prompt template, logs token estimation telemetry, and dispatches an LLM inference call through utils.call_llm.call_llm. If the target language column does not yet exist in strings.csv, the module dynamically provisions it.

Once the language model returns translated values, the module extracts the JSON response via regular expressions, parses the translated keys, and persists them back to disk using UTF-8 with Byte Order Mark (utf-8-sig) encoding. This encoding preserves special characters across varying operating systems and ensures compatibility with spreadsheet applications such as Microsoft Excel. If translation fails due to network issues, malformed LLM outputs, or unparseable JSON, the module emits a diagnostic warning and falls back to default English strings without halting application execution.

docs.title: auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def auto_translate(lang_col, language, csv_path, use_cache, thinking_level):

Description: Discovers missing translation keys for a given language column in strings.csv, executes an LLM inference pass to translate them, and persists the updated records back to the CSV file. If translations are written, it signals callers to reload localized caches.

Parameters:

  • lang_col (str): Lowercase language column name in the CSV file (e.g., "vietnamese").
  • language (str): Capitalized human-readable language display name (e.g., "Vietnamese").
  • csv_path (str): Absolute file path to strings.csv.
  • use_cache (bool): Flag indicating whether LLM caching should be used for the call.
  • thinking_level (str | int): Model reasoning effort or thinking level passed to the LLM backend.

Returns:

  • bool: True if new translations were successfully written to disk (signaling the caller to reload its string cache), or False if no translations were needed or if an error occurred.

Raises:

  • None directly. All file I/O, token estimation, network inference, and parsing exceptions are caught internally and handled with diagnostic warnings.

docs.title: Phase 1: Input Validation and Translation Inspection
docs.text:
from utils.output import emit_raw

    if lang_col == "english":
        return False

    if not csv_path or not os.path.exists(csv_path):
        return False

    # Collect strings that have no translation in the target language column
    missing = {}
    is_new_column = False
    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        is_new_column = lang_col not in fieldnames
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue
            # Check if the language column exists and has a value
            lang_text = row.get(lang_col, "").strip() if lang_col in fieldnames else ""
            if lang_text:
                continue  # Already translated

            english_text = row.get("english", "").strip()
            if english_text:
                missing[key] = english_text

    if not missing:
        return False

This initial phase validates preconditions and inspects the persistent storage file. If the requested language is "english", or if csv_path is invalid or missing, the function terminates early with False. The file is opened using utf-8-sig encoding to handle potential byte order marks cleanly. As rows are parsed, comments prefixed with # and empty keys are bypassed. If the target column does not yet exist or contains an empty string for a given key, the corresponding English string is placed into the missing dictionary. If no untranslated keys are identified, execution exits without incurring network overhead.

docs.title: Phase 2: Prompt Formatting and Token Telemetry
docs.text:
# Report what we found
    if is_new_column:
        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] New language '{language}' — adding column to strings.csv")
    emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] {len(missing)} strings need translation to {language}")

    # Batch translate via LLM
    try:
        from utils.call_llm import call_llm

        entries_json = json.dumps(missing, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

        # Load prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md
        prompt_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
            "prompts",
            "common",
            "translate_strings.md",
        )
        with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8") as pf:
            prompt_template = pf.read()
        prompt = prompt_template.format(language=language, entries=entries_json)

        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] Calling LLM to translate {len(missing)} strings...")
        from utils.token_utils import log_token_estimation, resolve_max_tokens

        try:
            context_tokens = resolve_max_tokens({})
        except Exception:
            context_tokens = 0
        log_token_estimation("TranslateStrings", prompt, context_tokens)

In the second phase, telemetry notices inform the user of newly introduced language columns and the count of strings requiring translation. The missing dictionary is serialized to formatted JSON without escaping Unicode characters (ensure_ascii=False). The system loads the prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md relative to the module root and interpolates the language name and serialized entries. Before dispatching the request, token usage is estimated via log_token_estimation, safely resolving maximum tokens through resolve_max_tokens with an exception guard that falls back to 0.

docs.title: Phase 3: LLM Dispatch, Parsing, and Persistence
docs.text:
response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=use_cache, thinking_level=thinking_level, step="translate_strings")

        # Extract JSON from response
        json_match = re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)
        if json_match:
            translations = json.loads(json_match.group())
            translated_count = len(translations)

            # Write translations back into strings.csv
            _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations)
            emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] Translated {translated_count}/{len(missing)} strings — saved to strings.csv")
            return True
        emit_raw("WARNING", "[i18n] LLM response did not contain valid JSON — falling back to English")

    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"[i18n] Translation failed: {e} — falling back to English")

    return False

The final phase invokes call_llm with the step identifier "translate_strings". To isolate the translated dictionary from potential conversational preamble or markdown code blocks returned by the model, the response is filtered using a balanced regular expression matching nested JSON braces. Once parsed by json.loads, the dictionary is dispatched to _write_translations_to_csv for atomic in-place persistence. If the model output fails regex matching or raises an unhandled exception, a warning is emitted via emit_raw, and the function returns False, allowing the application to continue using default English text.

Example:

# Invocation pattern used by localization setup callers:
reload_needed = auto_translate(
    lang_col="vietnamese",
    language="Vietnamese",
    csv_path="/path/to/project/utils/strings.csv",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level="low",
)
if reload_needed:
    # Reload localized dictionary from strings.csv
    pass

docs.title: _write_translations_to_csv()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):

Description: Updates existing rows and introduces new language columns into strings.csv, persisting translated key-value pairs back to disk for subsequent runs.

Parameters:

  • csv_path (str): Absolute file system path to the target strings.csv file.
  • lang_col (str): Column header name corresponding to the target language.
  • fieldnames (list[str]): List of current CSV header fields from the original read pass.
  • translations (dict[str, str]): Key-value mapping of string identifiers to their translated text.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates the file on disk directly.

Raises:

  • OSError: If the target path cannot be read or written due to file system permission issues.
def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):
    """Write LLM translations back into strings.csv, persisting them for future runs.

    If the target language column doesn't exist, it is added to the CSV.
    """
    rows = []

    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        # Add language column if it doesn't exist
        if lang_col not in fieldnames:
            fieldnames.append(lang_col)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if key in translations:
                row[lang_col] = translations[key]
            rows.append(row)

    # Write with BOM so Excel opens as UTF-8 without extra import steps
    with open(csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)

The function performs a two-pass update against the persistent storage file. First, it re-reads strings.csv with utf-8-sig encoding, ensuring fieldnames contains lang_col by appending it to the list if previously absent. For each row parsed by csv.DictReader, if STRING_KEY is present in the translations dictionary, the row dictionary is updated with the translated text. In the second pass, the updated row objects are written out using csv.DictWriter with encoding="utf-8-sig" and newline="", ensuring that spreadsheet applications render multi-byte Unicode strings properly without corrupting line endings.

Example:

# Internal invocation inside auto_translate():
_write_translations_to_csv(
    csv_path="/path/to/strings.csv",
    lang_col="vietnamese",
    fieldnames=["STRING_KEY", "english"],
    translations={"PROMPT_START": "Bắt đầu tiến trình", "PROMPT_END": "Hoàn tất"},
)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/i18n.py implements defensive boundaries to prevent localization errors from causing workflow crashes:

  • Missing File and Precondition Guards: auto_translate verifies file existence and validates that lang_col is not "english". If these checks fail, it exits immediately with False.
  • Token Estimation Resilience: Resolving token bounds can fail in environments lacking configuration attributes. The call to resolve_max_tokens({}) is wrapped in a dedicated try/except block, defaulting context_tokens to 0 on failure so logging can continue.
  • Non-JSON LLM Output Interception: Large language models occasionally prepend markdown formatting or explanations. The module uses a regular expression (re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)) to isolate JSON blocks. If no JSON structure is detected, it logs a warning via emit_raw("WARNING", ...) and returns False.
  • Global Translation Safety Net: The entire inference and persistence sequence is encapsulated in a generic except Exception as e: block. Any transport errors, file lock contentions, or deserialization failures emit a descriptive warning and gracefully degrade execution back to English.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/llm_anthropic.py is the dedicated native Anthropic (Claude) provider implementation within the LLM execution pipeline. Operating directly behind the central gateway in utils/call_llm.py, it encapsulates all Claude-specific API mechanisms, streaming lifecycles, prompt construction, adaptive reasoning configurations, and cost accounting. By isolating Anthropic-specific dependencies and protocols, the module allows the rest of the application to interact with language models through an abstract interface without forcing environments utilizing alternative providers to install the anthropic client SDK.

The module is specifically tuned for modern Claude model families (including Claude 5 and 4.6+ series) while retaining backward compatibility for models requiring token-based budget configurations (such as Haiku 4.5). It natively implements adaptive thinking using the API's output_config.effort parameter, automatically enables optional ephemeral prompt caching, dynamically discovers context and output token boundaries via the Anthropic Models API, and coordinates server-side safety fallbacks (anthropic-beta headers) for models utilizing content classifiers. Every request is streamed to prevent HTTP timeout issues during extensive reasoning or generation cycles.

Operational resilience and precision billing are central to the module's architecture. It implements dynamic token clamping that balances prompt size against model context windows, an automatic one-time retry mechanism that re-requests truncated completions at maximum permissible token ceilings, and a fallback disabling mechanism that gracefully recovers from rejected beta headers. Furthermore, the module tracks multi-iteration usage metrics generated by server-side fallbacks, observes runtime prompt token discrepancies for calibration against local tokenizers, and persists financial ledgers.

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Queries the Anthropic Models API via the client SDK to determine the authoritative input context window and maximum output tokens for a specified model. Results are stored in the module-level _model_limits_cache to avoid repeated remote API lookups during execution. If the API is unreachable or returns an anthropic.APIError, the function emits a warning and gracefully degrades to static offline definitions found in _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier being inspected.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A two-element tuple containing (context_window, max_output_tokens).

Raises:

No exceptions raised externally; catches anthropic.APIError.

Example:

# Look up limits to calculate safe headroom for prompt and generation
context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
cap = anthropic_output_cap()
wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)

The underlying implementation attempts remote retrieval, falling back to cached or hardcoded constants upon failure:

def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (context_window, max_output_tokens) from the Models API, with offline fallback."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    fallback = next((v for k, v in _MODEL_LIMITS.items() if model.startswith(k)), _DEFAULT_LIMITS)
    try:
        info = _get_client().models.retrieve(model)
        limits = (getattr(info, "max_input_tokens", None) or fallback[0], getattr(info, "max_tokens", None) or fallback[1])
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Anthropic Models API | model={model} | context={limits[0]:,} | max_output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
    except anthropic.APIError as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e))
        limits = fallback
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits

The method inspects the in-memory cache before initiating network communication. When invoking retrieve(), it safely inspects max_input_tokens and max_tokens attributes on the response object, falling back to preset boundaries if either property is null. Any unexpected API failure is logged via emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP"), ensuring execution continues unabated.

Description: Maps a generic thinking level string to an effort keyword accepted by the target model family using anthropic_effort() from utils.llm_config. Handles model-specific capabilities such as remapping minimal to low or downgrading xhigh to high on Claude 4.6 family models. Emits a warning if a non-empty level cannot be mapped.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier string.
  • level (str | None): Desired reasoning level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max").

Returns:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Map a thinking level to an effort value the model accepts (None = model default)."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, level)  # minimal → low; xhigh → high on the 4.6 family
    if level and effort is None:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_INVALID", level=level.lower(), model=model, supported=str(list(EFFORT_LEVELS)))
    return effort

The function queries anthropic_effort() to validate compatibility. When an explicit thinking level is supplied but evaluates to None, it formats a localized warning informing the operator of the invalid level and listing all permissible entries from EFFORT_LEVELS.

docs.title: call_anthropic()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_anthropic(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary public inference entry point for executing Claude completions. Manages the full request lifecycle: resolves models and budgets, compiles request parameters and fallback beta headers, dispatches streaming completions, transparently retries output truncated by max_tokens, logs multi-iteration usage metrics, intercepts safety refusals, and extracts plain text from content blocks.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The prompt payload to send to Claude.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Optional thinking intensity override (None uses model default).

Returns:

  • str: The generated text response. If the response remains truncated after retry, returns a TruncatedResponse wrapper.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: Raised when Claude halts generation due to content safety policies (stop_reason == "refusal").

docs.title: Phase 1: Request Sizing and Payload Compilation
docs.text:
model = get_model()
    effort = normalize_effort(model, thinking_level)
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
    max_tokens, ceiling = _resolve_max_tokens(int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()), model, effort)
    params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, max_tokens)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Anthropic request | model={model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | max_tokens={max_tokens:,} | "
        f"fallbacks={'on' if betas else 'off'} | prompt_cache={'on' if 'cache_control' in params else 'off'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

The invocation begins by resolving active model identifiers and normalizing reasoning effort. It retrieves the prompt's token footprint using count_tokens_raw() and scales it by the dynamic token_ratio() calibration multiplier. Using this estimated prompt size, _resolve_max_tokens() calculates the planned max_tokens allocation alongside an absolute context-safe ceiling. The method then passes these arguments into _build_request() to obtain the final message parameters and beta header arrays.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution and Dynamic Truncation Retry
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    message = _send(params, betas)

    if message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and max_tokens < ceiling:
        # Thinking + reply outgrew the budget: retry once at the largest budget that fits.
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}", cap=f"{ceiling:,}")
        _record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model, observe=False)  # same prompt: observe once
        params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, ceiling)
        start = time.time()
        message = _send(params, betas)

The request is dispatched over network transport via _send(), which streams the completion to avoid connection timeouts. If the model concludes processing with stop_reason == "max_tokens" and the initial max_tokens was smaller than the permissible ceiling, the system detects that thinking or response tokens exceeded planned budgets. It logs a warning, persists the partial usage to the ledger without triggering tokenizer re-calibration, re-builds the request allocating the maximum ceiling, and executes a single retry.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry, Refusal Traps, and Text Extraction
docs.text:
_record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model)
    if is_debug():
        _log_thinking(message)

    if _served_by_fallback(message) and message.stop_reason != "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "fallbacks")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED", model=model, served_by=getattr(message, "model", "unknown"))

    if message.stop_reason == "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals")
        details = getattr(message, "stop_details", None)
        category = getattr(details, "category", None) if details else None
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL", model=model, category=category or "unknown")
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")

    text = _extract_text(message)
    if message.stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS:
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED", max_tokens=f"{params['max_tokens']:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(text)
    if not text:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Anthropic response contained no text blocks (stop_reason={message.stop_reason})", dest="LOG")
    return text

In the final phase, _record_usage() logs execution time, token metrics, and pricing across all attempts to the central ledger while passing the observed token ratio to calibration routines. If verbose debugging is enabled, _log_thinking() extracts and emits reasoning summaries to the log file. The method detects whether a server-side fallback model fulfilled the request, logs policy refusals before raising LLMRefusalError, and converts output truncated by context limits into a TruncatedResponse wrapper. If the response is valid, it concatenates and returns all text blocks.

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily constructs and returns the thread-safe singleton anthropic.Anthropic client configured with a maximum retry threshold of 3 for transient network or status codes (408, 409, 429, 5xx).

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • anthropic.Anthropic: The shared API client instance.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        # SDK resolves credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / AUTH_TOKEN / ant profile) and
        # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL itself. SDK retries 408/409/429/5xx with backoff;
        # PocketFlow node retries sit on top of this.
        _client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=3)
    return _client

This helper ensures the SDK client is initialized only when an Anthropic inference task is actually executed, reading standard environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL implicitly via the SDK constructor.

docs.title: _matches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:

Description: Helper evaluating whether a model identifier begins with any prefix string in an iterable collection of prefixes.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model name string to test.
  • prefixes (Iterable[str]): Collection of model prefix strings.

Returns:

  • bool: True if any prefix matches the start of model; otherwise False.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:
    return any(model.startswith(p) for p in prefixes)

Used internally across model classification routines to group models into operational categories such as adaptive thinking, fallback targets, or legacy budgeting without strict equality constraints.

docs.title: _fallback_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:

Description: Resolves the necessary anthropic-beta headers and extra_body payload parameters required to configure server-side refusal fallbacks. Checks the ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS environment variable and the module's _fallbacks_disabled flag.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier string.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], dict]: A pair containing a list of beta header strings and a dictionary of parameters to merge into the request's extra_body.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (betas, extra_body) for server-side refusal fallbacks, or empty when disabled."""
    setting = (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS") or "default").strip()
    if _fallbacks_disabled or setting.lower() == "off":
        return [], {}
    if setting.lower() == "default":
        if not _matches(model, _FALLBACK_PREFIXES):
            return [], {}
        return [_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}
    targets = [m.strip() for m in setting.split(",") if m.strip()]
    return [_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m} for m in targets]}

When ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS is set to "default", fallbacks are restricted to models with active classifiers defined in _FALLBACK_PREFIXES. An explicit comma-separated list enables fallbacks unconditionally for the designated secondary models using the server-side-fallback-2026-06-01 beta protocol.

docs.title: _build_request()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:

Description: Constructs the parameters dictionary and beta header list required by the Anthropic SDK message stream method. Configures adaptive thinking, output effort, budget tokens, top-level ephemeral prompt caching, and server-side fallback bodies.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): Text prompt content.
  • model (str): Anthropic model identifier.
  • effort (str | None): Normalized effort level string or None.
  • max_tokens (int): Maximum output tokens budget.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, list[str]]: A tuple containing the parameters dictionary (params) and a list of beta feature tags (betas).

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    params = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    }
    if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
        if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
            thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
            if is_debug():
                # Readable reasoning summaries go to the log file (never to stdout).
                thinking["display"] = "summarized"
            params["thinking"] = thinking
        if effort:
            params["output_config"] = {"effort": effort}
    elif effort:
        budget = min(_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL[effort], max_tokens - 1_024)
        if budget >= 1_024:
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget}

    if (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE") or "off").strip().lower() == "on":
        params["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}

    betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
    if extra_body:
        params["extra_body"] = extra_body
    return params, betas

The function handles multiple model generations: adaptive models receive an output_config dict and optional reasoning display settings, while older models compute an explicit budget_tokens threshold clamped between 1,024 and max_tokens - 1024. Ephemeral cache control is enabled if ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE=on.

docs.title: _resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Computes the optimal generation token budget and maximum allowable token ceiling. Calculates remaining headroom inside the model's context window after subtracting prompt tokens and safety margins, and clamps output against hardware boundaries and optional configuration caps.

Parameters:

  • prompt_tokens (int): Token count of the input prompt scaled by token ratio calibration.
  • model (str): Target model identifier string.
  • effort (str | None): Desired effort level for planned generation sizing.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A tuple containing (wanted, ceiling), where wanted is the planned token budget and ceiling is the maximum allowable token limit that fits within the context window.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (max_tokens, ceiling): the planned budget and the largest budget allowed."""
    context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)  # same value input_token_budget reserved

    room = max(context_window - prompt_tokens - ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096)
    ceiling = min(output_cap, room, cap) if cap else min(output_cap, room)
    if ceiling < wanted:
        # Small shortfalls (template overhead on a budget-packed prompt) are expected; only report real cuts.
        if ceiling < wanted * 0.9:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED", wanted=f"{wanted:,}", available=f"{ceiling:,}")
        wanted = ceiling
    return wanted, ceiling

The calculation guarantees that room never falls below 4,096 tokens, ensuring space remains for generation even under tight context constraints. If available room forces a reduction of more than 10% below the planned output budget, it publishes a WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED warning.

docs.title: _stream_message()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Dispatches a streaming request through the Anthropic client SDK, selecting either the beta streaming interface or standard streaming interface based on whether beta tags are present.

Parameters:

  • params (dict): Keyword request parameters for message generation.
  • betas (list[str]): List of active beta capability strings.

Returns:

  • anthropic.types.Message: The fully accumulated final message instance after stream closure.

Raises:

  • anthropic.APIError: Raised on transport, authorization, or upstream service errors.

Example:

def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    client = _get_client()
    if betas:
        with client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params) as stream:
            return stream.get_final_message()
    with client.messages.stream(**params) as stream:
        return stream.get_final_message()

By processing all requests within streaming context managers, large responses and long reasoning blocks do not trigger read timeouts. The call blocks until streaming concludes, returning the accumulated Message.

docs.title: _fallback_rejected()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:

Description: Analyzes the error text from a 400 Bad Request error to evaluate whether the failure was caused by lack of support for the server-side fallback beta feature rather than invalid user parameters.

Parameters:

  • error_text (str): Lowercased or raw error message returned by the Anthropic API.
  • params (dict): Request parameters that produced the error.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the API rejected the beta header or default fallbacks; otherwise False.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:
    """True when a 400 rejects the fallback feature itself (beta header not enabled, or
    `fallbacks: "default"` unsupported for this model/account) — not a user config error."""
    text = error_text.lower()
    if "anthropic-beta" in text and "server-side-fallback" in text:
        return True
    return params.get("extra_body", {}).get("fallbacks") == "default" and "fallbacks" in text

This inspection ensures the application distinguishes between fatal parameter errors and unsupported server-side fallback betas, allowing automatic recovery.

docs.title: _send()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: High-level dispatch wrapper executing _stream_message(). If a BadRequestError indicates that server-side fallbacks are rejected by the API endpoint, it sets _fallbacks_disabled = True, logs a diagnostic warning, removes extra_body from parameters, and retries the stream without betas.

Parameters:

  • params (dict): Parameters dictionary for the request.
  • betas (list[str]): Active beta feature flags.

Returns:

  • anthropic.types.Message: The final accumulated API message.

Raises:

  • anthropic.BadRequestError: Re-raised if the bad request was not caused by rejected fallback headers.
  • anthropic.APIError: Any other upstream API error.

Example:

def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    """Send one streamed request; disable fallbacks for the run if the feature is unavailable."""
    global _fallbacks_disabled
    try:
        return _stream_message(params, betas)
    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise

This helper guarantees self-healing execution: once a fallback feature rejection is detected, the run latch disables fallbacks globally to prevent redundant failing calls on subsequent requests.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the monetary cost in USD for a given token breakdown based on longest-prefix matching against the _PRICING lookup table. Cache writes are billed at 1.25x the standard input token rate.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Served model identifier.
  • tokens_in (int): Count of non-cached input tokens.
  • tokens_out (int): Count of generated output tokens.
  • cache_read (int): Count of tokens read from prompt cache.
  • cache_write (int): Count of tokens written to prompt cache.

Returns:

  • float | None: Total cost in USD, or None if the model has no entry in _PRICING.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:
    price = next((_PRICING[k] for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if (model or "").startswith(k)), None)
    if price is None:
        return None
    p_in, p_out, p_read = price
    return (tokens_in * p_in + tokens_out * p_out + cache_read * p_read + cache_write * p_in * 1.25) / 1_000_000

Matches models using reverse length-sorted prefix matching so specific entries (e.g., claude-opus-5-5) take precedence over broader family prefixes (e.g., claude-opus-5).

docs.title: _tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:

Description: Extracts standard token counts safely from an SDK Usage object, substituting 0 for any missing or None attributes.

Parameters:

  • usage: An Anthropic SDK usage object or iteration dictionary.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int, int, int]: A tuple containing (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens).

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    return (
        getattr(usage, "input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
    )

Provides a defensive extraction layer shielding downstream ledger calculations from missing or dynamically structured usage responses across different SDK versions.

docs.title: _thinking_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:

Description: Safely extracts the count of reasoning/thinking tokens from the output_tokens_details structure of a usage record.

Returns:

def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:
