Extracts internal thinking token counts to allow accurate reporting of cognitive effort vs. direct completion output.

docs.title: _declined_before_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a request was rejected by safety classifiers before generating any output tokens. Such requests incur no financial charge.

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.

Returns:

  • bool: True if stop_reason == "refusal" and output_tokens == 0; otherwise False.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:
    """A refusal with no output tokens at all is not billed (the same rule as for fallback iterations)."""
    return getattr(message, "stop_reason", None) == "refusal" and not (getattr(message.usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0)

Enforces Anthropic's billing specification, ensuring zero cost is logged for requests terminated by content safety boundaries prior to output emission.

docs.title: _billed_entries()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _billed_entries(message) -> list:

Description: Collects all usage entries that represent billed attempts. When server-side fallbacks occur, it selects all iterations from usage.iterations that generated output tokens. Otherwise, it selects top-level usage unless declined prior to output generation.

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.

Returns:

  • list: Collection of usage entries subject to billing.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _billed_entries(message) -> list:
    """Usage entries of the billed attempts: every usage.iterations entry with output (server-side
    fallbacks), else the top-level usage unless the request was declined before any output."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        return [entry for entry in iterations if (getattr(entry, "output_tokens", 0) or 0) > 0]
    return [] if _declined_before_output(message) else [message.usage]

Handles multi-turn fallback chains where multiple models may have run during a single API invocation, isolating only those attempts that generated chargeable tokens.

docs.title: _billed_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:

Description: Computes the aggregated sum of tokens across all billed attempts. Combines base input, prompt cache reads, and prompt cache writes into total input.

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int, int, int, int]: A 5-tuple of (total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) tokens.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
    """(total input incl. cache read/write, output, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) summed over the
    billed attempts (_billed_entries), so token totals match _message_cost."""
    total_in = out = cache_read = cache_write = thinking = 0
    for entry in _billed_entries(message):
        tokens_in, tokens_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        total_in += tokens_in + read + write
        out += tokens_out
        cache_read += read
        cache_write += write
        thinking += _thinking_tokens(entry)
    return total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking

Ensures aggregated token values displayed in debug summaries match the financial accounting computed by _message_cost().

docs.title: _message_cost()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated total USD cost of a message response. Handles both single-attempt usage and server-side fallback chains by pricing each attempt according to its specific model pricing tier.

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.
  • served_model (str): Default fallback model identifier string if an entry does not declare its own model.

Returns:

  • float | None: Total computed cost in USD, or None if any participating model lacks pricing data.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        total, known = 0.0, True
        for entry in iterations:
            tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(entry)
            if tokens_out == 0:
                continue  # declined before any output (primary or fallback attempt): not billed
            cost = _price(getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write)
            known = known and cost is not None
            total += cost or 0.0
        return total if known else None
    if _declined_before_output(message):
        return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
    return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))

Iterates over fallback attempts, verifying pricing for every model involved. If all participating models have established pricing definitions, it returns the sum of all individual costs.

docs.title: _record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:

Description: Records detailed usage statistics into the application ledger via utils.llm_common.record_usage(). Feeds observed token ratios into utils.token_utils.observe_prompt_tokens() for dynamic tokenizer calibration, and prints structured debug telemetry.

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): Input token count estimated prior to the call.
  • effort (str | None): Effort setting applied to the generation.
  • elapsed (float): Call duration in seconds.
  • model (str): Requested model string.
  • observe (bool): Whether to update tokenizer calibration with this request's observed token count. Default True.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:
    from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
    has_iterations = bool(getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None))
    entries = _billed_entries(message)
    if not entries:
        record_usage("ANTHROPIC", served_model, cost=0.0, measured=False)  # declined before any output: not billed
    # One ledger request per billed attempt (primary + fallback each billed at its own model's rate), so
    # request counts, per-request estimate deviation and the model list stay correct.
    for entry in entries:
        t_in, t_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        entry_model = (getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model) if has_iterations else served_model
        record_usage(
            "ANTHROPIC",
            entry_model,
            input_tokens=t_in + read + write,
            output_tokens=t_out,
            thinking_tokens=_thinking_tokens(entry),
            cache_read=read,
            cache_write=write,
            cost=_price(entry_model, t_in, t_out, read, write) if has_iterations else _message_cost(message, served_model),
        )
    total_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking = _billed_tokens(message)  # totals for the debug line
    cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)

    # Observed Claude/tiktoken ratio of the attempt that produced this message (top-level usage),
    # fed to the calibration unless another model (server-side fallback) served it.
    tokens_in, _, read, write = _tokens(message.usage)
    attempt_in = tokens_in + read + write
    ratio = attempt_in / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    if observe and model and not _served_by_fallback(message):
        observe_prompt_tokens("ANTHROPIC", model, raw_prompt_tokens, attempt_in, served_model=served_model)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"ANTHROPIC USAGE | model={served_model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | stop={message.stop_reason} | "
        f"in={total_in:,} | out={tokens_out:,} | thinking={thinking:,} | cache_read={cache_read:,} | cache_write={cache_write:,} | "
        f"est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="BOTH",
    )

The function splits usage logging across distinct entries in _billed_entries(). If fallbacks occurred, each model in the chain is accounted for at its own pricing rate. Calibration observation is conditionally suppressed if the response was fulfilled by a fallback model, preventing ratio pollution across differing tokenizers.

docs.title: _log_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _log_thinking(message) -> None:

Description: Scans response content blocks for thinking/reasoning segments and logs them to the application log file when debug logging is active.

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _log_thinking(message) -> None:
    for block in message.content:
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "thinking" and getattr(block, "thinking", ""):
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{block.thinking}", dest="LOG")

Reasoning summaries are routed exclusively to disk logs (dest="LOG") and never written to standard output, ensuring clean terminal presentation while preserving audit trails.

docs.title: _served_by_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:

Description: Inspects content blocks and usage iterations to determine whether the final completion was fulfilled by a fallback model rather than the primary target model.

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.

Returns:

  • bool: True if any block or iteration contains fallback metadata; otherwise False.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:
    if any(getattr(block, "type", None) == "fallback" for block in message.content):
        return True
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    return any(getattr(entry, "type", None) == "fallback_message" for entry in iterations)

Detects whether Claude's server-side safety classifier initiated a routing handover to an alternative model during request processing.

docs.title: _extract_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _extract_text(message) -> str:

Description: Concatenates and returns the text from all content blocks in the message whose type is "text".

Parameters:

  • message: The Anthropic response Message object.

Returns:

  • str: Joined response text string.

Raises:

No custom exceptions raised.

Example:

def _extract_text(message) -> str:
    return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text")

Extracts only visible completion output, ignoring non-text elements such as reasoning blocks or fallback tracking markers.

docs.title: Model Pricing Table (_PRICING)
docs.text:
Defines token pricing rates in USD per one million tokens. Matched against model names using longest-prefix evaluation.

Field Index Name Type Description 0 input_price float Cost per 1M non-cached input tokens. 1 output_price float Cost per 1M generated output tokens. 2 cache_read_price float Cost per 1M tokens read from prompt cache.

Note: 5-minute cache writes are billed at input_price * 1.25.

Representative entries from _PRICING:

Model Prefix Input ($/M) Output ($/M) Cache Read ($/M) Cache Write ($/M) claude-opus-5-5 4.00 20.00 0.20 5.00 claude-opus-5 5.00 25.00 0.50 6.25 claude-fable-5-1 10.00 50.00 0.25 12.50 claude-fable-5 10.00 50.00 1.00 12.50 claude-mythos-5-1 10.00 50.00 0.25 12.50 claude-mythos-5 10.00 50.00 1.00 12.50 claude-sonnet-5 2.00 10.00 0.20 2.50 claude-opus-4-8 5.00 25.00 0.50 6.25 claude-haiku-4-5 1.00 5.00 0.10 1.25

docs.title: Request Payload Shape (params)
docs.text:
The dictionary constructed by _build_request() and dispatched to client.messages.stream() or client.beta.messages.stream().

Key Type Required Description model str Yes Target Claude model identifier. max_tokens int Yes Upper bound on generated tokens. messages list[dict] Yes Single-turn message list containing [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. thinking dict No Adaptive thinking configuration (e.g., {"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"}) or legacy budget tokens. output_config dict No Effort specification (e.g., {"effort": "high"}). cache_control dict No Cache directive (e.g., {"type": "ephemeral"}) when prompt caching is active. extra_body dict No Fallback configuration dictionary passed when server-side fallbacks are enabled.

docs.title: Billed Token Metrics Tuple
docs.text:
The 5-element integer tuple returned by _billed_tokens():

Index Field Type Description 0 total_in int Sum of all input tokens (standard input + cache read + cache write). 1 out int Sum of generated completion and thinking tokens. 2 cache_read int Tokens retrieved from ephemeral prompt cache. 3 cache_write int Tokens written to ephemeral prompt cache. 4 thinking int Internal reasoning tokens consumed during generation.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
The module intercepts situations where Claude refuses a prompt due to safety policy classifications (stop_reason == "refusal"). It extracts classification metadata from message.stop_details.category and raises LLMRefusalError:

    if message.stop_reason == "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals")
        details = getattr(message, "stop_details", None)
        category = getattr(details, "category", None) if details else None
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL", model=model, category=category or "unknown")
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")

Downstream callers in utils/call_llm.py treat LLMRefusalError as an unretryable failure and cache the refusal event to avoid repeated billing.

docs.title: Fallback Beta Incompatibility Recovery
docs.text:
When server-side fallbacks are requested via anthropic-beta headers, older accounts or specific models may reject the beta header with an HTTP 400 BadRequestError. The _send() function intercepts this error, disables fallbacks globally, and retries the request transparently:

    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise

docs.title: Context Boundary Truncation
docs.text:
Truncation occurs when output terminates with stop_reason in ("max_tokens", "model_context_window_exceeded"). The module handles this in two stages:

  1. Dynamic Retry: If the initial max_tokens allocation was below the maximum permissible ceiling, it logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY and retries once allocating ceiling.
  2. Truncated Response Object: If generation remains truncated after the retry, it records the event, emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED, and wraps the extracted text in a TruncatedResponse object:
    text = _extract_text(message)
    if message.stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS:
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED", max_tokens=f"{params['max_tokens']:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(text)

The TruncatedResponse return signals utils/call_llm.py that the output was prematurely severed, preventing it from being committed to the on-disk cache.

  • utils/llm_config.py — defines Anthropic model prefixes, default model identifiers, effort mapping logic, output caps, and token budget profiles.
  • utils/output.py — provides application logging facilities (emit, emit_raw, is_debug) used for telemetry and warnings.
  • utils/token_utils.py — supplies prompt token counting utilities, runtime token ratio calibration, and token observation hooks.

docs.title: llm_common.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_common.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/llm_common.py module provides provider-neutral foundation primitives, data structures, and stateful tracking mechanisms shared across all Large Language Model (LLM) vendor adapters within the codebase. It operates strictly without external third-party SDK dependencies, relying entirely on the Python standard library (contextlib, contextvars, and hashlib). By isolating common abstractions from provider specifics, this module decouples core workflow nodes from vendor implementations such as Anthropic, Google Gemini, and OpenRouter, establishing a consistent runtime contract for error signaling, refusal management, and financial token accounting.

Architecturally, the module fulfills four primary responsibilities:

  1. Signal In-Band Truncation: Provides the TruncatedResponse string specialization to denote model replies that hit token generation ceilings without raising immediate runtime errors. This allows callers to inspect partial responses while explicitly barring them from disk caches and downstream parsers.
  2. Refusal Circuit Breaking and Memoization: Implements the LLMRefusalError hierarchy and an in-memory SHA-256 hash registry (_refused). This registry captures safety, moderation, and policy refusals, distinguishing between unretryable prompt-level rejections (which are short-circuited to avoid billable retries) and retryable candidate-generation blocks.
  3. Multi-Dimensional Telemetry and Ledger Accounting: Tracks token metrics, reasoning tokens, prompt caching breakdowns (reads and writes), USD monetary costs, and operational events across both vendor providers and pipeline workflow steps using an execution context variable (_current_step).
  4. Log De-duplication: Supplies a call-site memoization utility (warn_once) that suppresses redundant warning messages across batch generation loops.

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: A specialized subclass of Python's built-in str that signals that an LLM completion was prematurely cut off by the provider due to token constraints (such as reaching max_tokens or exhausting the context window). It behaves as a standard string for string inspection and printing operations, but exposes a boolean class attribute truncated = True. Gateway callers such as call_llm use this attribute to identify partial responses, ensuring they are excluded from the persistent disk cache and prompting downstream YAML or JSON parsers to reject the output and trigger retries.

Example:

class TruncatedResponse(str):
    """Response text from a reply that was cut off; call_llm returns it but never caches it."""

    truncated = True

The implementation relies on subclassing the immutable primitive str and binding the class-level marker truncated = True. Because TruncatedResponse is an instance of str, functions that handle plain text strings can inspect, log, or evaluate its length without type casting. However, downstream persistence layers intercept this class specifically to prevent storing partial code blocks, truncated JSON documents, or cut-off Markdown chapters in long-term caches.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):

Description: Exception raised when an LLM provider or its configured fallback candidates refuse to process or complete a prompt. This encompasses Claude refusals, Google Gemini safety or recitation blocks, and OpenRouter content moderation filters. It differentiates between deterministic refusals (retryable=False, representing static prompt policy violations that must never be re-sent) and stochastic candidate rejections (retryable=True, representing output generation blocks where re-sampling may produce a valid completion).

docs.title: Phase 1: Initialization
docs.text:
def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
        self.model = model
        self.category = category
        self.provider = provider
        self.retryable = retryable
        super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")

The constructor accepts the target model identifier, an optional refusal category string supplied by the provider, the canonical provider name, and a boolean flag indicating whether the failure is retryable. It assigns these parameters to instance attributes for runtime introspection and initializes the underlying RuntimeError base class with a standardized diagnostic message formatted as "{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category})".

docs.title: request_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:

Description: Generates an authoritative 64-character SHA-256 hexadecimal hash string uniquely identifying an LLM invocation. The hash is constructed by combining the provider name, the model string, a normalized thinking effort level, and the prompt text. This hash serves as the cache lookup key in the in-memory refusal memoization table to identify repeated requests across workflow steps and node retries.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Canonical provider name (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER").
  • model (str): Model name or identifier string.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Reasoning effort configuration (e.g., "low", "high", or None), which defaults to "default".
  • prompt (str): The complete UTF-8 prompt payload dispatched to the model.

Returns:

  • str: A 64-character SHA-256 hexadecimal digest string.

Raises: None.

Example:

def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The function computes the hash by first formatting a single-line scoping prefix containing the provider, model, and lowercase thinking level separated by pipe delimiters and terminated by a newline. It concatenates this prefix with the raw prompt text, encodes the aggregate string into UTF-8 bytes, and processes it through hashlib.sha256(). This design ensures that identical prompts evaluated under different models, providers, or reasoning levels produce distinct keys.

docs.title: remember_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:

Description: Stores a non-retryable refusal exception in the module-level memoization dictionary _refused. When a deterministic policy rejection occurs, recording it prevents downstream retry mechanisms from resubmitting the identical payload, thereby preventing rate-limit consumption and redundant API charges for partial streams.

Parameters:

  • key (str): The unique 64-character SHA-256 request identifier computed via request_key().
  • error (LLMRefusalError): The refusal exception instance capturing model, provider, and category metadata.

Returns:

  • None

Raises: None.

Example:

def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:
    _refused[key] = error

The helper performs a direct assignment of the LLMRefusalError instance into the module-level _refused dictionary keyed by the calculated hash. Because Python dictionaries retain in-memory state across imports within the same process lifecycle, any subsequent invocation throughout the pipeline run can instantly inspect prior refusal states without performing remote network calls.

docs.title: previous_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:

Description: Queries the internal refusal memoization table for an existing LLMRefusalError associated with the provided request key. It acts as an early-exit circuit breaker for inference calls.

Parameters:

  • key (str): The 64-character SHA-256 request hash generated by request_key().

Returns:

  • LLMRefusalError | None: The cached refusal exception if previously encountered and recorded, or None if the request has not been refused.

Raises: None.

Example:

def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:
    return _refused.get(key)

The implementation performs a safe retrieval from the internal _refused dictionary using .get(key). If a matching key is found, the caller (typically call_llm) immediately re-raises the stored exception without dispatching HTTP requests or SDK calls, thereby protecting API budgets and avoiding pipeline delays.

docs.title: usage_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_step(step: str | None):

Description: A context manager that scopes LLM token usage and event accounting to a specific pipeline execution step. It temporarily modifies the thread- and task-local _current_step context variable, ensuring that all invocations of record_usage() and count_event() within the enclosed code block attribute their metrics to the specified workflow node.

Parameters:

  • step (str | None): Name of the active pipeline step (e.g., "draft_chapters", "map_abstractions"). If None or empty, defaults to "other".

Returns:

  • Generator context manager yielding control to the enclosed code block.

Raises: None.

Example:

@contextlib.contextmanager
def usage_step(step: str | None):
    """Attribute every record_usage / count_event inside the block to `step`."""
    token = _current_step.set(step or "other")
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _current_step.reset(token)

The function utilizes @contextlib.contextmanager to encapsulate the lifecycle of a contextvars.Token. Upon entry, it calls _current_step.set(step or "other") and stores the resulting token. The enclosed logic executes within a try block, and the finally block guarantees that _current_step.reset(token) restores the prior context state, preserving step boundaries even when exceptions occur inside the context.

docs.title: current_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def current_step() -> str:

Description: Retrieves the identifier of the workflow step currently associated with the calling context.

Parameters: None.

Returns:

  • str: The name of the active pipeline step, or "other" if no step context has been set.

Raises: None.

Example:

def current_step() -> str:
    return _current_step.get()

The function delegates directly to the get() method of the module-level _current_step context variable. Because _current_step is backed by Python's contextvars subsystem, this lookup remains isolated across concurrent coroutines or asynchronous execution threads.

docs.title: record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature:

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:

Description: Records the resource consumption, token metrics, and monetary cost of an individual API request. It increments running totals in both the provider-level ledger (_usage) and the active step-level ledger (_steps).

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Name of the LLM provider (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI").
  • model (str): Identifier of the specific model that processed the request.
  • input_tokens (int, keyword-only): Total prompt tokens counted by the provider, including cached tokens. Defaults to 0.
  • output_tokens (int, keyword-only): Total generated tokens, including reasoning/thinking tokens. Defaults to 0.
  • thinking_tokens (int, keyword-only): Explicit subset of output tokens dedicated to reasoning. Defaults to 0.
  • cache_read (int, keyword-only): Tokens read from the provider's prompt cache. Defaults to 0.
  • cache_write (int, keyword-only): Tokens written to the provider's prompt cache. Defaults to 0.
  • cost (float | None, keyword-only): Billed request cost in USD. If None, indicates unknown pricing and increments the unpriced call counter. Defaults to None.
  • measured (bool, keyword-only): Indicates whether the provider returned verified usage metrics. If False (such as on an unbilled decline or uninstrumented endpoint), the request increments unmeasured_calls. Defaults to True.

Returns:

  • None

Raises: None.

Example:

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Accumulate one API request. `input_tokens` = total prompt tokens (cached included);
    `output_tokens` includes thinking. `cost` is USD; None = unknown price (counted as unpriced).
    measured=False: the provider reported no usage, or the request was an unbilled decline — it counts
    as a request but is left out of estimate-vs-billed comparisons (`unmeasured_calls`)."""
    for entry in (_usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry()), _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())):
        if model:
            entry["models"].add(model)
        entry["calls"] += 1
        if not measured:
            entry["unmeasured_calls"] += 1
        entry["input"] += input_tokens or 0
        entry["output"] += output_tokens or 0
        entry["thinking"] += thinking_tokens or 0
        entry["cache_read"] += cache_read or 0
        entry["cache_write"] += cache_write or 0
        if cost is None:
            entry["unpriced_calls"] += 1
        else:
            entry["cost"] += cost

The function iterates over two ledger target dictionaries: the entry for the specified provider within _usage and the entry for the active step within _steps (resolved via current_step()). If an entry does not exist, setdefault initializes it using _new_entry(). It tracks distinct model names in the models set, increments the total call count, and conditionally increments unmeasured_calls when measured is False. Token counts are accumulated using defensive fallback checks (or 0). When cost is None, the function increments unpriced_calls; otherwise, it adds the floating-point USD amount to cost.

docs.title: count_event()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:

Description: Increments an operational event counter (such as "refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations") for both the specified provider and the currently active workflow step.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Target provider name.
  • event (str): Event key corresponding to a counter defined in _new_entry() (typically "refusals", "fallbacks", or "truncations").

Returns:

  • None

Raises: None.

Example:

def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:
    """Increment 'refusals' | 'fallbacks' | 'truncations' for a provider (and the current step)."""
    _usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry())[event] += 1
    _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())[event] += 1

The function retrieves or creates the ledger entry for the given provider in _usage and for the active step in _steps, then increments the counter specified by event by 1. This dual-accounting model enables the system to report diagnostic event distributions by both provider infrastructure and workflow stage.

docs.title: record_estimate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:

Description: Records an upfront token estimation or cache hit for a specific step. This telemetry allows the system to compare estimated prompt tokens against billed provider metrics or track computational savings from local disk cache hits.

Parameters:

  • step (str): Name of the pipeline workflow step. If empty, falls back to "other".
  • estimated_input (int): Number of estimated input prompt tokens before dispatch.
  • cache_hit (bool, keyword-only): Whether the request was served directly from the local disk cache without hitting the provider network. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • None

Raises: None.

Example:

def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:
    """Add call_llm's input estimate for a call (billed or served from the LLM cache) to a step."""
    entry = _steps.setdefault(step or "other", _new_entry())
    if cache_hit:
        entry["cache_hits"] += 1
    else:
        entry["estimated_input"] += estimated_input or 0

The function locates the target step dictionary within _steps. If cache_hit is true, it increments cache_hits, bypassing input token accumulation since no remote prompt tokens were processed. If cache_hit is false, it increments estimated_input by the estimated token count, providing the baseline for subsequent estimation accuracy calculations.

docs.title: usage_snapshot()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:

Description: Captures a snapshot of a provider's current metrics, excluding non-numeric set fields such as models. By taking snapshots immediately before and after an API invocation, callers can calculate per-call token usage differentials via usage_delta().

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Canonical provider name to inspect.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing copies of all metric counters for the provider, excluding the models key. If the provider has no recorded usage, returns an initialized dictionary of zeroed counters.

Raises: None.

Example:

def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:
    """Copy of a provider's running totals (diff two snapshots to get one call's usage)."""
    entry = _usage.get(provider)
    return {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "models"} if entry else {k: v for k, v in _new_entry().items() if k != "models"}

The function checks whether an entry exists for provider in _usage. If present, it uses a dictionary comprehension to copy all keys except "models". If no entry exists, it generates a default entry via _new_entry() and strips "models", ensuring callers always receive a uniform dictionary schema with zeroed values.

docs.title: usage_delta()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:

Description: Calculates the arithmetic difference between two usage snapshots, producing a delta dictionary representing the net resources consumed by an operation.

Parameters:

  • before (dict): Usage snapshot taken prior to request execution.
  • after (dict): Usage snapshot taken following request completion.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary where each key maps to the difference after[k] - before.get(k, 0).

Raises: None.

Example:

def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: after[k] - before.get(k, 0) for k in after}

The function iterates over the keys of the after snapshot, subtracting the corresponding numeric value from before (defaulting missing keys in before to 0). This differential calculation isolates the exact token and cost footprint of a single call, even when concurrent or sequential calls are updating the global ledger.

docs.title: get_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_usage_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles a comprehensive usage summary for all providers that processed at least one API call during the current execution run. The returned dictionary formats internal sets into sorted lists and includes derived metadata flags.

Parameters: None.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary mapping provider names to sanitized public ledger entries. Providers with zero recorded calls are omitted.

Raises: None.

Example:

def get_usage_summary() -> dict:
    """{provider: totals} for every provider that made at least one call this run."""
    return {provider: _public(entry) for provider, entry in _usage.items() if entry["calls"]}

The function iterates over _usage.items(), filtering out any provider entry whose calls counter equals 0. For all active providers, it transforms the raw internal ledger entry into a public-facing dictionary using _public(), converting the internal models set into a sorted list and evaluating whether all costs are fully known.

docs.title: get_step_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_step_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles an aggregated summary of usage across all pipeline workflow steps that recorded at least one API call or served at least one prompt from the local disk cache.

Parameters: None.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary mapping step names (in order of first appearance) to sanitized public ledger entries.

Raises: None.

Example:

def get_step_summary() -> dict:
    """{step: totals} in first-use order, including steps answered only from the LLM cache."""
    return {step: _public(entry) for step, entry in _steps.items() if entry["calls"] or entry["cache_hits"]}

The function iterates through the _steps dictionary, preserving its insertion order. It retains steps that executed remote API calls (entry["calls"] > 0) or fulfilled queries via cache hits (entry["cache_hits"] > 0). Each qualifying entry is passed through _public() to normalize fields for summary reporting.

docs.title: reset_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def reset_usage() -> None:

Description: Resets all in-memory usage tracking ledgers and refusal registries. This clears all accumulated metrics, step allocations, and refusal memoization entries, returning the module to its initial state (typically used between test cases or independent pipeline runs).

Parameters: None.

Returns:

  • None

Raises: None.

Example:

def reset_usage() -> None:
    _usage.clear()
    _steps.clear()
    _refused.clear()

The function invokes the .clear() method on the three primary mutable module-level dictionaries: _usage, _steps, and _refused. Note that _warned is intentionally retained to prevent duplicate warning messages from re-appearing after a ledger reset within the same process.

docs.title: warn_once()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:

Description: Tracks diagnostic warning events to ensure that a given warning key and its argument tuple are logged only once per process execution.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Unique category identifier or warning format string.
  • *parts (Any): Variable arguments that distinguish specific instances of the warning (e.g., model name, threshold value).

Returns:

  • bool: True if this specific (key, *parts) combination has not been logged previously during the current run; False if it has already been observed.

Raises: None.

Example:

def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:
    """True the first time a (key, parts) combination is seen this run."""
    marker = (key, *parts)
    if marker in _warned:
        return False
    _warned.add(marker)
    return True

The function constructs a composite tuple marker = (key, *parts) and checks its membership against the module-level _warned set. If the marker is already present, it returns False. If absent, it inserts the marker into _warned and returns True, signaling to the caller that the warning should be emitted.

docs.title: _refused
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _refused = {}

Description: Module-level dictionary mapping 64-character SHA-256 request hash strings to their corresponding LLMRefusalError instances. It acts as an in-memory cache to prevent repeated submission of declined prompts.

docs.title: _usage
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _usage = {}

Description: Module-level dictionary mapping provider name strings (e.g., "ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI") to their respective ledger entry dictionaries generated by _new_entry().

docs.title: _steps
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _steps = {}

docs.title: _new_entry()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _new_entry() -> dict:

Description: Factory function that creates and returns a new zeroed ledger dictionary schema. Used to initialize new provider or workflow step entries in _usage and _steps.

Parameters: None.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary initialized with default counter values and an empty set of models.

Raises: None.

Example:

def _new_entry() -> dict:
    return {
        "models": set(),
        "calls": 0,
        "input": 0,
        "output": 0,
        "thinking": 0,
        "cache_read": 0,
        "cache_write": 0,
        "cost": 0.0,
        "unpriced_calls": 0,
        "unmeasured_calls": 0,
        "refusals": 0,
        "fallbacks": 0,
        "truncations": 0,
        "estimated_input": 0,
        "cache_hits": 0,
    }

The factory instantiates a dictionary containing all fifteen standard tracking fields. The "models" key is initialized to an empty set() to accumulate unique model identifiers without duplication. All token, call, and event counters are set to 0, while the monetary "cost" is initialized to 0.0.

docs.title: _public()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:

Description: Transforms an internal ledger dictionary into a public-facing representation suitable for serialization and reporting. It converts the mutable models set into a sorted list and appends a derived boolean flag cost_known.

Parameters:

  • entry (dict): An internal ledger dictionary structured according to _new_entry().

Returns:

  • dict: A shallow copy of the input entry with models sorted as a list of strings and cost_known set to True if unpriced_calls == 0, or False otherwise.

Raises: None.

Example:

def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:
    return dict(entry, models=sorted(entry["models"]), cost_known=entry["unpriced_calls"] == 0)

The function uses the dict() constructor to clone entry while overriding the models key with sorted(entry["models"]). This produces deterministic, JSON-serializable output for downstream consumers. It also calculates cost_known = (entry["unpriced_calls"] == 0), allowing external callers to immediately verify whether the recorded cost accurately reflects the entire operational volume or is missing unpriced requests.

docs.title: Internal Ledger Entry
docs.text:
The primary dictionary structure instantiated by _new_entry() and accumulated inside _usage and _steps.

Field Type Description models set[str] Set of unique model identifiers that executed calls under this provider or step. calls int Total number of API requests dispatched. input int Total prompt tokens reported by the provider (including cached tokens). output int Total completion tokens generated, including reasoning tokens. thinking int Subset of output tokens dedicated to model reasoning/thinking. cache_read int Number of prompt tokens read from the provider's server-side cache. cache_write int Number of prompt tokens written to the provider's server-side cache. cost float Cumulative monetary expenditure calculated in USD. unpriced_calls int Number of requests whose pricing was unavailable (cost is None). unmeasured_calls int Number of requests where the provider returned no usage metrics or unbilled declines. refusals int Count of request refusals encountered. fallbacks int Count of model fallback invocations triggered. truncations int Count of responses terminated due to token length limits. estimated_input int Cumulative input prompt tokens estimated before dispatch. cache_hits int Requests fulfilled by the local disk cache without contacting the provider.

docs.title: Public Summary Entry
docs.text:
The dictionary structure returned by get_usage_summary() and get_step_summary(), created by passing an internal ledger entry through _public().

Field Type Description models list[str] Alphabetically sorted list of model identifiers used during the run. calls int Total number of API requests dispatched. input int Total prompt tokens reported by the provider. output int Total completion tokens generated (including reasoning). thinking int Subset of output tokens dedicated to reasoning. cache_read int Tokens read from the server-side prompt cache. cache_write int Tokens written to the server-side prompt cache. cost float Cumulative monetary cost in USD. cost_known bool True if every call had known pricing (unpriced_calls == 0); False otherwise. unpriced_calls int Number of requests with unknown pricing. unmeasured_calls int Number of requests with unmeasured usage. refusals int Count of refusal events. fallbacks int Count of fallback events. truncations int Count of truncation events. estimated_input int Cumulative estimated input tokens. cache_hits int Requests served from the local disk cache.

The dictionary returned by usage_snapshot() and usage_delta(). Matches the Internal Ledger Entry schema exactly, but omits the models set field.

Field Type Description calls int Total calls or call delta. input int Prompt tokens or token delta. output int Output tokens or token delta. thinking int Reasoning tokens or token delta. cache_read int Cache-read tokens or token delta. cache_write int Cache-write tokens or token delta. cost float Cost in USD or cost delta. unpriced_calls int Unpriced calls or call delta. unmeasured_calls int Unmeasured calls or call delta. refusals int Refusals or refusal delta. fallbacks int Fallbacks or fallback delta. truncations int Truncations or truncation delta. estimated_input int Estimated input tokens or token delta. cache_hits int Cache hits or cache hit delta.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module defines the LLMRefusalError exception and provides truncation signaling through TruncatedResponse. These mechanisms manage provider rejection states across the application:

flowchart TD errorCheck["Evaluate Model Failure"] --> isRefusal{"Is Request Refused?"} subgraph SubgraphPolicy["Refusal Classification"] isRefusal -->|Yes| checkRetryable{"Is error.retryable True?"} checkRetryable -->|False| nonRetryable["Deterministic Policy Decline"] checkRetryable -->|True| retryable["Stochastic Generation Block"] nonRetryable --> saveMemo["remember_refusal(key, error)"] saveMemo --> haltRetries["Abort Node Retries for Key"] retryable --> allowRetry["Allow Node Retry to Re-sample"] end subgraph SubgraphTruncation["Truncation Signaling"] isRefusal -->|No| isTruncated{"Did Output Hit Max Tokens?"} isTruncated -->|Yes| wrapTruncated["Return TruncatedResponse(text)"] wrapTruncated --> bypassCache["Bypass Local Disk Cache"] bypassCache --> parserReject["Parser Rejects Incomplete Payload"] isTruncated -->|No| normalReturn["Return Plain Text Response"] end classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class errorCheck entryNode class checkRetryable entryNode class isTruncated entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: Deterministic vs. Retryable Refusals
docs.text:
When a provider rejects a prompt, the adapter wraps the rejection in an LLMRefusalError:

  • Deterministic Refusals (retryable=False): Occur when a prompt violates safety policies, system instructions, or content guardrails (e.g., Claude refusals, blocked prompt filters). The gateway invokes remember_refusal(key, error). Any subsequent attempt to execute that exact prompt under the same provider, model, and thinking level triggers an immediate short-circuit via previous_refusal(key), which re-raises the exception and bypasses network dispatch.
  • Retryable Refusals (retryable=True): Occur when output-side sampling triggers a block on candidate tokens (e.g., Gemini RECITATION or candidate safety triggers, OpenRouter content_filter). Because an alternative sampling path may succeed, these errors are not memoized in _refused, allowing node-level retries to re-dispatch the prompt with fresh random seeds or updated temperatures.

docs.title: In-Band Truncation Handling
docs.text: Rather than raising an exception when an LLM runs out of output tokens, providers return TruncatedResponse(text). This allows the calling orchestration layer to inspect the partial generation or log diagnostics. Because TruncatedResponse has truncated = True, cache storage logic avoids caching the incomplete response, and downstream structured data parsers (such as YAML and JSON parsers) fail validation on the incomplete syntax, prompting the workflow node to trigger a retry with expanded token headroom.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Following the foundational execution and telemetry contracts established in utils/llm_common.py, utils/llm_config.py acts as the centralized configuration, credential preflight, and model parameter resolution layer across all supported Large Language Model providers. The module was explicitly extracted from call_llm.py to break a circular import dependency between execution dispatching and tokenizer budgeting (call_llm ↔ token_utils). By consolidating provider settings, endpoint URLs, API keys, thinking budget profiles, context length querying, and token-ratio priors into a single source of truth, it provides a decoupled configuration foundation for downstream runtime systems.

The module manages multi-provider interoperability across Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and generic OpenAI-compatible gateways. It establishes deterministic parameter mappings for model capabilities, including adaptive thinking effort levels, token-ratio adjustments between tiktoken and Claude tokenizers, Vertex AI regional endpoint routing, and OpenRouter dynamic catalog inspection. To avoid runtime disruptions during heavy pipeline execution passes, utils/llm_config.py encapsulates early preflight authentication routines that validate local CLI credentials, Workload Identity Federation profiles, and SDK version compatibility before network requests are dispatched.

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash"
DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION = "global"  # Vertex: Gemini 3.x is served from global / us / eu, not us-central1
DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5"
DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_ENDPOINT = "https://api.anthropic.com"
DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api"

The default endpoints and model identifiers establish baseline connection targets when environment variables are omitted. DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION designates global as the default Vertex AI region because modern Gemini 3.x endpoints are served globally or across multi-regions rather than legacy zonal identifiers like us-central1.

OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT = {
    None: 64_000,
    "minimal": 32_000,
    "low": 32_000,
    "medium": 64_000,
    "high": 64_000,
    "xhigh": 96_000,
    "max": 128_000,
}
ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT = OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT  # Claude uses the shared table as-is
CONTEXT_MARGIN = 2_000
ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN = CONTEXT_MARGIN

Token allocation tables size the maximum planned output tokens across abstract reasoning efforts. The output reservations defined in OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT directly dictate upstream prompt packing thresholds in token_utils.input_token_budget, ensuring prompts never starve the model of generation headroom. CONTEXT_MARGIN provides a flat 2,000-token safety buffer between input prompts plus generation ceilings and the hard physical context boundary of the model.

ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES = (
    "claude-opus-5",
    "claude-sonnet-5",
    "claude-fable-",
    "claude-mythos-",
    "claude-opus-4-8",
    "claude-opus-4-7",
    "claude-opus-4-6",
    "claude-sonnet-4-6",
)
ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES = ("claude-opus-4-6", "claude-sonnet-4-6")  # 4.6 predates xhigh
ANTHROPIC_THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES = ("claude-opus-5", "claude-sonnet-5", "claude-fable-", "claude-mythos-")

Prefix tuples classify Claude models into behavioral generations. Models matching ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES support adaptive thinking via output_config.effort, while legacy models require explicit budget_tokens. ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES enforces backward compatibility by downscaling xhigh effort levels to high for the 4.6 family, and ANTHROPIC_THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES identifies next-generation models that think adaptively even when thinking flags are omitted.

CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_NEW_TOKENIZER = 1.55
CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_OLD_TOKENIZER = 1.2
TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS = (0.5, 3.0)
DEFAULT_CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO = CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_NEW_TOKENIZER

Static priors for token scaling factors. Because local context packing utilizes tiktoken (cl100k) which systematically undercounts Claude tokens—especially across dense source code—these ratios scale token estimations prior to live feedback calibration. The default ratio of 1.55 accounts for the Opus 4.7+ tokenizer expanding token counts by approximately 30% over earlier Claude tokenizers.

GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS = (
    ("gemini-3.8-flash", ("low", "medium", "high")),
    ("gemini-3.7-flash", ("low", "medium", "high")),
    ("gemini-3.6-flash", ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high")),
    ("gemini-3.5-flash", ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high")),  # also gemini-3.5-flash-lite
    ("gemini-3.1-pro", ("low", "medium", "high")),  # thinking cannot be turned off
    ("gemini-3.1-flash-lite", ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high")),
    ("gemini-3-pro", ("low", "medium", "high")),  # AI Studio serves 3.1 Pro under this retired id
    ("gemini-3-flash", ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high")),
)
GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS = ("low", "medium", "high")  # every documented 3.x text model accepts these
GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES = (
    ("gemini-2.5-flash-lite", 512, 24_576, True),
    ("gemini-2.5-flash", 1, 24_576, True),
    ("gemini-2.5-pro", 128, 32_768, False),
)
GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS = {"minimal": 512, "low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192, "xhigh": 16384, "max": 24576}
GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS = (1_048_576, 65_536)  # every Gemini 3.x / 2.5 text model: input, output
GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT = {None: 65_536, "minimal": 32_768, "low": 32_768, "medium": 65_536, "high": 65_536, "xhigh": 65_536, "max": 65_536}
GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS = {
    "gemini-3-pro-preview": ("gemini-3.1-pro-preview", True),  # AI Studio routes it to 3.1 Pro Preview
    "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview": ("gemini-3.1-flash-lite", False),
}
GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS = (
    ("gemini-3.8-flash-cyber", ("global", "us")),
    ("gemini-3.5-flash-lite", ("global", "us", "eu")),
    ("gemini-3.5-flash", None),
    ("gemini-3.1-pro", ("global",)),
    ("gemini-3-flash", ("global",)),
    ("gemini-3-pro", ("global",)),
)
GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS = ("global", "us", "eu")

Gemini family configuration structures. Gemini 3.x relies on discrete thinking levels (GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS), while Gemini 2.5 models require numerical budgets bounded by GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES. GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS defines the baseline 1,048,576 input and 65,536 output token thresholds, while GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS maps model families to their supported Vertex multi-region availability.

ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL = {"low": 2_048, "medium": 8_192, "high": 16_384, "xhigh": 24_576, "max": 32_000}
ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS = 16_000
ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS = ("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max")
GEMINI_MIN_SDK = (1, 56, 0)

Configuration structures for pre-adaptive Anthropic models and minimum SDK bounds. Pre-adaptive models (such as Haiku 4.5) map effort levels to fixed token counts defined in ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL and add ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS (16,000) to ensure adequate reply capacity. GEMINI_MIN_SDK marks the minimum google-genai package version (1.56.0) required to utilize discrete thinking levels without encountering client Pydantic validation errors.

docs.title: anthropic_output_cap()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:

Description: Retrieves the maximum allowed output tokens configured for Anthropic requests from the environment. It inspects the ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable, delegating parsing to _env_int().

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • int | None: The integer token ceiling parsed from the environment, or None if unset or invalid.

Example:

cap = anthropic_output_cap()
return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

This method is invoked internally by output budget calculators to allow user configuration to override hardcoded model ceilings. When set to a valid positive integer, the cap clamps planned output token allocations across all Anthropic requests.

docs.title: anthropic_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Resolves the planned output token allocation for adaptive Anthropic models based on the specified thinking level, applying the optional ceiling from anthropic_output_cap().

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): The requested abstract thinking effort ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", or None).

Returns:

  • int: Output token count allocated for the request.

Example:

def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-effort table value capped by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (adaptive models)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The function normalizes the thinking level string to lowercase and retrieves the mapped value from ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT. If thinking_level is None or not present in the table, it falls back to the default effort budget (64,000 tokens). Finally, if ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is defined, the budget is clamped to that ceiling.

docs.title: anthropic_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Normalizes and validates an abstract thinking level string into a supported Claude API effort parameter, adjusting for family-specific capabilities.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The name or identifier of the Anthropic model.
  • level (str | None): The desired thinking level string.

Returns:

  • str | None: The validated effort string ("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"), or None if disabled/unsupported.

Example:

def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Thinking level → effort the model accepts: minimal → low, xhigh → high on the 4.6 family,
    unknown values → None (model default)."""
    if not level:
        return None
    level = level.lower()
    if level == "minimal":
        level = "low"
    if level not in ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS:
        return None
    if level == "xhigh" and (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES):
        return "high"
    return level

The method standardizes input strings by converting them to lowercase and mapping "minimal" up to "low", as Anthropic APIs do not support a minimal tier. If the normalized value is not recognized in ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS, None is returned so the provider uses its default behavior. For models belonging to ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES (such as Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6), the effort is clamped from "xhigh" down to "high".

docs.title: anthropic_planned_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Calculates the total planned output token reservation (max_tokens) for Anthropic requests. It differentiates between adaptive thinking models and legacy fixed-budget models before factoring in user-configured environment caps.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Anthropic model identifier.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Target thinking effort level.

Returns:

  • int: Total output token reservation planned for the API request.

Example:

def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Claude max_tokens the request will plan for (before the model/context ceiling): the per-effort
    table on adaptive models, budget_tokens + 16K on pre-adaptive ones (Haiku 4.5), capped by
    ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_anthropic and token_utils.input_token_budget."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, thinking_level)
    if (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
        return anthropic_output_budget(effort)
    planned = ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL.get(effort, 0) + ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(planned, cap) if cap else planned

If the model matches ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES, the output budget is resolved directly via anthropic_output_budget(). For pre-adaptive architectures (such as Haiku 4.5), thinking budget tokens are explicitly looked up from ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL and added to ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS (16,000 tokens) to guarantee reply space. The computed total is clamped by anthropic_output_cap() if configured.

docs.title: gemini_thinking_mode()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:

Description: Determines the thinking configuration mode and parameter constraints for a given Gemini model identifier.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Gemini model identifier or full resource path.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, object]: A mode tuple categorizing thinking behavior:
    • ("budget", (min, max, can_disable)) for legacy Gemini 2.5 models.
    • ("level", allowed_levels) for modern Gemini 3.x models.
    • ("none", None) for unmapped, non-Gemini, or non-text models.

Example:

def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """('level', allowed_levels) for Gemini 3.x, ('budget', (min, max, can_disable)) for 2.5,
    ('none', None) for models without a thinking control the project maps."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, low, high, can_disable in GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "budget", (low, high, can_disable)
    if not name.startswith("gemini-") or name.startswith(("gemini-1", "gemini-2")):
        return "none", None  # 1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants (image, live, TTS) and non-Gemini ids
    for prefix, levels in GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "level", levels
    # Other 3.x ids, '-latest' aliases (gemini-flash-latest, gemini-pro-latest) and newer families:
    # the level set every documented 3.x model accepts (a model that rejects it is handled at runtime).
    return "level", GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS

The function normalizes the input model identifier using gemini_model_id() and iterates through GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES to identify budget-based models. If the model represents an older family (Gemini 1.x, 2.0) or non-text variant, thinking controls are disabled via ("none", None). For 3.x models, it matches against GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS or defaults to GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS for latest aliases and future revisions.

docs.title: gemini_model_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:

Description: Extracts the bare model identifier from a full Gemini API or Vertex AI resource path.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Full or partial model path (e.g., "models/gemini-3.8-flash" or "publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash").

Returns:

  • str: Normalized bare model identifier (e.g., "gemini-3.8-flash").

Example:

def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:
    """'models/gemini-3.8-flash' / 'publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash' → 'gemini-3.8-flash'."""
    return (model or "").strip().lower().rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

The implementation strips surrounding whitespace, converts the text to lowercase, and splits on forward slashes, selecting the terminal path component. This ensures consistent string prefix evaluations across both Google AI Studio and Google Cloud Vertex AI endpoint notations.

docs.title: gemini_vertex_locations()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:

Description: Resolves the allowed Vertex AI deployment locations that serve a specific Gemini 3.x model.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Gemini model identifier.

Returns:

  • tuple | None: A tuple of valid region strings (e.g., ("global", "us", "eu")), or None if the model can be served from any regional endpoint.

Example:

def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:
    """Vertex AI locations that serve a Gemini 3.x model (None = any, including regional endpoints)."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, locations in GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return locations
    return GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS if name.startswith("gemini-3") else None

The model identifier is extracted and compared against prefixes in GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS using longest-prefix matching. If matched, the associated location tuple (or None for unconstrained regional serving) is returned. Unlisted 3.x models default to GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS (("global", "us", "eu")), while non-3.x models return None.

docs.title: gemini_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:

Description: Computes the planned Gemini max_output_tokens parameter based on effort level, model-specific boundaries, and environment caps.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired thinking effort level.
  • output_limit (int | None): Optional hard model output limit (defaults to 65,536).

Returns:

  • int: The resolved output token budget for the request.

Example:

def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:
    """Planned Gemini max_output_tokens: per-level table, capped by the model output limit and
    GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_gemini (request) and token_utils (prompt budget)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    budget = min(budget, output_limit or GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1])
    cap = _env_int("GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The function looks up the target effort in GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT, defaulting to 65,536 tokens if omitted. It clamps the budget against the provided output_limit or GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1]. If the GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable is defined and positive, it applies that ceiling.

docs.title: openrouter_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Resolves planned maximum output tokens for models routed through OpenRouter, referencing catalog provider metadata and environment overrides.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target OpenRouter model identifier.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired thinking effort level.

Returns:

  • int | None: Resolved token reservation, or None if the model is unlisted in the catalog and no explicit environment cap is defined.

Example:

def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Planned OpenRouter max_tokens: shared per-effort table, capped by the catalog's
    top_provider.max_completion_tokens and OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. None when the model is not
    in the catalog (unknown limits, e.g. a non-OpenRouter proxy): max_tokens is then omitted."""
    info = openrouter_model_info(model)
    if info is None:
        return _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    model_cap = (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("max_completion_tokens")
    budget = min(budget, model_cap) if model_cap else min(budget, 32_000)
    cap = _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The function queries openrouter_model_info(). If catalog information is unavailable (such as with local proxies), it falls back strictly to OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (which may be None). Otherwise, it determines the budget from OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT, clamps it against max_completion_tokens from top_provider (or a 32,000-token ceiling if unset), and applies OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS if configured.

docs.title: context_output_reserve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Identifies how many output tokens must be reserved from the shared prompt context window for the currently active provider.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): The requested thinking effort level.

Returns:

  • int | None: Token count that must be subtracted from the prompt window budget, 0 if input/output windows are decoupled (Gemini), or None if the provider does not size output.

Example:

def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Output tokens that share the context window with the prompt, for the active provider.
    ANTHROPIC / OPENROUTER: the planned max_tokens (thinking included). GEMINI: 0 — Gemini's input and
    output limits are separate. None: the provider does not size output (5% reserve in token_utils)."""
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return anthropic_planned_output(model, thinking_level)
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return 0
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return openrouter_output_budget(model, thinking_level)
    return None

Under Anthropic and OpenRouter, generation tokens share the context window with prompt input, requiring planned generation limits to be subtracted from prompt budgets. Conversely, Google Gemini maintains fully decoupled input and output token buffers (1M/2M input vs 64K output), returning 0. For unmanaged providers, returning None prompts token_utils to apply a heuristic 5% reserve.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Resolves the active LLM provider identity from environment variables, enforcing explicit configuration rules and legacy fallbacks.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str | None: The resolved provider string in uppercase ("ANTHROPIC", "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER", or custom), or None if unconfigured.

Example:

def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:
    """Determine the LLM provider from environment variables.

    Explicit LLM_PROVIDER wins; otherwise Gemini credentials select GEMINI (legacy default).
    ANTHROPIC is never auto-selected: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is often exported globally for other
    tools (e.g. Claude Code), and a silent switch to a paid Claude run would be surprising.
    """
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        return provider.strip().upper()
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        return "GEMINI"
    return None

The function prioritizes an explicit LLM_PROVIDER environment variable. If absent, it checks for Gemini credentials (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY) and defaults to "GEMINI". It explicitly avoids auto-selecting "ANTHROPIC" even when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present, preventing unintentional billing incurred by ambient shell credentials exported for developer tools like Claude Code.

docs.title: resolve_llm_settings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_llm_settings() -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:

Description: Primary configuration orchestrator that resolves the active provider name, model identifier, API endpoint host, and API key into a single 4-element tuple.

docs.title: Phase 1: Provider Determination and Gemini Resolution
docs.text:
provider = get_llm_provider()
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            location = gemini_location().lower()
            if location == "global":
                host = "aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            elif location in ("us", "eu"):
                host = f"aiplatform.{location}.rep.googleapis.com"  # multi-region endpoints
            else:
                host = f"{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            return provider, model, host, ""
        return provider, model, "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")

In the first phase, get_llm_provider() determines the target backend. If Gemini is selected, the model is resolved from GEMINI_MODEL or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL. For Google Cloud Vertex AI configurations (indicated by GEMINI_PROJECT_ID), the host endpoint is dynamically mapped: global maps to aiplatform.googleapis.com, multi-regions us and eu map to replicated endpoints (aiplatform.{location}.rep.googleapis.com), and regional deployments use {location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com. Because Vertex AI utilizes ambient Google Cloud credentials, the returned API key string is empty. For Google AI Studio, the host is set to generativelanguage.googleapis.com alongside GEMINI_API_KEY.

docs.title: Phase 2: Anthropic, OpenRouter, and Generic Fallbacks
docs.text:
if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        endpoint = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_ENDPOINT
        return provider, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_MODEL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL, endpoint, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "")
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return provider, os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "unknown"), openrouter_base_url(), os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")
    if provider:
        return (
            provider,
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_API_KEY", ""),
        )
    return "UNKNOWN", "unknown", "unknown", ""

In the second phase, Anthropic resolves its endpoint from ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (defaulting to https://api.anthropic.com), its model from ANTHROPIC_MODEL (defaulting to claude-sonnet-5), and its API key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. OpenRouter sources OPENROUTER_MODEL, openrouter_base_url(), and OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Any custom provider string dynamically reads {PROVIDER}_MODEL, {PROVIDER}_BASE_URL, and {PROVIDER}_API_KEY. If no provider can be identified, fallback sentinel strings ("UNKNOWN") are returned.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, str, str, str]: Tuple representing (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key).

docs.text:

Signature: def rejects_sampling_params(model_name: str) -> bool:

Description: Identifies models that reject or deprecate standard sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, top_k), triggering 400 Bad Request errors.

Parameters:

Returns:

Example:

def rejects_sampling_params(model_name: str) -> bool:
    """True for models that reject or ignore temperature/top_p/top_k: Claude Opus 4.7+, Opus/Sonnet 5,
    Fable, Mythos (400), and Gemini 3.x (deprecated; ignored or erroring on some endpoints)."""
    name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    return _normalize_claude_id(name).startswith(_NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES) or "gemini-3" in name.lower()

The model identifier is resolved via OpenRouter catalog aliases (_catalog_model_id) and normalized. It tests whether the model matches _NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES (e.g., Opus 4.7+, Claude 5 series, Fable, Mythos) or contains "gemini-3". Downstream callers inspect this return value to omit sampling flags from request payloads.

docs.title: get_token_ratio()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_token_ratio() -> float:

Description: Computes the static prior multiplier used to convert raw tiktoken (cl100k) token estimates to the active model's native tokenizer.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • float: Multiplier clamped within TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS (0.5 to 3.0).

Example:

def get_token_ratio() -> float:
    provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    model_name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    if is_claude_model(provider, model_name):
        claude_id = _normalize_claude_id(model_name)  # also handles gateway ids on the native provider
        default = CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_NEW_TOKENIZER if claude_id.startswith(_NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES) else CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_OLD_TOKENIZER
        return max(_ratio_from_env("ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO", default), 1.0)
    if is_gemini_model(provider, model_name):
        return _ratio_from_env("GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)
    return _ratio_from_env("LLM_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)

For Claude models, the function differentiates between modern tokenizers (_NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES, default 1.55) and older tokenizers (default 1.2), checking ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO with a lower clamp of 1.0. For Gemini and other architectures, it evaluates GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO and LLM_TOKEN_RATIO (defaulting to 1.0).
