docs.title: openrouter_catalog()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_catalog() -> list | None:

Description: Fetches and caches the OpenRouter models catalog via HTTP GET, enforcing failure cooldown intervals and error suppression.

docs.title: Phase 1: Cache and Cooldown Validation
docs.text:
global _openrouter_models_cache, _openrouter_last_failure
    if _openrouter_models_cache is not None:
        return _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_last_failure and time.time() - _openrouter_last_failure < _OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN:
        return None

The first phase checks the in-memory singleton _openrouter_models_cache. If empty, it inspects the timestamp _openrouter_last_failure. If an HTTP error or parsing failure occurred within the last 60 seconds (_OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN), the function immediately aborts network dispatch and returns None, shielding startup routines from repeated network timeouts.

docs.title: Phase 2: Remote Catalog Fetch and Error Suppression
docs.text:
url = f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/models"
    try:
        resp = requests.get(url, timeout=20)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json().get("data")
        if not isinstance(data, list):
            raise ValueError("OpenRouter model catalog response has no 'data' list")
        _openrouter_models_cache = data
        return data
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.llm_common import warn_once
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        _openrouter_last_failure = time.time()
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Failed to fetch OpenRouter model info from {url}: {e}", dest="LOG")
        if warn_once("openrouter_catalog_unavailable"):
            emit("WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE", url=url, error=str(e)[:200])
        return None

The second phase performs an HTTP GET request to {openrouter_base_url()}/v1/models with a 20-second timeout. The JSON response is inspected to verify that the top-level "data" key contains a list. Upon success, the list is cached in _openrouter_models_cache. If an exception occurs, the failure timestamp is recorded, a warning is logged to the debug log, and a user-facing warning is emitted once via warn_once("openrouter_catalog_unavailable").

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • list | None: A list of model specification dictionaries, or None if the fetch failed or is cooling down.

docs.title: openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Locates a model's specification dictionary in the OpenRouter catalog using exact IDs, routing suffixes, dated slugs, or alias targets.

docs.title: Phase 1: Candidate Generation and Exact Match
docs.text:
catalog = openrouter_catalog()
    if not catalog or not model_id:
        return None
    wanted = model_id.strip()
    candidates = [wanted, *(wanted[: -len(suffix)] for suffix in _OPENROUTER_ROUTING_SUFFIXES if wanted.endswith(suffix))]
    for name in candidates:
        entry = next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == name or m.get("canonical_slug") == name), None)

The function retrieves the catalog and builds a list of candidate strings. If the requested model_id terminates in an OpenRouter routing suffix (:nitro, :floor, :online, :thinking, :extended, :exacto), candidate variants stripping that suffix are appended. It searches the catalog for an item matching either id or canonical_slug.

docs.title: Phase 2: Regex Dated Slug and Alias Target Resolution
docs.text:
if entry is None:
            # Dated canonical slug only ('anthropic/claude-4.6-opus' → '…-20260205'): a looser prefix
            # match would map typos such as 'google/gemini-3.1-pro' onto a different model.
            dated = re.compile(re.escape(name) + r"-\d{8}")
            entry = next((m for m in catalog if dated.fullmatch(str(m.get("canonical_slug", "")))), None)
        if entry is not None:
            target = (entry.get("alias_target") or {}).get("slug")
            if target and target != entry.get("id"):
                return next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == target or m.get("canonical_slug") == target), entry)
            return entry
    return None

If an exact candidate match is not found, the second phase tests for dated release slugs using regular expressions (name-\d{8}). This maps base model references (e.g. anthropic/claude-4.6-opus) to dated catalog targets (e.g. anthropic/claude-4.6-opus-20260205) while avoiding incorrect prefix matches. Once an entry is identified, alias redirection is resolved by inspecting alias_target.slug.

Parameters:

  • model_id (str): Target OpenRouter model identifier or slug.

Returns:

  • dict | None: Catalog model specification dictionary, or None if unresolvable.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Discovers the maximum input context window size for a given model and endpoint.

docs.title: Phase 1: Provider-Specific Limit Inspection
docs.text:
default_limit = 100000
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    try:
        if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
            from utils.llm_anthropic import get_model_limits

            return get_model_limits(model_name)[0]

        if provider == "OPENROUTER" or "openrouter.ai" in (endpoint_url or ""):
            info = openrouter_model_info(model_name)
            if info:
                return (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or info.get("context_length") or default_limit
            return default_limit

        if provider == "GEMINI":
            try:
                from utils.llm_gemini import get_model_limits as gemini_limits
            except ImportError:
                return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
            return gemini_limits(model_name)[0]

In the first phase, if the provider is "ANTHROPIC", it lazily imports get_model_limits from utils.llm_anthropic. For OpenRouter or endpoints matching "openrouter.ai", context limits are extracted from the catalog's top_provider.context_length or base context_length. For Gemini, it attempts to load limits via utils.llm_gemini, falling back to GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0] (1,048,576 tokens) if the SDK is missing.

docs.title: Phase 2: Endpoint Pattern Fallbacks and Error Handling
docs.text:
if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit
        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("WARN_CONTEXT_LENGTH_FETCH", model=model_name, endpoint=endpoint_url, error=str(e))

    return default_limit

In the second phase, generic endpoints are analyzed. If the URL points to generativelanguage.googleapis.com or the model name contains "gemini", it applies GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]. If any exception occurs during limit inspection, an operational telemetry warning is emitted and the function falls back to a safe default of 100,000 tokens.

Parameters:

  • endpoint_url (str): Target API endpoint URL.
  • model_name (str): Model identifier.
  • api_key (str, optional): API key string. Defaults to "".

Returns:

  • int: Context length in tokens.

docs.title: describe_thinking_support()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:

Description: Formats a single-line summary string describing how thinking/reasoning parameters are applied to the active model for UI console display.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Active provider identifier.
  • model (str): Target model name.

Returns:

  • str: Human-readable summary description.

Example:

def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:
    """One-line description of how thinking levels are applied for the startup display."""
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        name = (model or "").lower()
        if not name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
            return "thinking.budget_tokens (low…max → 2,048…32,000)"
        levels = "low, medium, high, max" if name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES) else "low, medium, high, xhigh, max"
        return f"adaptive thinking + output_config.effort ∈ {{{levels}}}"
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
        if mode == "level":
            return f"thinking_level ∈ {{{', '.join(spec)}}}"
        if mode == "budget":
            low, high, can_disable = spec
            return f"thinking_budget {low:,}-{high:,}" + (f" ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_BUDGET_OFF')})" if can_disable else "")
        return "—"
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        info = openrouter_model_info(model)
        if info is None:
            return f"reasoning.effort ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE')})" if not openrouter_catalog() else "—"
        reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
        if not isinstance(reasoning, dict):
            return "reasoning.effort" if "reasoning" in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []) else "—"
        efforts = reasoning.get("supported_efforts")
        if "supported_efforts" not in reasoning and reasoning.get("supports_max_tokens"):
            text = "reasoning.max_tokens (minimal…max → 1,024…32,000)"  # llm_openrouter._REASONING_BUDGETS
        elif efforts:
            text = f"reasoning.effort ∈ {{{', '.join(e for e in efforts if e != 'none')}}}"
        else:
            text = "reasoning.effort"
        extras = [_ui("CFG_THINKING_DEFAULT_EFFORT", effort=reasoning["default_effort"])] if reasoning.get("default_effort") else []
        if reasoning.get("mandatory"):
            extras.append(_ui("CFG_THINKING_MANDATORY"))
        return text + (f" · {' · '.join(extras)}" if extras else "")
    return "—"

For Anthropic, the function differentiates adaptive effort sets (low, medium, high, max) from legacy token budget ranges (2,048…32,000). For Gemini, it displays accepted discrete levels or formatted numeric budget bounds. For OpenRouter, it inspects catalog metadata to describe supported effort sets, token budgets, default effort levels, or mandatory reasoning constraints.

  • tuple[str | None, str | None]: A tuple containing (credential, workspace).

Example:

def parse_ant_auth_status(output: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    section, credential, workspace = None, None, None
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if not line[0].isspace():
            header = line.strip().lower()
            section = header if header in ("credentials", "workspace") else None
            continue
        if "(active)" not in line:
            continue
        text = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", _redact(re.sub(r"^\s*\(active\)\s*\*?\s*", "", line))).strip()
        if section == "workspace":
            workspace = workspace or text
        else:
            credential = credential or text
    return credential, workspace

Because ant auth status exit codes do not indicate authentication state, this function parses stdout/stderr lines. It identifies top-level section headers (Credentials, Workspace), searches for lines marked (active), redacts sensitive token strings via _redact(), and strips leading bullets to extract clean descriptor strings.

docs.title: check_anthropic_auth()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_anthropic_auth() -> bool:

Description: Executes comprehensive credential and SDK preflight verification for LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC, guiding the user through login options if credentials are missing.

docs.title: Phase 1: SDK Installation and Direct Credential Evaluation
docs.text:
from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

    if get_llm_provider() != "ANTHROPIC":
        return True
    if not _anthropic_sdk_installed():
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING")
        return False

    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") and _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_KEY_AND_TOKEN")
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        return True
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN")
        return True
    if all(_env_set(v) for v in _FEDERATION_VARS) and (_env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE") or _env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN")):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="Workload Identity Federation")
        return True

The first phase checks whether anthropic is installed via _anthropic_sdk_installed(). It then verifies environment credentials in prioritized order: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, and Workload Identity Federation variables (_FEDERATION_VARS combined with identity token files or values). If both an API key and auth token are present, a warning is emitted before accepting the credentials.

docs.title: Phase 2: CLI Binary Verification and Profile Status Execution
docs.text:
# No key: the SDK falls back to an `ant auth login` profile. Verify one is active.
    ant = shutil.which("ant")
    if not ant:
        stored = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(_anthropic_config_dir(), "credentials", "*.json")))
        if stored:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND", path=stored[0])
            return True
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS")
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=False)
        return False

    # Run with the same environment the SDK will see; empty key variables are dropped so the
    # CLI reports the profile the SDK will actually use (the SDK treats empty as unset).
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not (k in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN") and not v.strip())}
    try:
        result = subprocess.run([ant, "auth", "status"], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=30, env=env)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED", error=str(e))
        return True

    output = f"{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}"
    credential, workspace = parse_ant_auth_status(output)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ant auth status | exit={result.returncode}\n{_redact(output).strip()}", dest="LOG")
    if not credential:
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN")
        details = _redact(output).strip()
        if details:
            emit_raw("INFO", "\n".join(f"    {line}" for line in details.splitlines()))
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=True)
        return False

    source = _ui("AUTH_SOURCE_ANT_LOGIN", credential=credential)
    if workspace:
        source += f" | {_ui('AUTH_SOURCE_WORKSPACE', workspace=workspace)}"
    emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source=source)
    return True

If no direct credentials exist, the SDK requires an active profile from the ant CLI tool. If the CLI binary is absent, it inspects _anthropic_config_dir() for stored credential JSON files. If ant is found, it executes ant auth status within a sanitized environment that strips empty API key strings. The output is parsed using parse_ant_auth_status(). If no active profile is detected, setup guidance is output via _emit_auth_help().

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if valid authentication was verified; False otherwise.

docs.title: check_gemini_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_gemini_config() -> bool:

Description: Validates SDK installation, SDK version constraints, model retirement status, and authentication credentials for Gemini configurations.

docs.title: Phase 1: SDK Version and Model Deprecation Validation
docs.text:
model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
    version = _installed_version("google-genai")
    if version is None:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_MISSING")
        return False
    if version < GEMINI_MIN_SDK:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_OUTDATED", version=".".join(map(str, version)), required=".".join(map(str, GEMINI_MIN_SDK)))
        return False

    retired = GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS.get(gemini_model_id(model))
    if retired:
        replacement, aliased_on_ai_studio = retired
        if aliased_on_ai_studio and not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
        else:
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
            return False

The first phase checks that google-genai is installed and meets GEMINI_MIN_SDK (1.56.0). It then checks the model against GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS. If the model is retired, it emits a warning if Google AI Studio aliases it transparently, or raises an error and halts execution if running under Vertex AI where the endpoint is deprecated.

docs.title: Phase 2: Vertex AI vs AI Studio Credential Verification
docs.text:
if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        location = gemini_location()
        allowed = gemini_vertex_locations(model)
        if allowed is not None and location.lower() not in allowed:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_LOCATION", location=location, model=model, allowed=", ".join(allowed))
        try:
            import google.auth

            google.auth.default()
        except Exception as e:  # DefaultCredentialsError, or google-auth missing
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS", error=str(e).splitlines()[0][:200])
            return False
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_VERTEX", project=os.environ["GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"], location=location))
        return True
    if _env_set("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_AI_STUDIO"))
        return True
    emit("ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS")
    return False

The second phase evaluates provider-specific authentication. If GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is present, it validates GEMINI_LOCATION against gemini_vertex_locations() and tests Application Default Credentials via google.auth.default(). If Vertex parameters are absent, it checks for GEMINI_API_KEY. If neither credential exists, an error is emitted.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if configuration and credentials are valid; False otherwise.

docs.title: check_openrouter_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_openrouter_config() -> bool:

Description: Performs preflight validation for LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER, verifying API keys, model variables, and catalog registration.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if OpenRouter configuration passes preflight checks; False otherwise.

Example:

def check_openrouter_config() -> bool:
    """Preflight for LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER."""
    from utils.output import emit

    if not _env_set("OPENROUTER_API_KEY") and is_openrouter_host():
        emit("ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_KEY")
        return False
    model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "").strip()
    if not model:
        emit("ERROR_OPENROUTER_NO_MODEL")
        return False
    if openrouter_catalog() and openrouter_model_info(model) is None:
        emit("WARN_OPENROUTER_MODEL_UNKNOWN", model=model)
    emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="OpenRouter", source=f"OPENROUTER_API_KEY | {model} | {openrouter_base_url()}")
    return True

The function checks for OPENROUTER_API_KEY when targeting the official host (is_openrouter_host()). It ensures OPENROUTER_MODEL is populated, and if the catalog is reachable, checks whether the configured model is listed, emitting WARN_OPENROUTER_MODEL_UNKNOWN if unresolvable.

docs.title: check_llm_auth()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_llm_auth() -> bool:

Description: Top-level dispatcher that executes credential and environment preflight verification for the currently active provider before pipeline initialization.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the active provider passes preflight validation; False otherwise.

Example:

def check_llm_auth() -> bool:
    """Credential/SDK preflight for the active provider, run before any LLM call by main() and the
    utils/call_llm.py self-test. Prints setup instructions and returns False when the run cannot work."""
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return check_anthropic_auth()
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return check_gemini_config()
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return check_openrouter_config()
    return True

The dispatcher queries get_llm_provider() and routes execution to check_anthropic_auth(), check_gemini_config(), or check_openrouter_config(). For generic or unrecognized providers, it passes preflight by returning True.

docs.title: Constants and Variables
docs.text:
_NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES = ("claude-opus-4-7", "claude-opus-4-8", "claude-opus-5", "claude-sonnet-5", "claude-fable", "claude-mythos")
_NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES = ("claude-opus-4-7", "claude-opus-4-8", "claude-opus-5", "claude-sonnet-5", "claude-fable", "claude-mythos")
_CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST = re.compile(r"claude-(\d+)(?:-(\d+))?-(opus|sonnet|haiku|fable|mythos)")
_openrouter_models_cache = None
_openrouter_last_failure = 0.0
_OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN = 60.0
_OPENROUTER_ROUTING_SUFFIXES = (":nitro", ":floor", ":online", ":thinking", ":extended", ":exacto")
_get_openrouter_model_info = openrouter_model_info  # backward-compatible name
_FEDERATION_VARS = ("ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID", "ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID", "ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID")
_TOKEN_PATTERN = re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*(?:\.\.\.)?")

Internal module constants and operational states. _NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES identifies models that return 400 errors when sampling parameters are passed. _NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES designates Claude families that use the newer tokenizer requiring a 1.55 token ratio prior. _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST provides a compiled regular expression for normalizing non-standard Claude identifiers. _openrouter_models_cache and _openrouter_last_failure manage the OpenRouter catalog cache and failure backoff timer. _FEDERATION_VARS defines required Google Cloud/AWS Workload Identity Federation environment variables, and _TOKEN_PATTERN matches API token prefixes for sanitizing console and log output.

docs.title: _env_int()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _env_int(name: str) -> int | None:

Description: Safely parses a positive integer from a specified environment variable.

Parameters:

  • name (str): Environment variable key name.

Returns:

  • int | None: Parsed positive integer, or None if the variable is unset, empty, non-digit, or less than or equal to zero.

Example:

def _env_int(name: str) -> int | None:
    value = os.getenv(name, "").strip()
    return int(value) if value.isdigit() and int(value) > 0 else None

The function reads the specified environment variable, strips whitespace, verifies digits via isdigit(), and confirms the value is positive before casting it to an integer.

docs.title: _normalize_claude_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes heterogeneous Claude identifiers (such as AWS Bedrock resource paths or reversed version strings) into canonical family-first slugs.

Parameters:

  • model_name (str): Raw model identifier or path.

Returns:

  • str: Canonical normalized identifier (e.g., "claude-opus-4-7").

Example:

def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:
    """Gateway/cloud IDs → bare family-first Claude ID: 'anthropic/claude-opus-4.7',
    'bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1:0' and the version-first alias
    'anthropic/claude-4.7-opus-20260416' all → 'claude-opus-4-7...'."""
    name = (model_name or "").lower().replace(".", "-")
    start = name.find("claude-")
    name = name[start:] if start >= 0 else name
    match = _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST.match(name)
    if match:
        major, minor, family = match.groups()
        name = f"claude-{family}-{major}" + (f"-{minor}" if minor else "") + name[match.end() :]
    return name

The function replaces periods with hyphens, extracts the substring starting at "claude-", and applies the _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST regex. If an identifier uses version-first ordering (e.g., claude-4.7-opus), it rewrites the token order to family-first (claude-opus-4-7).

docs.title: _catalog_model_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _catalog_model_id(model_name: str) -> str:

Description: Resolves OpenRouter model aliases against the model catalog to expose the underlying canonical model ID for capability detection.

Parameters:

  • model_name (str): Target model name or alias.

Returns:

  • str: Canonical target model identifier from the catalog, or the original string if not running on OpenRouter.

Example:

def _catalog_model_id(model_name: str) -> str:
    """On OPENROUTER, resolve aliases ('~anthropic/claude-opus-latest', canonical slugs) through the
    catalog so family checks see the real model; other providers use the name as given."""
    if get_llm_provider() == "OPENROUTER":
        info = openrouter_model_info(model_name)
        if info and info.get("id"):
            return info["id"]
    return model_name or ""

When get_llm_provider() is "OPENROUTER", this helper queries openrouter_model_info(). If the entry contains a primary id, that ID is returned so capability checks evaluate the underlying model.

docs.title: _ratio_from_env()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:

Description: Safely parses a float ratio from an environment variable, clamping the result within TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS.

Parameters:

  • name (str): Environment variable name.
  • default (float): Fallback default ratio if missing or unparsable.

Returns:

  • float: Validated ratio bounded between 0.5 and 3.0.

Example:

def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """Float env ratio clamped to TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS; unparsable / non-finite values use the default."""
    try:
        ratio = float(os.getenv(name, default))
    except ValueError:
        ratio = default
    if not math.isfinite(ratio):
        ratio = default
    low, high = TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS
    return min(max(ratio, low), high)

The function attempts to cast the environment variable to a float. If a ValueError occurs or the parsed float is non-finite (NaN or infinite), default is used. The resulting value is clamped to TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS ((0.5, 3.0)).

docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _anthropic_sdk_installed() -> bool:

Description: Determines if the official anthropic Python SDK is available in the current Python environment without importing it.

None.

def _anthropic_sdk_installed() -> bool:
    try:
        return importlib.util.find_spec("anthropic") is not None
    except (ImportError, ValueError):  # ValueError: module already imported without a spec
        return "anthropic" in sys.modules

The function uses importlib.util.find_spec("anthropic") to test module availability without executing package initialization code, avoiding circular dependencies and side effects during preflight verification.

docs.title: _anthropic_config_dir()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _anthropic_config_dir() -> str:

Description: Resolves the local configuration directory where Anthropic CLI profiles are stored.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str: Filesystem path to the Anthropic configuration directory.

Example:

def _anthropic_config_dir() -> str:
    """Directory where `ant auth login` stores profiles (ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR or the OS default)."""
    if os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR"):
        return os.environ["ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR"]
    if os.name == "nt":
        return os.path.join(os.getenv("APPDATA", os.path.expanduser("~")), "Anthropic")
    return os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".config", "anthropic")

Checks ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR first. If unset, it resolves %APPDATA%\Anthropic on Windows or ~/.config/anthropic on Unix systems.

def _emit_auth_help(ant_installed: bool) -> None:

docs.title: _installed_version()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _installed_version(dist: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:

Description: Inspects installed package distributions to parse semantic version numbers into integer comparison tuples.

Parameters:

  • dist (str): Package distribution name (e.g., "google-genai").

Returns:

  • tuple[int, ...] | None: Up to a 3-integer version tuple (e.g., (1, 56, 0)), or None if uninstalled.

Example:

def _installed_version(dist: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
    from importlib import metadata

    try:
        raw = metadata.version(dist)
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        return None
    parts = []
    for piece in raw.split(".")[:3]:
        digits = re.match(r"\d+", piece)
        parts.append(int(digits.group()) if digits else 0)
    return tuple(parts)

The helper calls importlib.metadata.version(). If installed, it splits the version string on periods and parses the first three numeric components into integers for version comparison operations.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive validation patterns to catch configuration and runtime issues before downstream inference runs:

  • OpenRouter Catalog Fetch Fault Tolerance: When querying {openrouter_base_url()}/v1/models, network exceptions (requests.RequestException), HTTP errors (raise_for_status()), or invalid JSON structures raise exceptions internally. openrouter_catalog() catches these errors, logs a warning via emit_raw, records the timestamp in _openrouter_last_failure, and surfaces a deduplicated warning via warn_once("openrouter_catalog_unavailable"). Calls during the 60-second _OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN window return None immediately, preventing cascading startup timeouts.
  • SDK Version and Dependency Validation: check_gemini_config() and check_anthropic_auth() verify that required packages are installed and meet version constraints before execution begins. If google-genai is older than GEMINI_MIN_SDK (1.56.0), the pipeline halts and reports the installed vs. required version strings.
  • Environment Variable Type Safety: Numeric parsing helpers _env_int() and _ratio_from_env() handle malformed or non-numeric environment values safely. _ratio_from_env() catches ValueError, validates that the result is finite via math.isfinite(), and clamps it to TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS (0.5 to 3.0).
  • Subprocess Error Isolation: When invoking ant auth status to check Anthropic authentication profiles, subprocess execution is bounded by a 30-second timeout. Any OSError or subprocess.SubprocessError is captured and logged as WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED, allowing pipeline execution to continue if credentials can be resolved through another mechanism.

docs.text: Source: utils/llm_gemini.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the runtime parameters, quota boundaries, and authentication preflights established in utils/llm_config.py, this module serves as the dedicated Google Gemini provider adapter for the codebase's centralized inference gateway. It encapsulates all direct interactions with the google-genai SDK, isolating external Google Cloud and AI Studio dependencies from downstream workflow nodes. The module manages runtime execution across both Google AI Studio (authenticated via GEMINI_API_KEY) and Google Cloud Vertex AI (authenticated via GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and regional location settings), dynamically selecting transport configurations based on environment variables.

The core execution path is designed around resilient chunked streaming through generate_content_stream. Because Google Gemini imposes a total per-request stream deadline rather than an idle read timeout, the module calculates and applies per-request deadlines (defaulting to 1,800 seconds) via SDK-level HTTP options, with automated retries for transient status codes (408, 429, 5xx). Furthermore, it features dynamic reasoning configuration: Gemini 3.x models consume reasoning levels clamped to valid model capabilities, whereas Gemini 2.5 models receive token budgets. If a model rejects thinking configuration headers with an HTTP 400 Client Error, the module dynamically records the rejection and replays the stream without thinking parameters.

The module provides rigorous post-stream telemetry, accounting, and completion categorization. Token consumption across prompts, candidate outputs, thoughts, and cached inputs is tracked against multi-tier pricing schedules that support introductory discounts, long-context surcharges (prompts exceeding 200,000 tokens), and Vertex regional pricing uplifts. Candidate finish reasons and prompt feedback blocks are evaluated to raise structured LLMRefusalError exceptions—differentiating stochastic, retryable candidate blocks (such as SAFETY or RECITATION) from deterministic prompt violations (such as PROHIBITED_CONTENT or BLOCKLIST). Responses truncated by output token limits return TruncatedResponse instances to guarantee that incomplete outputs bypass persistent disk caches.

docs.title: call_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches a single-turn completion prompt to the configured Google Gemini model over a chunked streaming transport. It orchestrates preflight sizing, thinking parameter validation, client invocation, dynamic fallback recovery, usage telemetry recording, and finish reason validation.

docs.title: Phase 1: Preflight Configuration and Prompt Sizing
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw

    model = get_model()
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
    max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)
    thinking, level_desc = _thinking_config(model, thinking_level)
    # No tools are passed, so automatic function calling is off (google-genai warns on streams otherwise).
    no_afc = types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True)
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=thinking, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Gemini request | model={model} | {level_desc} | max_output_tokens={max_output:,} | location={gemini_location() if os.getenv('GEMINI_PROJECT_ID') else 'ai-studio'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

In the initial configuration phase, the target model identifier is resolved via get_model(), and the raw prompt is tokenized using count_tokens_raw() to establish baseline token metrics. The maximum allowable output tokens are resolved based on model ceilings and requested thinking levels via _max_output_tokens(). The reasoning parameters are assembled into a types.ThinkingConfig instance via _thinking_config(). Finally, automatic function calling is explicitly disabled through types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True) to prevent the SDK from issuing console warnings during streaming when no tools are declared.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution and Fallback Recovery
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    try:
        result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
    except genai_errors.ClientError as e:
        # A model that rejects our thinking control (unknown future model, level set changed):
        # warn once and resend without it for the rest of the run.
        if getattr(e, "code", None) == 400 and thinking is not None and "think" in str(e).lower():
            _thinking_rejected.add(model)
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
            config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=None, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
            result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
        else:
            raise
    elapsed = time.time() - start

The execution phase dispatches the streaming request via _stream() inside a monitored execution block. If Google Gemini returns an HTTP 400 ClientError indicating that the target model does not support the supplied thinking configuration parameters, the handler intercepts the exception. It logs a warning via WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED, adds the model identifier to the module-level _thinking_rejected set to prevent future attempts during the run, constructs a new GenerateContentConfig omitting thinking_config, and replays the request. Any unhandled or non-thinking 400 errors are re-raised immediately.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry and Cost Recording
docs.text:
if result["usage"] is not None:
        _record(model, result["usage"], raw_tokens, level_desc, result["finish"], elapsed)
    else:
        record_usage("GEMINI", model, cost=None, measured=False)  # stream carried no usage_metadata
    if is_debug() and result["thoughts"]:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{result['thoughts']}", dest="LOG")

Once the stream terminates, post-flight telemetry processing evaluates the accumulated usage_metadata. If usage metrics are present on the stream payload, _record() extracts prompt, candidate, thinking, and cached token totals, determines monetary cost against pricing tables, updates global usage ledgers, and logs execution benchmarks. If usage metadata was omitted by the API, record_usage() records an unmeasured event. In addition, when debug mode is enabled via is_debug(), accumulated internal thinking summaries are emitted to the debug log stream.

docs.title: Phase 4: Block, Refusal, and Truncation Post-Processing
docs.text:
if result["block_reason"] or result["finish"] in _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS:
        category = result["block_reason"] or result["finish"]
        # A blocked prompt repeats for the same input; a stop on the candidate may pass on resampling.
        retryable = not result["block_reason"] and result["finish"] in _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS
        count_event("GEMINI", "refusals")
        emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="Gemini", model=model, category=category)
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="GEMINI", retryable=retryable)
    if result["finish"] in _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS:
        count_event("GEMINI", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="Gemini", max_tokens=f"{max_output:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
    if not result["text"]:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Gemini response contained no text (finish_reason={result['finish'] or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
    return result["text"]

The final phase inspects response stop conditions. If the request triggered an upstream block (via prompt_feedback.block_reason) or the candidate finish reason belongs to _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS, the module registers a refusal event. It flags candidate sampling stops (e.g., SAFETY, RECITATION) as retryable=True while treating prompt-level violations as permanent (retryable=False), raising an LLMRefusalError. If the candidate was stopped due to token budget exhaustion (MAX_TOKENS), the text is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse to prevent caching. Otherwise, the generated completion text is returned to the caller.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The input prompt string to be evaluated by the model.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Optional reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high") or token budget string. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The decoded text completion, or a TruncatedResponse instance if the generation was terminated by maximum token ceilings.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: When prompt feedback or candidate finish reasons indicate content policy violations, safety blocks, or recitation filters.
  • genai_errors.ClientError: When non-thinking 4xx API errors occur during transport.
  • ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is set in the runtime environment.

Example:

# Actual call site from utils/call_llm.py dispatching to Gemini
response = call_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the maximum context input limit and maximum output token limit for a designated Gemini model. When connected via AI Studio (without GEMINI_PROJECT_ID), the limits are dynamically queried from the Gemini API via client.models.get() and cached in _model_limits_cache. When running on Vertex AI or if API lookup fails, it falls back to the static boundaries defined in GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS.

def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(input_token_limit, output_token_limit). AI Studio reports them via models.get; Vertex does
    not (the SDK maps no limits there), so the static Gemini 3.x / 2.5 table applies."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    limits = GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS
    if not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        try:
            info = _get_client().models.get(model=model)
            limits = (getattr(info, "input_token_limit", None) or limits[0], getattr(info, "output_token_limit", None) or limits[1])
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Gemini models.get | model={model} | input={limits[0]:,} | output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
        except Exception as e:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits

The function checks the module-level dictionary _model_limits_cache to bypass repeated network queries. If uncached, it establishes defaults from GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS (typically (1_048_576, 65_536)). If Vertex AI is not in use, it invokes _get_client().models.get(model=model) to inspect remote metadata. Any network or lookup failures trigger a WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP warning and default boundaries are safely preserved.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The normalized model identifier string.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A two-element tuple containing (input_token_limit, output_token_limit).

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

# Call site within _max_output_tokens()
_input_limit, output_limit = get_model_limits(model)
return gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit)

docs.title: _timeout_ms()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _timeout_ms() -> int:

Description: Computes the total request deadline in milliseconds from the GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable. The value represents the deadline for the entire streamed response rather than an idle read timeout. It enforces a lower bound of 30.0 seconds and defaults to 1,800.0 seconds if parsing fails or the variable is omitted.

def _timeout_ms() -> int:
    """Total per-request deadline (the SDK applies it to the whole streamed response)."""
    try:
        seconds = float(os.getenv("GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "1800"))
    except ValueError:
        seconds = 1800.0
    return int(max(seconds, 30.0) * 1000)

The implementation reads GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, safely handling non-numeric configurations by reverting to 1,800.0 seconds. It calculates milliseconds using int(max(seconds, 30.0) * 1000), ensuring that connections do not hang indefinitely while preventing aggressive timeouts during extended reasoning phases.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • int: The request timeout deadline in milliseconds.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

# Call site inside _get_client()
http_options = types.HttpOptions(
    timeout=_timeout_ms(),
    retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, http_status_codes=[408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]),
)

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily initializes and returns the singleton genai.Client instance stored in the module-level _client variable. It configures transport deadlines and automatic HTTP retry policies, selecting either Vertex AI mode or AI Studio mode based on the presence of GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY.

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        http_options = types.HttpOptions(
            timeout=_timeout_ms(),  # milliseconds; with no timeout a stalled connection hangs forever
            # One SDK retry for transient errors; PocketFlow node retries (5 x 20 s) sit on top.
            retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, http_status_codes=[408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]),
        )
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=gemini_location(), http_options=http_options)
        elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            # vertexai=False explicitly: GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true in the environment would otherwise
            # route the API key to Vertex AI.
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=False, api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"), http_options=http_options)
        else:
            raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    return _client

The function checks if _client is already cached. If uninitialized, it constructs a types.HttpOptions instance specifying total request timeouts and an HTTP retry policy covering status codes [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]. If GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is defined, it instantiates genai.Client(vertexai=True, ...) using the location resolved by gemini_location(). Otherwise, if GEMINI_API_KEY is present, it explicitly forces vertexai=False to prevent ambient Google Cloud environment variables from misrouting traffic.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • genai.Client: The initialized Google GenAI SDK client.

Raises:

  • ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is configured in the environment.

Example:

# Call site inside _stream()
for chunk in _get_client().models.generate_content_stream(model=model, contents=[prompt], config=config):
    # Process stream chunk

docs.title: _thinking_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None):

Description: Constructs the appropriate types.ThinkingConfig object and a human-readable telemetry description string based on model capabilities. It guarantees that thinking_level and thinking_budget parameters are never simultaneously transmitted, clamps levels to model allowances, and formats debug thought summary requests.

def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None):
    """(ThinkingConfig | None, description). Never mixes thinking_level with thinking_budget."""
    mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
    include = True if is_debug() else None  # thought summaries only for the debug log
    if model in _thinking_rejected:
        return None, "default (thinking config rejected by model)"
    if not level:
        # Model default thinking; with --debug still ask for summaries so they can be logged.
        return (types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True) if include and mode != "none" else None), "default"
    if mode == "level":
        effective = clamp_level(level.lower(), spec) or spec[-1]
        if effective != level.lower() and warn_once("gemini_level", model, level):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effective, model=model)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=effective, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_level={effective}"
    if mode == "budget":
        low, high, _can_disable = spec
        budget = min(max(GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS.get(level.lower(), 4096), low), high)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=budget, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_budget={budget}"
    if warn_once("gemini_no_thinking", model):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
    return None, "unsupported"

The function calls gemini_thinking_mode(model) to determine whether the model uses discrete levels ("level"), numeric token budgets ("budget"), or does not support reasoning ("none"). If the model previously returned an HTTP 400 error, it returns early with None. For level-based models, it invokes clamp_level() against the allowed set and emits WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED if adjustments were necessary. For budget-based models, it clamps predefined budget lookups between lower and upper token boundaries.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort string or None.

Returns:

  • tuple[types.ThinkingConfig | None, str]: A tuple containing the initialized SDK thinking configuration (or None) and a telemetry description string.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

# Call site inside call_gemini()
thinking, level_desc = _thinking_config(model, thinking_level)

docs.title: _max_output_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Calculates the maximum output token reservation for a model based on the requested thinking level and the model's structural ceiling. Because Google Gemini tracks separate input and output limits, output token allocations are capped solely by the model's output boundary rather than prompt length.

def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-level budget capped by the model's output limit. Gemini documents separate input and
    output limits, so output is not reduced for large prompts (input_token_budget still reserves it)."""
    _input_limit, output_limit = get_model_limits(model)
    return gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit)

The function retrieves the model limits via get_model_limits(), extracting output_limit. It then delegates to gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit), which maps reasoning levels to token allocations while bounding them to the maximum ceiling permitted by the target architecture.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort level.

Returns:

  • int: The token budget allocated for completion generation and internal reasoning.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

# Call site inside call_gemini()
max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)

docs.title: _name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _name(value) -> str:

Description: Normalizes SDK enumeration instances or dynamic string representations into clean, uppercase symbolic names.

def _name(value) -> str:
    """Enum → 'NAME' (unknown enum members arrive as dynamic values; compare by name)."""
    return (getattr(value, "name", None) or str(value or "")).split(".")[-1].upper()

The function inspects the input object for a .name attribute commonly found on Python enum members. If absent, it converts the value to a string, splits on period delimiters to discard enum class qualifications, and normalizes the final segment to uppercase.

Parameters:

  • value (Any): An enum member, string, or object representing a finish or block status.

Returns:

  • str: The uppercase string name representation.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

# Call site inside _stream()
if feedback is not None and getattr(feedback, "block_reason", None):
    block_reason = _name(feedback.block_reason)

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:

Description: Estimates the monetary cost in USD for a given Gemini invocation. It evaluates model prefixes against pricing schedules, accounts for introductory pricing windows, computes tiered rates for long-context prompts, and applies regional Vertex AI surcharges.

def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:
    key = next((k for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if model.lower().startswith(k)), None)
    if key is None:
        return None
    row = _PRICING[key]
    if key in _INTRO_PRICING and (today or datetime.date.today()) <= _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL:
        row = _INTRO_PRICING[key]
    p_in, p_out, p_cache = row[3:6] if len(row) == 6 and prompt_tokens > _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD else row[:3]
    uncached = max(prompt_tokens - cached, 0)
    cost = (uncached * p_in + cached * p_cache + output_tokens * p_out) / 1_000_000
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") and gemini_location().lower() != "global":
        cost *= _REGIONAL_UPLIFT
    return cost

The function matches the model against _PRICING keys using longest-prefix matching. If the model falls under active introductory rates in _INTRO_PRICING (valid through _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL), those rates supersede standard tiers. If prompt tokens exceed _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD (200,000 tokens) and the pricing entry defines a 6-element tuple, long-context rates are applied. The cost is calculated per million tokens across uncached prompts, cached prompts, and combined output tokens. Finally, if the request is routed through Vertex AI outside the "global" region, a 10% uplift (_REGIONAL_UPLIFT = 1.10) is applied.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • prompt_tokens (int): Total prompt tokens reported by usage metadata.
  • cached (int): Tokens read from explicit cache layers.
  • output_tokens (int): Combined candidate and thinking tokens.
  • today (datetime.date | None): Optional date override for introductory pricing evaluation. Defaults to datetime.date.today().

Returns:

  • float | None: The estimated USD cost, or None if the model pricing is unmapped.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

# Call site inside _record()
cost = _price(model, prompt, cached, output)

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:

Description: Extracts token counts from SDK usage metadata, calculates USD cost, registers execution metrics in the central ledger, and calibrates local prompt tokenizer scaling ratios.

def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:
    prompt = getattr(usage, "prompt_token_count", 0) or 0
    candidates = getattr(usage, "candidates_token_count", 0) or 0
    thoughts = getattr(usage, "thoughts_token_count", 0) or 0
    cached = getattr(usage, "cached_content_token_count", 0) or 0
    output = candidates + thoughts  # thinking is billed as output
    cost = _price(model, prompt, cached, output)
    record_usage("GEMINI", model, input_tokens=prompt, output_tokens=output, thinking_tokens=thoughts, cache_read=cached, cost=cost)
    ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    observe_prompt_tokens("GEMINI", model, raw_prompt_tokens, prompt)  # prompt_token_count includes cached tokens
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"GEMINI USAGE | model={model} | {level_desc} | finish={finish or 'n/a'} | in={prompt:,} | out={candidates:,} | thinking={thoughts:,} | "
        f"cached={cached:,} | est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="BOTH",
    )

The function reads prompt_token_count, candidates_token_count, thoughts_token_count, and cached_content_token_count from the usage_metadata object. Thinking tokens are combined with candidate tokens into output, reflecting Google's billing architecture. It calls record_usage() from utils.llm_common, invokes observe_prompt_tokens() from utils.token_utils to calibrate estimation ratios against actual token counts, and outputs formatted execution metrics via emit_raw().

Parameters:

  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • usage (Any): The usage_metadata object returned on the stream payload.
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): Pre-call token count estimated by the local tokenizer.
  • level_desc (str): Text description of the active thinking level.
  • finish (str): The candidate finish reason string.
  • elapsed (float): Total wall-clock seconds consumed by the stream.

Returns:

  • None.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

# Call site inside call_gemini()
if result["usage"] is not None:
    _record(model, result["usage"], raw_tokens, level_desc, result["finish"], elapsed)

docs.title: _stream()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config) -> dict:

Description: Consumes the generator returned by generate_content_stream(), iterating over all stream chunks to concatenate completion text and reasoning thought parts while capturing finish reasons, prompt feedback blocks, and usage metadata.

def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config) -> dict:
    """Consume generate_content_stream; returns text, thoughts, finish, block_reason, usage."""
    text, thoughts = [], []
    finish, block_reason, usage = "", "", None
    for chunk in _get_client().models.generate_content_stream(model=model, contents=[prompt], config=config):
        feedback = getattr(chunk, "prompt_feedback", None)
        if feedback is not None and getattr(feedback, "block_reason", None):
            block_reason = _name(feedback.block_reason)
        if getattr(chunk, "usage_metadata", None) is not None:
            usage = chunk.usage_metadata
        for candidate in getattr(chunk, "candidates", None) or []:
            if getattr(candidate, "finish_reason", None):
                finish = _name(candidate.finish_reason)
            content = getattr(candidate, "content", None)
            for part in (getattr(content, "parts", None) or []) if content is not None else []:
                if getattr(part, "text", None):
                    (thoughts if getattr(part, "thought", False) else text).append(part.text)
            break  # candidate_count is 1
    return {"text": "".join(text), "thoughts": "".join(thoughts), "finish": finish, "block_reason": block_reason, "usage": usage}

The function dispatches _get_client().models.generate_content_stream(). For each streamed chunk, it inspects prompt_feedback for safety blocks, records incoming usage_metadata, and traverses candidate content parts. Content parts tagged with thought=True are routed into thoughts, while standard content parts append to text. The function returns an aggregated dictionary once the stream concludes.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • prompt (str): The raw text prompt.
  • config (types.GenerateContentConfig): The fully populated configuration instance.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing aggregated response text, thought strings, finish reason, block reason, and usage metadata. See Stream Result Dictionary for schema details.

Raises:

  • genai_errors.ClientError: If the Google GenAI backend rejects the request payload or stream.

Example:

# Call site inside call_gemini()
result = _stream(model, prompt, config)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive error handling to classify network, validation, and content policy failures:

  • Authentication Validation: In _get_client(), if neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment, execution halts immediately by raising a ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment").
  • Dynamic Thinking Fallback: When _stream() encounters a google.genai.errors.ClientError with HTTP status code 400 whose message references thinking configuration, call_gemini() intercepts the exception. It adds the model name to _thinking_rejected, emits WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED, strips thinking_config, and replays the request without raising an exception to the caller.
  • Content Refusal and Policy Blocks: In call_gemini(), if result["block_reason"] is non-empty or result["finish"] appears in _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS, the module registers an event via count_event("GEMINI", "refusals") and raises an LLMRefusalError. It evaluates retryable status: candidate stops (SAFETY, RECITATION, LANGUAGE, OTHER) set retryable=True to allow caller resampling, whereas prompt-level blocks (PROHIBITED_CONTENT, BLOCKLIST, SPII) set retryable=False.
  • Truncation Safeguards: If a candidate terminates with MAX_TOKENS, it is registered via count_event("GEMINI", "truncations") and wrapped in TruncatedResponse. This prevents callers (such as call_llm) from committing partial responses to persistent SHA-256 disk caches.
  • Stream Deadlines and Transport Retries: Transient HTTP status codes (408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) trigger automatic client-side retries governed by types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2). Stalled streaming connections are terminated according to _timeout_ms().

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/llm_openrouter.py provides the catalog-driven OpenRouter inference adapter for the centralized Large Language Model (LLM) execution pipeline in call_llm.py. Operating across OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoints, the module dynamically interfaces with heterogeneous upstream model families (such as Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and Qwen) without relying on hardcoded parameter tables. Instead, it inspects dynamic metadata retrieved from the OpenRouter model catalog via utils.llm_config to govern reasoning effort parameters, output token ceilings, and sampling options at runtime.

The module enforces Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming for all completions to eliminate read timeouts during prolonged multi-turn reasoning phases, filtering out transient : OPENROUTER PROCESSING keep-alive comments. Network interactions are safeguarded by an exponential backoff retry loop with bounded attempts for transient HTTP status codes (such as rate limits and gateway timeouts) while respecting server-supplied Retry-After headers. In addition, the component manages opt-in application attribution headers, classifies guardrail blocks and safety refusals into retryable or non-retryable exceptions, returns truncation indicators when response ceilings are reached, and records multi-dimensional token counts and financial costs (including Bring Your Own Key / BYOK upstream fees) directly into the system's global usage ledger.

docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves and sanitizes the configured OpenRouter model identifier by inspecting the OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable. Whitespace is stripped to ensure clean lookup strings for catalog queries and API payload generation.

Parameters:

  • This function takes no arguments.

Returns:

  • str: The target model name (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet"), or an empty string if unset.

Example:

model = get_model()
if not model:
    raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")

The function provides safe fallback access to the primary configuration variable. Callers verify that the string is non-empty before initiating downstream payload preparation or authorization preflight checks.

docs.title: build_payload()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_payload(prompt: str, model: str, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, str]:

Description: Compiles the OpenAI-compatible JSON dictionary payload dispatched to the OpenRouter chat completions endpoint. It inspects catalog specifications via openrouter_model_info to adjust token limits, configure reasoning structures, and evaluate whether sampling parameters should be included.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The raw input user prompt text.
  • model (str): The designated OpenRouter model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The desired thinking effort level ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", or None).
  • prompt_tokens (int): The estimated prompt token consumption used for context window margin calculations.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, str]: A 2-tuple where index 0 contains the completion request payload dictionary, and index 1 contains a human-readable telemetry description of the reasoning configuration.

Example:

info = openrouter_model_info(model)
max_tokens = _max_tokens(model, info, level, prompt_tokens)
reasoning, desc = _reasoning(model, info, level, max_tokens)
payload = {
    "model": model,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    "stream": True,
}
if max_tokens:
    payload["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
if reasoning is not None:
    payload["reasoning"] = reasoning
if _sends_temperature(model, info, reasoning):
    try:
        payload["temperature"] = float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE", "0.7"))
    except ValueError:
        payload["temperature"] = 0.7

build_payload() enforces stream mode ("stream": True) unconditionally to support progressive SSE reads. It dynamically attaches max_tokens, reasoning, and temperature fields based on catalog parameters, guarding against invalid API requests such as sending temperature to reasoning models or requesting thinking capabilities from models that do not support them.

docs.title: call_openrouter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_openrouter(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary public inference coordinator for the OpenRouter provider. It resolves environment parameters, measures input tokens, compiles headers and payloads, handles streaming HTTP execution, logs diagnostic and reasoning metrics, records ledger usage, and translates termination indicators into completions, truncations, or refusal errors.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The input prompt string dispatched for completion.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Optional reasoning effort level. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The completed response text, or a TruncatedResponse instance if generation was cut off by token limits.

Raises:

  • ValueError: If the OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is not defined or is empty.
  • RuntimeError: If network retries are exhausted, an upstream or streaming error occurs, the stream ends without a finish reason, or generation terminates with an error code.
  • LLMRefusalError: If the model or OpenRouter guardrail filters block the request.

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment and Token Validation
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, token_ratio

model = get_model()
if not model:
    raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")
api_key = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "").strip()
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
payload, desc = build_payload(prompt, model, thinking_level, int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()))
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", **_attribution_headers()}
if api_key:
    headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"
max_tokens = payload.get("max_tokens")

The initial phase validates that a target model is configured and reads the optional API key from OPENROUTER_API_KEY. It estimates prompt tokens by querying count_tokens_raw scaled by the current token_ratio(), then constructs the request payload and headers (including opt-in attribution metadata).

docs.title: Phase 2: Streaming Transport and Error Recovery
docs.text:
start = time.time()
resp = _post(f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/chat/completions", headers, payload)
generation_id = resp.headers.get("X-Generation-Id")
try:
    result = _consume(resp)
except Exception:
    # An error chunk mid-stream ("Upstream idle timeout exceeded") still was a request: unmeasured, like a
    # dropped stream, so a failed attempt and its retry both show in the usage ledger
    record_usage("OPENROUTER", model, cost=None, measured=False)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | stream error, no usage reported | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}", dest="BOTH")
    raise

The transport phase initiates the HTTP request via _post() against the configured base URL. If the SSE stream fails or drops unexpectedly during _consume(), the exception handler ensures the failed attempt is recorded in the usage ledger as an unmeasured request prior to re-raising the exception.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry Accounting and Response Classification
docs.text:
_record(model, result, raw_tokens, desc, time.time() - start, generation_id)
if is_debug() and result["reasoning"]:
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"REASONING:\n{result['reasoning']}", dest="LOG")

finish, native = (result["finish"] or ""), (result["native"] or "")
if finish == "error":
    raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter generation ended with an error (native_finish_reason={native or 'n/a'})")
if finish == "content_filter" or result["refusal"] or native.lower() in _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS:
    category = native or finish or "refusal"
    # Filters on sampled output (safety, recitation, content_filter) may pass on another attempt.
    retryable = not result["refusal"] and native.lower() not in _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS
    count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
    emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
    raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER", retryable=retryable)
if not finish:
    # No data at all, or the connection dropped mid-answer: never return a partial reply.
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"OpenRouter stream ended without a finish_reason after {result['events']} events ({len(result['text']):,} characters received)"
    )
if finish == "length":
    count_event("OPENROUTER", "truncations")
    emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="OpenRouter", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}" if max_tokens else "default")
    return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
if not result["text"]:
    emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter response contained no text (finish_reason={finish or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
return result["text"]

The final phase commits detailed token usage and timing statistics via _record(). It evaluates the completion's finish_reason and native_finish_reason, distinguishing between non-retryable deterministic refusals and retryable sampling blocks (e.g., safety filters). If output is bounded by max tokens (finish == "length"), it wraps the text in a TruncatedResponse to prevent caching incomplete responses.
