docs.title: _read_timeout()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _read_timeout() -> float:

Description: Calculates the HTTP streaming read timeout threshold in seconds. It parses the OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable, enforcing a minimum lower bound of 30.0 seconds to prevent early drops during extended thinking phases.

Parameters:

  • This function takes no arguments.

Returns:

  • float: Read timeout duration in seconds (defaulting to 300.0).

Example:

def _read_timeout() -> float:
    try:
        return max(float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "300")), 30.0)
    except ValueError:
        return 300.0

This helper wraps environment parsing in a ValueError guard. If invalid or non-numeric values are supplied in the environment, it safely falls back to the default duration of 300.0 seconds.

docs.title: _reasoning()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _reasoning(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, max_tokens: int | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:

Description: Constructs the "reasoning" configuration sub-dictionary for the request payload. Based on the model catalog metadata, it determines whether to send effort-based reasoning ("effort"), token budget-based reasoning ("max_tokens"), or omit reasoning entirely if unsupported.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): Model catalog metadata returned by openrouter_model_info.
  • level (str | None): Desired thinking level string.
  • max_tokens (int | None): Planned maximum completion token limit. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict | None, str]: A tuple containing the reasoning configuration dictionary (or None if disabled/unsupported) and an audit description string.

Example:

def _reasoning(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, max_tokens: int | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:
    if not level:
        return None, "default"
    level = level.lower()
    exclude = not is_debug()
    if info is None:
        return {"effort": level, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={level} (unverified)"
    reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
    if not isinstance(reasoning, dict) and "reasoning" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
        if warn_once("openrouter_no_reasoning", model):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
        return None, "unsupported"
    meta = reasoning if isinstance(reasoning, dict) else {}
    if "supported_efforts" not in meta and meta.get("supports_max_tokens"):
        budget = _REASONING_BUDGETS.get(level, _REASONING_BUDGETS["medium"])
        if max_tokens:
            budget = max(min(budget, max_tokens - 1_024), 1_024)
        return {"max_tokens": budget, "exclude": exclude}, f"reasoning.max_tokens={budget}"
    efforts = meta.get("supported_efforts")
    effort = level
    if efforts:
        effort = clamp_level(level, [e for e in efforts if e != "none"]) or level
        if effort != level and warn_once("openrouter_level", model, level):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effort, model=model)
    return {"effort": effort, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={effort}"

The function clamps requested effort levels using clamp_level() to prevent invalid configurations, explicitly filtering out 'none' which causes HTTP 400 errors on mandatory reasoning models. When operating in non-debug mode (not is_debug()), it injects "exclude": True to prevent raw thinking traces from appearing in final completions while still allowing token billing.

docs.title: _sends_temperature()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the temperature parameter may be safely sent in the payload. Sampling parameters are suppressed if reasoning is active, if the model family rejects sampling, or if catalog metadata flags reasoning as mandatory or enabled by default.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): Catalog metadata dictionary for the model.
  • reasoning (dict | None): Configured reasoning dictionary, if any.

Returns:

  • bool: True if temperature should be included, False otherwise.

Example:

def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:
    if reasoning is not None or rejects_sampling_params(model):
        return False
    if info is None:
        return True
    if "temperature" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
        return False
    meta = info.get("reasoning") if isinstance(info.get("reasoning"), dict) else {}
    return not (meta.get("mandatory") or meta.get("default_enabled"))

The function incorporates guard logic against sending sampling parameters to advanced reasoning models (such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet in thinking mode or Gemini 2.5/3.x series). It verifies compatibility against both catalog parameter declarations and family-level rules defined in rejects_sampling_params().

docs.title: _max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:

Description: Computes the output token budget for the request. It retrieves the planned budget from openrouter_output_budget and clamps it to ensure it does not exceed the remaining provider context window after subtracting prompt tokens and safety margins.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): Catalog metadata for the model.
  • level (str | None): Thinking effort level.
  • prompt_tokens (int): Number of tokens consumed by the prompt.

Returns:

  • int | None: Clamped output token limit, or None if the model or context window limits are unknown.

Example:

def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:
    planned = openrouter_output_budget(model, level)
    context = ((info or {}).get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or (info or {}).get("context_length")
    if planned and context:
        planned = min(planned, max(context - prompt_tokens - CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096))
    return planned

The calculation resolves context limits by prioritizing top_provider.context_length before falling back to top-level context_length. If remaining context is constrained, it clamps output to available headroom while enforcing a floor of 4,096 tokens.

docs.title: _attribution_headers()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _attribution_headers() -> dict:

Description: Constructs HTTP headers used for OpenRouter ranking and application attribution. These headers are only generated if the OPENROUTER_APP_URL environment variable is explicitly set.

Parameters:

  • This function takes no arguments.

Returns:

  • dict: Dictionary containing HTTP-Referer, X-OpenRouter-Title, and legacy X-Title header fields, or an empty dictionary if unconfigured.

Example:

def _attribution_headers() -> dict:
    url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_APP_URL", "").strip()
    if not url:
        return {}
    return {"HTTP-Referer": url, "X-OpenRouter-Title": _APP_TITLE, "X-Title": _APP_TITLE}

This helper guarantees privacy by default: no identifying metadata about the host tool or calling environment is transmitted to OpenRouter unless the user opts in by setting OPENROUTER_APP_URL.

docs.title: _retry_after()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:

Description: Parses the standard Retry-After HTTP response header into a floating-point number representing seconds to wait before attempting another request.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response object.

Returns:

  • float | None: Wait time in seconds, or None if the header is absent or non-numeric.

Example:

def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:
    value = resp.headers.get("Retry-After")
    try:
        return float(value) if value else None
    except ValueError:
        return None

The function isolates header parsing within a try-except block to guard against malformed header values or HTTP-date formats, returning None to permit exponential backoff fallbacks when seconds cannot be parsed.

docs.title: _error_body()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_body(resp) -> dict:

Description: Safely parses the JSON error payload from an HTTP response, extracting inner error dictionaries if wrapped under a root "error" key.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The failing HTTP response object.

Returns:

  • dict: Extracted error dictionary, or a synthesized dictionary wrapping string error representations.

Example:

def _error_body(resp) -> dict:
    try:
        body = resp.json()
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    err = body.get("error", body) if isinstance(body, dict) else body
    return err if isinstance(err, dict) else {"message": str(err)}

By safely converting parsing failures to empty dictionaries and standardizing primitive string bodies into {"message": str(err)}, this helper provides a uniform interface for downstream error extractors.

docs.title: _error_detail()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_detail(resp) -> str:

Description: Formats an actionable error diagnostic message from an HTTP response by inspecting error bodies, metadata, raw provider messages, and text truncations.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response object.

Returns:

  • str: Human-readable error diagnostic string.

Example:

def _error_detail(resp) -> str:
    err = _error_body(resp)
    if not err:
        return resp.text[:300].strip()
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    raw = meta.get("raw") or meta.get("provider_name") or ""
    return f"{err.get('message', err)}" + (f" ({raw})" if raw else "")

If structured JSON is available, the helper combines the primary error message with upstream provider metadata (such as backend error reasons). If JSON parsing fails, it truncates the raw response body to 300 characters to prevent log flooding.

docs.title: _refusal_category()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:

Description: Analyzes an HTTP 403 Forbidden response to determine if it represents a moderation, guardrail, or content policy refusal rather than a general permission or authentication failure.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response object.

Returns:

  • str | None: Refusal category identifier (e.g., "content_policy_violation", "moderation"), or None if the status code is not 403 or the error is unrelated to content moderation.

Example:

def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:
    if resp.status_code != 403:
        return None
    err = _error_body(resp)
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    kind = str(err.get("type") or err.get("error_type") or meta.get("error_type") or "").lower()
    if kind in _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES:
        return kind
    if meta.get("reasons") or meta.get("flagged_input"):
        reasons = meta.get("reasons") or ["moderation"]
        return ",".join(map(str, reasons)) if isinstance(reasons, list) else str(reasons)
    return None

The function checks both standard OpenRouter error type fields and nested metadata arrays (metadata.reasons). When flagged input reasons are detected, it joins them into a comma-delimited string to classify the refusal.

docs.title: _post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _post(url: str, headers: dict, payload: dict):

Description: Dispatches the HTTP POST request to the completion endpoint with a streaming response connection. It encapsulates retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors, handles connection failures, and translates HTTP 403 moderation blocks into LLMRefusalError.

Parameters:

  • url (str): Target completions endpoint URL.
  • headers (dict): HTTP request headers.
  • payload (dict): Serialized JSON payload dictionary.

Returns:

  • requests.Response: An open streaming response object.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: When an HTTP 403 response corresponds to a content moderation or policy refusal.
  • RuntimeError: When network connection retries are exhausted or a non-refusal HTTP error occurs.

docs.title: Connection Management and Transient Retry Loop
docs.text:
for attempt in range(1, _MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
    try:
        resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, stream=True, timeout=(15, _read_timeout()))
    except (requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout) as e:
        if attempt == _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter request failed after {attempt} attempts: {e}") from e
        time.sleep(2**attempt)
        continue
    if resp.status_code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS and attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
        wait = min(_retry_after(resp) or 2**attempt * 2, 60)
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}; retrying in {wait:.0f}s ({_error_detail(resp)})", dest="LOG")
        resp.close()
        time.sleep(wait)
        continue

The loop attempts up to _MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) dispatches. Network timeouts and dropped connections trigger exponential backoff pauses (2**attempt). When receiving a retryable status code (such as 429 or 503), it honors the Retry-After header capped at 60 seconds.

docs.title: HTTP Error and Refusal Interception
docs.text:
if resp.status_code >= 400:
        detail, category = _error_detail(resp), _refusal_category(resp)
        resp.close()
        if category:
            model = payload.get("model", "")
            count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
            emit("WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP 403 refusal: {detail}", dest="LOG")
            raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER")
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}: {detail}")
    return resp
raise RuntimeError("OpenRouter request failed")  # unreachable

For HTTP status codes >= 400 that are not retried, the connection is closed immediately. The helper differentiates between content moderation blocks (raising LLMRefusalError) and standard HTTP errors (raising RuntimeError with extracted detail).

docs.title: _consume()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _consume(resp) -> dict:

Description: Parses the open response stream. It supports both standard Server-Sent Events (SSE) data streams and single-payload JSON bodies emitted by non-streaming OpenAI-compatible proxies.

Parameters:

  • resp (requests.Response): Open streaming HTTP response.

Returns:

  • dict: Accumulated output dictionary containing consolidated text, reasoning, finish states, and usage metrics.

Example:

def _consume(resp) -> dict:
    out = {"text": [], "reasoning": [], "finish": None, "native": None, "refusal": None, "usage": None, "events": 0}
    try:
        if "application/json" in (resp.headers.get("Content-Type") or "").lower():
            _apply_chunk(out, resp.json())
        else:
            for raw_line in resp.iter_lines():
                line = raw_line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if isinstance(raw_line, bytes) else raw_line
                if not line or line.startswith(":") or not line.startswith("data:"):
                    continue
                data = line[5:].strip()
                if data == "[DONE]":
                    break
                try:
                    chunk = json.loads(data)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                _apply_chunk(out, chunk)
    finally:
        resp.close()
    out["text"] = "".join(out["text"])
    out["reasoning"] = "".join(out["reasoning"])
    return out

The function processes stream lines as raw byte sequences decoded with errors="replace". This prevents decoding bugs with str.splitlines(), which breaks on Unicode line separators like U+2028 or U+0085 that may appear within raw JSON strings. It ignores comment lines (such as : OPENROUTER PROCESSING) and terminates when encountering the [DONE] SSE marker.

docs.title: _apply_chunk()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:

Description: Updates the accumulator dictionary in _consume() by folding in content deltas, reasoning strings, refusal notices, finish reasons, and usage metrics from a single deserialized stream chunk.

Parameters:

  • out (dict): The shared accumulator dictionary.
  • chunk (dict): Parsed JSON chunk from the SSE stream.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError: If the chunk contains a top-level or choice-level error definition from OpenRouter or the upstream provider.

Example:

def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:
    out["events"] += 1
    if chunk.get("error"):
        err = chunk["error"]
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter stream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")
    if chunk.get("usage"):
        out["usage"] = chunk["usage"]
    for choice in chunk.get("choices") or []:
        delta = choice.get("delta") or choice.get("message") or {}
        if delta.get("content"):
            out["text"].append(delta["content"])
        if delta.get("reasoning"):
            out["reasoning"].append(delta["reasoning"])
        if delta.get("refusal"):
            out["refusal"] = delta["refusal"]
        if choice.get("finish_reason"):
            out["finish"] = choice["finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("native_finish_reason"):
            out["native"] = choice["native_finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("error"):
            err = choice["error"]
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter upstream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")

_apply_chunk() checks for stream-level and choice-level error blocks (such as mid-stream upstream timeouts). It extracts content deltas across both streaming chunk formats (choice.delta) and non-streaming proxy formats (choice.message).

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:

Description: Extracts token counts and cost metrics from completion results, updates the global usage ledger via record_usage(), calibrates the tokenizer ratio using observe_prompt_tokens(), and emits structured debug telemetry.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier.
  • result (dict): Consolidated stream result dictionary produced by _consume().
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): Number of prompt tokens measured by the local tokenizer prior to the request.
  • desc (str): Descriptive string detailing reasoning configuration.
  • elapsed (float): Elapsed request execution time in seconds.
  • generation_id (str | None): OpenRouter generation identifier extracted from the X-Generation-Id response header.

Example:

def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:
    if not result["usage"]:
        record_usage("OPENROUTER", model, cost=None, measured=False)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | no usage reported | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}", dest="BOTH")
        return
    usage = result["usage"]
    prompt = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
    completion = usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0
    reasoning_tokens = (usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0
    details = usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}
    cached = details.get("cached_tokens") or 0
    cache_write = details.get("cache_write_tokens") or 0
    cost = usage.get("cost")
    upstream = (usage.get("cost_details") or {}).get("upstream_inference_cost")
    if usage.get("is_byok") and isinstance(upstream, int | float):
        cost = (cost if isinstance(cost, int | float) else 0.0) + upstream
    record_usage(
        "OPENROUTER",
        model,
        input_tokens=prompt,
        output_tokens=completion,
        thinking_tokens=reasoning_tokens,
        cache_read=cached,
        cache_write=cache_write,
        cost=float(cost) if isinstance(cost, int | float) else None,
    )
    ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    observe_prompt_tokens("OPENROUTER", model, raw_prompt_tokens, prompt)

The function handles Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests by combining OpenRouter routing fees with cost_details.upstream_inference_cost. It decomposes token usage into prompt, completion, reasoning, and cached token fields, feeding observed prompt token counts back into observe_prompt_tokens() to calibrate tokenizer ratios for subsequent runs.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/llm_openrouter.py implements a multi-tiered error recovery and classification strategy to distinguish between transient network issues, content policy blocks, generation truncation, and fatal errors:

  • Transient HTTP Retries: Status codes defined in _RETRYABLE_STATUS (408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529) trigger automated retries up to _MAX_ATTEMPTS (3). The wait time prioritizes the response's Retry-After header when available, falling back to exponential backoff (2**attempt * 2) bounded at 60 seconds.
  • HTTP 403 Refusal Classification: When an HTTP 403 Forbidden status is encountered, _refusal_category() inspects the response body and metadata. If classified as a content policy, guardrail, or moderation violation (matching _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES), it raises LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER") rather than a generic network exception.
  • Stream Disconnection and Mid-Stream Errors: If an SSE stream drops without providing a finish_reason, or if a chunk returns an explicit error payload, a RuntimeError is raised. The failure is recorded as an unmeasured attempt via record_usage() so that failed attempts are accounted for in the execution ledger.
  • Native Finish Reason Mapping: Upstream stop reasons in _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS (refusal, safety, prohibited_content, recitation, blocklist, spii, content_filter) raise LLMRefusalError. Deterministic triggers in _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS mark the error as non-retryable (retryable=False), while probabilistic filters (such as recitation or content_filter) allow retries (retryable=True).
  • Length Truncation: When generation ends due to token limits (finish == "length"), output is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse instance. This signals downstream callers that output was cut off, preventing partial answers from being committed to persistent disk caches.

docs.text:

  • utils/llm_config.py — supplies catalog lookups, base URLs, output token budgets, and sampling restriction policies.
  • utils/output.py — manages event emission, debug logging, and reasoning output traces.
  • utils/thinking.py — provides reasoning level clamping across supported model effort levels.
  • utils/token_utils.py — provides local token measurement and calibrates prompt token observation ratios.

docs.title: mkdocs.py
docs.text: Source: utils/mkdocs.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/mkdocs.py module is the centralized documentation synthesis, static site configuration, and navigation generation subsystem in Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. It consolidates output pipeline mechanics previously distributed across workflow nodes, providing end-to-end transformation of raw generated chapter content into fully configured MkDocs Material documentation suites or standalone multi-chapter Markdown bundles. The module handles configuration building (mkdocs.yml), JavaScript asset generation for Mermaid diagrams, LLM-driven architectural module grouping, dependency graph generation, cross-chapter link normalization, deterministic dependency provenance tagging, and render-verified CommonMark markup repair.

Architecturally, the module sits downstream of chapter generation and verification passes. When invoked in api-reference mode, it uses deterministic source facts extracted by utils/facts.py alongside LLM clustering to arrange modules into domain-driven architectural sections. It computes dependency fan-in metrics to identify shared structural hubs, generating responsive Mermaid diagrams for high-level module architecture and granular dependency interactions. For content integrity, the file implements a verification-guarded markup repair engine that re-indents nested lists and inserts missing blank lines ahead of tables and lists, verifying through an in-memory MkDocs Markdown renderer instance that no visible prose or fenced code blocks are mutated.

docs.title: yaml_str()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def yaml_str(value) -> str:

Description: Quotes and serializes a Python scalar value into a valid YAML double-quoted string literal using JSON encoding (json.dumps). This ensures that labels, navigation titles, and section names containing colons, quotes, leading @ symbols, or brackets can be safely embedded into hand-crafted YAML documents like mkdocs.yml without syntax corruption.

Parameters:

  • value (Any): The scalar value to stringify, strip, and quote.

Returns:

  • str: A JSON-encoded, double-quoted string literal safe for inclusion in YAML files.

Example:

# From utils/mkdocs.py: Hand-crafting safe navigation strings
home_line = f"  - {yaml_str(get('UI_HOME'))}: index.md\n" if include_home else ""
lines.append(f"{pad}- {yaml_str(section['name'])}:")

The function executes json.dumps(str(value).strip(), ensure_ascii=False). Because JSON string literals conform strictly to YAML scalar double-quote specifications, characters that would otherwise trigger YAML syntax errors (such as : or #) are safely escaped.

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:

Description: Generates the complete mkdocs.yml configuration specification for MkDocs Material sites. Configures theme settings, search, interactive Mermaid rendering via pymdownx.superfences using a custom mermaid-raw div class, pan/zoom plugin support, code syntax highlighting, copy-to-clipboard buttons, palette toggle controls (light/dark mode), and hierarchical navigation trees.

Parameters:

  • site_name (str): The project name and documentation title to display in the header.
  • nav_yaml (str): Pre-formatted YAML navigation block generated by navigation routines.
  • include_home (bool): Whether to insert an explicit Home (docs/index.md) entry at the top of navigation. Defaults to True.
  • lang_code (str): Optional ISO 639-1 language code string (e.g., "vi", "zh", "ja") for MkDocs Material UI localization. Defaults to "".

Returns:

  • str: The complete raw YAML text ready to be written to mkdocs.yml.

Example:

mkdocs_config = build_mkdocs_config(
    site_title,
    nav_snippet,
    include_home=True,
    lang_code=lang_code,
)
with open(mkdocs_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(mkdocs_config)

The function splits nav_yaml to strip the root nav: declaration before indenting the navigation body. It configures pymdownx.superfences with a custom fence formatter mapping mermaid to the mermaid-raw HTML class, ensuring MkDocs Material's built-in color schemes do not override native Mermaid styling. It also configures the panzoom plugin to target .mermaid-raw while explicitly excluding .mermaid to prevent double-wrapping containers.

docs.text:

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_mermaid_init_js() -> str:

Description: Returns the client-side JavaScript initialization script MERMAID_INIT_JS for deployment into docs/javascripts/mermaid-init.js.

Returns:

js_filepath = os.path.join(js_dir, "mermaid-init.js")
with open(js_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(build_mermaid_init_js())

The returned script injects a CSS rule ensuring Mermaid diagrams have a white background and rounded borders when the MkDocs Material dark (slate) palette is active, preventing dark-gray diagram connector lines from becoming invisible.

docs.title: site_renderer()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def site_renderer():

Description: Constructs a Markdown-to-HTML rendering callable identical to the runtime Markdown processing pipeline specified in mkdocs.yml. Reads the configured extensions (toc, tables, fenced_code, pymdownx.highlight, pymdownx.superfences, pymdownx.inlinehilite) directly from build_mkdocs_config using Python's YAML parser to instantiate a reusable markdown.Markdown renderer.

Returns:

  • Callable[[str], str] | None: A state-resetting render function that converts Markdown strings to HTML, or None if markdown or its extensions are not installed.

Example:

render = site_renderer()
if render:
    repaired = Counter()
    for chapter_info in chapter_files:
        chapter_info["content"], fixed = repair_markup(chapter_info["content"], render)

The callable handles runtime re-entrancy by executing renderer.reset().convert(text) on each invocation. If extensions or dependencies are missing, it emits a CHAPTER_CHECK_NO_RENDERER telemetry event via utils.output.emit and returns None.

docs.title: build_chapter_filenames()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_chapter_filenames(chapter_order: list, abstractions: list, is_mkdocs: bool) -> dict:

Description: Maps each integer chapter order index to a normalized output relative Markdown filename. Reconciles chapter filenames across LLM prompt generation and physical disk writing passes. Handles source path mirroring for API reference mode and zero-padded numerical prefixes (NN_name.md) for standalone mode, automatically deduplicating filenames case-insensitively and preventing collisions with index.md.

Parameters:

  • chapter_order (list): Indices referencing items in abstractions.
  • abstractions (list): List of abstraction metadata dictionaries containing name and optional original_path.
  • is_mkdocs (bool): Flag indicating whether output targets MkDocs or standalone Markdown.

Returns:

  • dict[int, str]: Mapping of chapter position index to relative Markdown filename.

Example:

filenames = {}
used = {"index.md"}
for i, abstraction_index in enumerate(chapter_order):
    if not 0 <= abstraction_index < len(abstractions):
        continue
    # ... calculates base and deduplicates suffix ...
    filenames[i] = filename
return filenames

The function normalizes Windows backslashes (\) to POSIX slashes (/). If an abstraction defines original_path and is_mkdocs is True, the mirrored source path is retained; otherwise, an alphanumeric sanitized name is generated. Case-insensitive collisions are resolved by appending numerical suffixes (_2.md, _3.md).

docs.title: split_frontmatter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def split_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:

Description: Strips leading YAML frontmatter blocks from Markdown source text according to MkDocs metadata parsing rules. Validates that the delimited block parses as a valid YAML mapping (dict) before stripping; horizontal rules (---) that do not constitute valid YAML mappings are retained as content.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw Markdown string.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool]: A tuple containing (body_text, found_flag).

Example:

match = _FRONTMATTER_RE.match(text)
if match:
    try:
        if isinstance(yaml.safe_load(match.group(1)), dict):
            return text[match.end() :].strip(), True
    except Exception:
        pass
return text, False

The method matches against _FRONTMATTER_RE. If yaml.safe_load fails with YAMLError or ValueError (such as impossible dates), the exception is suppressed and the text is returned unmodified.

docs.title: strip_summary_header()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def strip_summary_header(summary: str) -> str:

Description: Drops the auto-generated initial heading line (e.g., Chapter 1 — Abstraction:) prepended by WriteChapters routines from chapter summary blocks.

Parameters:

  • summary (str): Raw chapter summary text.

Returns:

  • str: The summary text with the header line removed and whitespace stripped.

Example:

first, sep, rest = summary.partition("\n")
if sep and _SUMMARY_HEADER_RE.match(first.strip()):
    return rest.strip()
return summary.strip()

Matches the first line using regex _SUMMARY_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^.+ \d+ — .+:$"). If a match is found, the rest of the text is returned.

docs.title: clip_sentences()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def clip_sentences(text: str, limit: int) -> str:

Description: Collapses irregular whitespace and extracts whole grammatical sentences from text up to a specified character limit. Preserves abbreviations, supports CJK sentence boundary delimiters, truncates gracefully at word boundaries if the first sentence exceeds the limit, and closes open Markdown inline backticks.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Source prose text.
  • limit (int): Maximum allowed character length.

Returns:

  • str: Truncated, whitespace-normalized sentence string ending cleanly or with an ellipsis (…).

Example:

# Extract up to 400 characters of clean sentence text
cleaned_desc = clip_sentences(raw_description, 400)

The function uses regex _SENTENCE_END_RE while evaluating tokens against _ABBREVIATIONS via _ends_with_abbreviation. If no complete sentence fits within limit, it splits at the last word boundary, counts backticks, appends a balancing backtick if odd (clipped.count("") % 2`), and terminates with an ellipsis.

docs.title: table_cell_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def table_cell_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Escapes pipe characters (|) with backslashes (\|) so the string can be safely embedded in Markdown table cells, while keeping pipes inside inline code spans (...) unescaped.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Text intended for insertion into a table column.

Returns:

  • str: Escaped string safe for Markdown table parsing.

Example:

parts, position = [], 0
for match in _CODE_SPAN_RE.finditer(text):
    parts.append(text[position : match.start()].replace("|", "\\|"))
    parts.append(match.group(0))
    position = match.end()
parts.append(text[position:].replace("|", "\\|"))
return "".join(parts)

Uses _CODE_SPAN_RE to iterate over code spans, escaping pipes only in text segments located between matches.

docs.title: summary_description()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def summary_description(summary: str, limit: int = 300) -> str:

Description: Extracts a clean, single-point technical summary description from a structured 4-point chapter summary brief for use in index tables. Extracts point (1) (Scope & Responsibility), strips out section numbering, labels, and preamble text, collapses sentence boundaries within the character limit, and escapes table cell pipes.

Parameters:

  • summary (str): The multi-point chapter summary brief.
  • limit (int): Maximum length of the output string. Defaults to 300.

Returns:

  • str: Formatted, single-paragraph description suitable for Markdown tables.

Example:

desc = match["description"]
if desc.startswith("Internal API reference"):
    desc = summaries.get(mod_name) or desc
cell = descriptions.get(mod_name) or summary_description(desc)

Searches for numbered markers using _POINT_PAREN_RE and _POINT_PLAIN_RE. It clips the substring between marker (1) and marker (2), strips labels matching _SUMMARY_LABEL_RE or preamble sentences, and calls clip_sentences and table_cell_text.

docs.title: md_link_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def md_link_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Escapes Markdown metacharacters (\, `, *, _, [, ], |) so that filenames such as __init__.py or array type annotations render literally inside Markdown hyperlink anchor text.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Unescaped display text.

Returns:

  • str: Escaped Markdown link text.

Example:

# Rendering literal filenames with underscores as Markdown links
label = md_link_text("__init__.py")  # Returns "\_\_init\_\_.py"

Applies _MD_ESCAPE_RE.sub(r"\\\1", " ".join(str(text).split())).

docs.title: md_heading_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def md_heading_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Extends md_link_text to additionally escape hash characters (#), preventing trailing directory names or language names (e.g., src/__tests__, C#) from being parsed as CommonMark heading closing tags.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw heading title.

Returns:

  • str: Escaped Markdown heading string.

Example:

lines.append(f"{heading} {md_heading_text(section['name'])}")

docs.title: module_name_lookup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def module_name_lookup(chapter_files: list) -> dict:

Description: Builds a name resolution dictionary that maps alternative module identifiers (such as original file paths, exact module names, and unique basenames) to canonical module_name values.

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • dict[str, str]: Mapping of identifier aliases to authoritative module names.

Example:

lookup = {}
basename_counts = Counter(os.path.basename(cf.get("original_path") or cf["module_name"]) for cf in chapter_files)
for cf in chapter_files:
    name = cf["module_name"]
    lookup[name] = name
    if cf.get("original_path"):
        lookup.setdefault(cf["original_path"], name)
    basename = os.path.basename(cf.get("original_path") or name)
    if basename_counts[basename] == 1:
        lookup.setdefault(basename, name)
return lookup

Identifies unique basenames across all modules. If a basename occurs only once, it is added to the dictionary to map LLM-shortened names back to their canonical modules.

docs.title: grouping_extras()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def grouping_extras(parsed, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[dict, dict]:

Description: Parses and validates the extra metadata fields (descriptions and dependencies) returned by the LLM in response to prompts/common/group_modules.md. Resolves names via module_name_lookup, drops invalid dependencies and self-references, and sanitizes descriptions for table formatting.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict | Any): Deserialized JSON/YAML payload from the grouping LLM step.
  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter file metadata dictionaries.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, list[str]]]: A 2-tuple containing:
    1. Mapping of module_name to sanitized description strings (max 400 characters).
    2. Mapping of source module_name to lists of target module_name dependencies.

Example:

parsed, sections = request_grouping(group_prompt, prep_res, chapter_files)
descriptions, replied = grouping_extras(parsed, chapter_files)

The function handles multiple formats for dependencies (dictionary mapping or lists of {"from": ..., "to": [...]} objects). It filters out references to unknown modules and suppresses self-dependencies (name != source).

docs.title: modules_with_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def modules_with_facts(module_facts: dict, chapter_files: list) -> set:

Description: Scans the AST-extracted facts database (module_facts) and returns the set of module names that have verified code claims, indicating their dependency edges are verified.

Parameters:

  • module_facts (dict): Extracted factual database mapping file paths to claims.
  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter file objects.

Returns:

  • set[str]: Set of canonical module names with verified extraction records.

Example:

name_of = {cf["original_path"]: cf["module_name"] for cf in chapter_files if cf.get("original_path")}
return {
    name_of[path]
    for path, entry in (module_facts or {}).items()
    if path in name_of and entry.get("claims") is not None
}

docs.title: verified_dependencies()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verified_dependencies(module_facts: dict, chapter_files: list) -> dict:

Description: Extracts deterministic cross-module dependency links directly from module_facts claims.

Parameters:

  • module_facts (dict): Factual database mapping source paths to AST extraction facts.
  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter records with original_path and module_name.

Returns:

  • dict[str, list[str]]: Mapping of source module_name to deduplicated lists of dependency module_name strings.

Example:

verified = verified_dependencies(module_facts, chapter_files)

Iterates over each entry's depends_on list in module_facts. Resolves paths to module names using name_of, discards self-dependencies, and deduplicates targets via dict.fromkeys.

docs.title: build_section_map()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_section_map(sections: list, dependencies: dict, max_listed: int = 8) -> tuple[str, bool, bool]:

Description: Generates Mermaid flowchart source code for the top-level architectural overview section in api/index.md. Renders each top-level navigation group as a single node listing its constituent modules, and draws directed edges between groups based on inter-module dependencies. Sections with two or more incoming cross-section edges are highlighted using the entryNode class.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section tree.
  • dependencies (dict): Dependency graph mapping source modules to target modules.
  • max_listed (int): Maximum number of module names to enumerate inside a node before appending a +N more indicator. Defaults to 8.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool, bool]: A 3-tuple containing:
    1. Mermaid flowchart specification string (empty if fewer than 2 sections).
    2. Boolean indicating whether any cross-section edges were drawn.
    3. Boolean indicating whether any hub sections received the entryNode highlight class.

Example:

section_map, map_has_arrows, map_has_hubs = build_section_map(sections, dependencies)
if section_map:
    index_lines += [f"## {get('UI_ARCH_OVERVIEW')}", "", "```mermaid", section_map, "```", ""]

Calls _section_members(sections) to collapse nested child sections into their top-level parents. Identifies cross-section dependencies where owner[source] != owner[target], tallies incoming edges per section node using collections.Counter, and appends _ENTRY_NODE_CLASSDEF styling when hubs are detected.

docs.title: build_module_graph()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_module_graph(sections: list, dependencies: dict, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[str, int]:

Description: Constructs a comprehensive Mermaid module dependency diagram for api/index.md. Generates a flowchart subgraph for each top-level section and individual nodes for each module. Central architectural hub modules (modules used by at least max(5, total // 4) other modules) have their incoming edges detached to prevent diagram tangling, and are instead annotated with usage counts and highlighted using the entryNode class.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section grouping list.
  • dependencies (dict): Map of source module names to lists of target module names.
  • chapter_files (list): List of all chapter metadata dictionaries.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, int]: A 2-tuple containing:
    1. Mermaid diagram source string (or empty string if dependencies are empty or module count exceeds 80).
    2. Integer hub threshold value (0 if no hubs were identified).

Example:

module_graph, hub_threshold = build_module_graph(sections, dependencies, chapter_files)
if module_graph:
    index_lines += [f"## {get('UI_MODULE_DEPENDENCIES')}", "", "```mermaid", module_graph, "```", ""]

If len(chapter_files) > _MODULE_GRAPH_MAX_MODULES (80), the function returns ("", 0) because full-system Mermaid rendering becomes unreadable. Edge connections directed into hub nodes are omitted from the diagram (if target not in hubs) to eliminate arrow clutter.

docs.title: build_hub_fan_ins()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_hub_fan_ins(sections: list, dependencies: dict, chapter_files: list, threshold: int) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:

Description: Generates dedicated, isolated Mermaid fan-in diagrams for modules identified as shared architectural hubs by build_module_graph. Creates a separate small diagram for each hub, grouping its consumer modules by section and displaying directed arrows annotated with consumer counts.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Section grouping tree.
  • dependencies (dict): Module dependency mappings.
  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter file objects.
  • threshold (int): Usage threshold used to qualify a module as a hub.

Returns:

  • list[tuple[str, str]]: List of (hub_module_name, mermaid_diagram_source) tuples sorted in descending order of consumer count.

Example:

for hub, fan_in in build_hub_fan_ins(sections, dependencies, chapter_files, hub_threshold):
    index_lines += [f"#### {md_heading_text(hub)}", "", "```mermaid", fan_in, "```", ""]

For each qualifying hub, the function inverts the dependency graph to find all consumers, groups those consumers by their parent navigation section, and draws arrows from the consumer section boxes to the central hub node with link labels showing user counts (-->|count| H).

docs.title: build_grouped_nav()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:

Description: Recursively constructs the lines of a YAML navigation tree for mkdocs.yml based on the section hierarchy. Groups modules located in subdirectories under deterministic directory subheadings, while leaving root-level modules flat.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): List of section dictionaries containing name, modules, and optional children.
  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter dictionaries containing module_name and filename.
  • indent (int): Base indentation column count. Defaults to 4.

Returns:

  • list[str]: Formatted YAML lines representing the navigation tree.

Example:

nav_lines = build_grouped_nav(sections, chapter_files, indent=4)
nav_lines.insert(0, "    - api/index.md")
nav_snippet = f"nav:\n  - {nav_label}:\n" + "\n".join(nav_lines)

The function iterates over each section, groups matched modules by os.path.dirname(match.get("original_path") or ""), outputs subdirectory groupings with additional padding, emits relative links targeting api/{filename}, and recurses on section["children"] with indent + 2.

docs.title: collect_all_modules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:

Description: Recursively walks a section tree and aggregates every referenced module name into a single set.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section list.

Returns:

  • set: Set of all module name strings found across the section hierarchy.

Example:

result = set()
for section in sections:
    result.update(section.get("modules", []))
    if "children" in section:
        result.update(collect_all_modules(section["children"]))
return result

docs.title: prune_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prune_sections(sections: list, chapter_files: list) -> list:

Description: Cleans an LLM-generated section tree by normalizing module names, removing references to non-existent chapters, and pruning empty sections or sections lacking names. Prevents generation of empty YAML keys (- "Name":) that cause MkDocs builds to fail with "Expected nav to be a list, got None".

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Raw section dictionaries parsed from LLM output.
  • chapter_files (list): Authoritative list of chapter file definitions.

Returns:

  • list: Pruned list of section dictionaries containing only valid modules and populated sub-trees.

Example:

lookup = module_name_lookup(chapter_files)
# ... recursively resolves lookup[name], filters empty children ...

docs.title: tree_order_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def tree_order_key(chapter_file: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Generates a stable sorting tuple based on the directory path of a chapter's source file, ordering root-level files first followed by subdirectories in alphabetical order. Matches the ordering used by build_directory_tree.

Parameters:

  • chapter_file (dict): Chapter file dictionary containing original_path.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, str]: Tuple of (directory_name, file_basename).

Example:

listed = sorted(zip(chapter_files, summaries, strict=True), key=lambda pair: tree_order_key(pair[0]))

Executes os.path.split(chapter_file.get("original_path") or "").

docs.title: directory_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def directory_sections(chapter_files: list) -> list:

Description: Constructs an index section grouping based on the filesystem directory layout. Used as an automatic fallback when LLM grouping is unavailable, fails, or when a project has 5 or fewer modules.

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: Section dictionaries with name (directory path or localized Root Files label) and modules (list of module names).

Example:

groups = {}
for cf in chapter_files:
    groups.setdefault(os.path.dirname(cf.get("original_path") or ""), []).append(cf["module_name"])
return [{"name": directory or get("UI_ROOT_FILES"), "modules": groups[directory]} for directory in sorted(groups)]

docs.title: GROUPING_ATTEMPTS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: GROUPING_ATTEMPTS = 3

Description: Integer constant defining the maximum number of attempts for the group_modules LLM request.

docs.title: GROUPING_WAIT
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: GROUPING_WAIT = 20

Description: Integer constant defining the wait time in seconds between retries of the group_modules LLM request.

docs.title: request_grouping()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def request_grouping(prompt: str, prep_res: dict, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[dict, list]:

Description: Dispatches the module grouping prompt to the LLM via call_llm with retry handling. Parses the response, prunes invalid modules and empty sections, and enforces retry limits. Non-retryable LLMRefusalError exceptions are re-raised immediately without backoff.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): Formatted grouping prompt string.
  • prep_res (dict): Pipeline run state dictionary containing cache settings and thinking levels.
  • chapter_files (list): Authoritative list of chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, list]: A 2-tuple containing (parsed_reply_dict, pruned_sections_list).

Raises:

  • ValueError: If the LLM response contains no valid sections after pruning.
  • LLMRefusalError: If the LLM provider explicitly rejects the prompt with an unretryable violation.
  • Exception: The final caught exception if all retry attempts fail.

Example:

response = call_llm(
    prompt,
    use_cache=use_cache and attempt == 1,
    thinking_level=prep_res.get("thinking_level"),
    step="group_modules",
)
parsed = parse_grouping_response(response)
sections = prune_sections(parsed.get("sections", parsed), chapter_files)
if not sections:
    raise ValueError(get("GROUP_NO_SECTIONS"))
return parsed, sections

The function reads the cache only on the first attempt (attempt == 1). If a failure occurs, it pauses for GROUPING_WAIT (20 seconds) and emits a GROUP_RETRY telemetry event before reattempting.

docs.title: SECTION_ROLES
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: SECTION_ROLES = ("types", "setup", "core", "support", "operational")

Description: Tuple defining the canonical architectural section reading order: domain vocabulary first, followed by setup/initialization, core domain logic, utility support, and finally operational/infrastructure modules.

docs.title: order_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def order_sections(sections: list, chapter_files: list) -> list:

Description: Re-orders sections and their internal modules into reading order. Sibling sections are sorted by their role attribute according to SECTION_ROLES. Within each section, modules are sorted by directory based on first appearance to align with navigation sub-layers.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Section dictionaries to sort.
  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter metadata records.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: New list of section dictionaries ordered by role and directory.

Example:

rank = {role: index for index, role in enumerate(SECTION_ROLES)}
# ... orders level by role_rank if all sections have recognized roles ...
sections = order_sections(sections, chapter_files)

If any section at a given hierarchy level lacks a recognized role, the model's original ordering for that level is preserved.

docs.title: build_index_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_index_sections(lines, sections, chapter_files, level=3, summaries=None, descriptions=None):

Description: Recursively generates Markdown heading blocks and summary tables for each section in the index page (api/index.md). Populates the description column using LLM-generated descriptions when available, falling back to brief extracts via summary_description.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): Mutable list of Markdown lines to append to.
  • sections (list): Hierarchy of section dictionaries.
  • chapter_files (list): Complete list of chapter file metadata dictionaries.
  • level (int): Markdown heading depth level (# count). Defaults to 3.
  • summaries (dict | None): Optional mapping of module names to chapter summary strings.
  • descriptions (dict | None): Optional mapping of module names to single-line descriptions.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates lines in place.

Example:

index_lines += [f"## {chapter_index_label}", ""]
build_index_sections(
    index_lines,
    sections,
    chapter_files,
    summaries=summary_by_module,
    descriptions=descriptions,
)

For each section, it outputs a heading formatted with md_heading_text, followed by a Markdown table with Chapter and Description columns. Modules are rendered with relative links using md_link_text. The function recurses for each child section with level + 1.

docs.title: normalize_chapter_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files):

Description: Scans all chapter content and rewrites cross-chapter Markdown links ([text](target.md)) so that targets use correct relative paths from the current chapter's directory. Handles unique basenames and pins relative paths with ./ when a target matches another chapter's root path.

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list[dict]): Mutable list of chapter file dictionaries containing filename and content.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates the content field of the dictionaries in chapter_files in place.

Example:

# Post-processing pass in write_mkdocs_output
normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files)

The function builds a lookup dictionary of known filenames and unique basenames. It then applies a regular expression (link_pattern = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)")) across each file's content, computing relative paths with os.path.relpath.

docs.title: add_used_by_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def add_used_by_lines(chapter_files: list, module_facts: dict) -> None:

Description: Appends a deterministic "Used by" line to the See Also section of each API reference chapter based on verified importers in facts.json. Removes any previously generated "Used by" lines, closes any open code fences to prevent content corruption, formats relative links, and appends the USED_BY_MARKER tracking token.

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list[dict]): Mutable list of chapter file definitions.
  • module_facts (dict): Verified factual database mapping file paths to AST extraction facts.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates chapter content strings in place.

Example:

# Add verified consumer relationships before writing to disk
add_used_by_lines(chapter_files, prep_res.get("module_facts") or {})

Uses parse_page from utils.chapter_check to identify existing lines ending in USED_BY_MARKER. If a page has an unclosed code block, it appends the matching closing fence before adding the "Used by" line.

docs.title: repair_markup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def repair_markup(markdown: str, render) -> tuple[str, Counter]:

Description: Detects and repairs Markdown formatting defects that would cause MkDocs Material to render tables or lists as plain text or flatten nested lists. Repairs are verified using an in-memory MkDocs renderer to ensure visible prose characters, code blocks, and CommonMark block interpretations remain unchanged.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): Raw Markdown content of a chapter.
  • render (Callable[[str], str]): Renderer function returned by site_renderer().

Returns:

  • tuple[str, Counter]: A 2-tuple containing:
    1. Repaired Markdown content string.
    2. Counter recording the number of repairs applied per issue category (lists_as_text, tables_as_text, lists_flattened).

Example:

render = site_renderer()
if render:
    repaired = Counter()
    for chapter_info in chapter_files:
        chapter_info["content"], fixed = repair_markup(chapter_info["content"], render)
        repaired += fixed

The repair loop runs up to 5 iterations, capped by _REPAIR_RENDERS (40 renders). For each candidate repair, improved() verifies that non-whitespace text remains identical (_visible()), code blocks match (_code_blocks()), and block parsing verdicts from markup_verdicts improve without introducing new errors.

docs.title: normalize_see_also()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_see_also(chapter_files: list) -> int:

Description: Normalizes the formatting of entries in the See Also section across all chapters to follow the standard pattern: - [path/to/file.ext](target) — description. Strips unwanted bold and code-span formatting from link titles and standardizes separators to an em dash (—).

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list[dict]): Mutable list of chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • int: Total number of See Also list items updated across all chapters.

Example:

changed = normalize_see_also(chapter_files)

The function identifies See Also sections using _see_also_lines and parses individual items with _SEE_ALSO_ITEM_RE. It strips extraneous backticks and asterisks from link text and normalizes separators to an em dash with surrounding spaces (—).

docs.title: write_mkdocs_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def write_mkdocs_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files):

Description: Main orchestrator for writing complete MkDocs static documentation sites. Handles navigation grouping, mkdocs.yml generation, JavaScript assets, homepage redirects, landing pages with Mermaid architectural diagrams, chapter link normalization, markup repair, file emission, stale page pruning, and automated quality validation.

Parameters:

  • output_path (str): Root destination directory for the generated documentation site.
  • prep_res (dict): Pipeline preparation state dictionary containing project metadata, modes, fact databases, and directory trees.
  • chapter_files (list[dict]): Complete list of chapter file objects to write.

Returns:

  • None

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment and Path Setup
docs.text:
project_name = prep_res["project_name"]
mode = prep_res["mode"]
api_docs_path = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "api")
os.makedirs(api_docs_path, exist_ok=True)

mode_labels = {
    "tutorial": get("UI_MODE_TUTORIAL"),
    "advanced": get("UI_MODE_ADVANCED"),
    "sdk": get("UI_MODE_SDK"),
    "api-reference": get("UI_MODE_API_REF"),
}
site_title = f"{project_name} — {mode_labels.get(mode, 'Documentation')}"
emit("COMBINE_FORMAT_MKDOCS", mode=mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation"))
emit("COMBINE_CHAPTER_COUNT", count=len(chapter_files))

Sets up the output directory structure under docs/api/, resolves localized mode labels, and initializes chapter summary mappings used for navigation generation and index descriptions.

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM Nav Grouping and Dependency Resolution
docs.text:
if mode == "api-reference":
    module_facts = prep_res.get("module_facts") or {}
    with_facts = modules_with_facts(module_facts, chapter_files)
    has_facts = bool(with_facts)
    verified = verified_dependencies(module_facts, chapter_files)
if mode == "api-reference" and len(chapter_files) > 5:
    try:
        listed = sorted(zip(chapter_files, summaries, strict=True), key=lambda pair: tree_order_key(pair[0]))
        # ... formats prompt, invokes request_grouping ...
        parsed, sections = request_grouping(group_prompt, prep_res, chapter_files)
        descriptions, replied = grouping_extras(parsed, chapter_files)
        if has_facts:
            dependencies = {source: targets for source, targets in replied.items() if source not in with_facts} | verified
        else:
            dependencies = replied
        sections = order_sections(sections, chapter_files)
        # ... builds nav lines and marks grouped = True ...
    except Exception as e:
        emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK", error=e)

In api-reference mode with more than 5 modules, the function invokes request_grouping to obtain an LLM-designed section taxonomy. Inferred dependencies are merged with source-verified dependencies from facts.json. If grouping fails, it falls back to a directory-based layout via directory_sections.

docs.title: prune_stale_pages()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prune_stale_pages(api_docs_path, chapter_files):

Description: Deletes orphaned Markdown files and empty directories under docs/api/ that do not correspond to any current chapter or index page. Matches files by filesystem device and inode (st_dev, st_ino) to handle case-insensitive filesystem renames safely.

Parameters:

  • api_docs_path (str): Absolute filesystem path to docs/api/.
  • chapter_files (list[dict]): List of current active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def identity(path):
    st = os.stat(path)
    return st.st_dev, st.st_ino

keep = set()
for filename in ["index.md", *(cf["filename"] for cf in chapter_files)]:
    path = os.path.join(api_docs_path, filename)
    if os.path.exists(path):
        keep.add(identity(path))
# ... walks api_docs_path bottom-up, unlinking untracked .md files and empty dirs ...

The function walks the directory tree bottom-up (topdown=False). Any .md file whose inode identity is not in the keep set is unlinked with os.remove, and directories left empty are removed with os.rmdir.

docs.title: _sentences()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _sentences(text: str):

Description: Generator function that splits prose text into grammatical sentences. Uses regex pattern _SENTENCE_END_RE while inspecting trailing tokens via _ends_with_abbreviation to avoid splitting on common abbreviations like "e.g." or "vs.".

Parameters:

  • text (str): Prose text string to split.

Yields:

  • str: Individual sentence strings with punctuation preserved.

Example:

for match in _SENTENCE_END_RE.finditer(text):
    piece = text[start : match.start()]
    if not piece or _ends_with_abbreviation(piece):
        continue
    yield piece
    start = match.end()

docs.title: _ends_with_abbreviation()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _ends_with_abbreviation(piece: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a text segment terminates with a recognized abbreviation from _ABBREVIATIONS.

Parameters:

  • piece (str): Text fragment preceding a sentence boundary candidate.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the segment ends with a recognized abbreviation; otherwise False.

Example:

lower = piece.lower()
for abbreviation in _ABBREVIATIONS:
    if lower.endswith(abbreviation):
        before = lower[: -len(abbreviation)][-1:]
        if not before or not before.isalnum():
            return True
return False

docs.title: _is_prose()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _is_prose(text: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a line of text represents prose rather than a heading or label by checking for sentence-ending punctuation or CJK stop characters.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Line of text to evaluate.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the text contains sentence punctuation; otherwise False.

Example:

stripped = text.rstrip("*_ ")
return any(mark in text for mark in (". ", "! ", "? ", *_CJK_STOPS)) or stripped.endswith((".", "!", "?"))

docs.text:

Signature: def _section_members(sections: list) -> list[tuple[str, list]]:

Description: Flattens nested child sections into their top-level parent section, producing a list of (top_level_section_name, [module_name, ...]) tuples. Each module is assigned exclusively to the first section in which it appears.

Parameters:

def modules_of(section):

docs.title: _flattened_run()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _flattened_run(lines: list[str], index: int) -> int:

Description: Finds the ending boundary index of a flattened list run starting at index, identifying all subsequent lines that belong to that list item's indentation scope.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of all lines in the document.
  • index (int): Starting line index of the list item.

Returns:

  • int: Index of the first line following the end of the list run.

Example:

indent, end = _indent_of(lines[index]), index + 1
for position in range(index, len(lines)):
    if lines[position].strip():
        if _indent_of(lines[position]) < indent:
            break
        end = position + 1
return end

docs.title: _repair()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _repair(lines: list[str], kind: str, finding: dict) -> list[str]:

Description: Applies a single formatting repair to a list of Markdown lines. Inserts missing blank lines ahead of unspaced lists and tables, or re-indents flattened nested list runs by 4 spaces while preserving code block indentation.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): Document lines to modify.
  • kind (str): Repair category (lists_as_text, tables_as_text, or lists_flattened).
  • finding (dict): Issue descriptor dictionary containing the target line number.

Returns:

  • list[str]: New list of lines with the repair applied.

Example:

index = finding["line"] - 1
if kind in ("lists_as_text", "tables_as_text"):
    if index == 0 or not lines[index - 1].strip():
        return lines
    quote = re.match(r"^(?: {0,3}> ?)+", lines[index])
    return [*lines[:index], quote.group(0).rstrip() if quote else "", *lines[index:]]

For flattened lists, it calculates parent indentation, skips lines containing raw tabs, tracks nested list item boundaries using _ITEM_START_RE, and preserves code block indentation within fenced code spans using _FENCE_LINE_RE.

docs.title: _page_link()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _page_link(page: str, target: str, filenames: set) -> str:

Description: Computes a page-relative link from page to target. Pins relative paths with ./ when the relative path collides with another chapter's root path, and wraps destinations containing spaces or parentheses in angle brackets (<...>).

Parameters:

  • page (str): Referencing chapter path.
  • target (str): Destination chapter path.
  • filenames (set): Set of all known documentation filenames.

Returns:

  • str: Formatted link target string.

Example:

directory = posixpath.dirname(page)
relative = posixpath.relpath(target, directory) if directory else target
if directory and relative in filenames and relative != target:
    relative = f"./{relative}"
return f"<{relative}>" if re.search(r"[\s()]", relative) else relative

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive error handling patterns across parsing, network requests, and static site generation:

  1. LLM Grouping Retries: request_grouping wraps calls to call_llm in a retry loop with a maximum of GROUPING_ATTEMPTS (3) attempts and a GROUPING_WAIT delay (20 seconds). Non-retryable LLMRefusalError exceptions break the retry loop and re-raise immediately, while retryable refusals and timeout exceptions trigger backoff and telemetry events. If all attempts fail, the function raises the underlying exception, allowing write_mkdocs_output to catch it and fall back to directory_sections.
  2. Empty Section Pruning: Empty sections parsed from LLM responses are pruned by prune_sections. If no valid sections remain after pruning, request_grouping raises a localized ValueError(get("GROUP_NO_SECTIONS")).
  3. Renderer Fault Tolerance: site_renderer wraps Markdown parser initialization in a broad exception handler. If dependencies or extensions are missing, it emits a CHAPTER_CHECK_NO_RENDERER telemetry event and returns None, allowing the pipeline to proceed without markup verification.
  4. Render-Guarded Markup Repair: repair_markup tests candidate fixes against an in-memory MkDocs renderer, discarding any repair that alters visible text characters (_visible), changes code blocks (_code_blocks), or shifts CommonMark block assignments (markup_verdicts).
  5. Frontmatter Validation: split_frontmatter catches yaml.YAMLError and ValueError exceptions when parsing frontmatter blocks, ensuring that Markdown documents opening with horizontal rules (---) are not corrupted.

docs.text: Source: utils/output.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/output.py module provides the centralized output, console styling, and persistent file logging infrastructure for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder repository. It decouples the visual and structured reporting of pipeline events from operational execution logic. Instead of hardcoding log strings or print statements within workflow nodes, the entire system routes user-facing text through a centralized localization catalog (utils/strings.csv). This design supports dynamic {placeholder} token interpolation and multi-language translation.

The module operates as a hybrid logging engine, simultaneously handling formatted console output on standard streams and raw, timestamped entries in run-specific log files. To resolve ordering constraints where telemetry and authorization events occur before CLI arguments configure the destination log file, the module maintains an in-memory pending ring buffer. When the file logger initializes, this buffer flushes all preflight events into the active file in chronological order without log loss.

Additionally, utils/output.py safeguards against character encoding failures on Windows environments. When streams are redirected or piped, standard streams can default to legacy ANSI code pages (such as cp1252), leading to fatal encoding exceptions on non-English characters. The module detects redirected streams and transparently reconfigures standard I/O streams to UTF-8. It also bridges missing language localizations by delegating to LLM-driven translation passes, persisting discovered translations directly back to disk.

flowchart TD emitCall["emit(key, suffix, **kwargs)"] findKey{"Key found in _strings?"} printUnknown["print([UNKNOWN STRING: key])"] formatText["_format_safe(entry.text, kwargs)"] appendSuffix["Append suffix if provided"] checkDest{"Evaluate destination and _debug"} routeConsole["print(color + text + reset)"] routeFile["_write_log(level, text)"] checkLogOpen{"_log_file is None?"} bufferPending["Append to _pending_log"] checkOverflow{"len(_pending_log) > 5000?"} evictOldest["del _pending_log[0]"] diskWrite["Write timestamped line and flush"] emitCall --> findKey findKey -->|No| printUnknown findKey -->|Yes| formatText formatText --> appendSuffix appendSuffix --> checkDest checkDest -->|STDOUT or BOTH| routeConsole checkDest -->|LOG or BOTH| routeFile routeFile --> checkLogOpen checkLogOpen -->|Yes| bufferPending bufferPending --> checkOverflow checkOverflow -->|Yes| evictOldest checkOverflow -->|No| donePending["Pending Complete"] checkLogOpen -->|No| diskWrite classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class emitCall entryNode Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):

Description: Initializes the output subsystem, configuring localization targets, stream encodings, and string catalogs. It sets module-level configuration variables, validates UTF-8 streams for piped environments via _ensure_utf8_streams(), and reads the localization table from disk using _load_strings(). If auto_translate is enabled, it immediately initiates an LLM check to translate untranslated keys.

Parameters:

  • language (str): Target language name used for display and column resolution (e.g., "english", "Vietnamese"). Defaults to "english".
  • use_cache (bool): Flag indicating whether downstream LLM caching is active during automated string translation calls. Defaults to True.
  • thinking_level (str | None): LLM thinking effort level passed through to automated translation prompts. Defaults to None.
  • debug (bool): Global switch to enable verbose debug-level console output. Defaults to False.
  • auto_translate (bool): Whether to immediately run translation for missing strings during initialization. Defaults to True.

Returns:

  • None: Does not return a value; mutates internal module-level state.

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions internally; delegates stream reconfiguration and missing file checks defensively.

Example:

from utils.output import init as init_output

# Initialize output with default English localization
init_output(language="english")

# Initialize output with Vietnamese localization and debug logging
init_output(
    language="Vietnamese",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level="low",
    debug=True,
    auto_translate=False
)

The init function sets the internal runtime context required for all subsequent output operations across the system. It initializes display and CSV lookup names (_language and _lang_col) while establishing the filesystem path to strings.csv. Stream checking prevents non-TTY output redirection on Windows hosts from crashing on multi-byte characters. When auto_translate is deferred by callers such as main.py, initialization completes quickly without performing network I/O.

docs.title: translate_missing_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def translate_missing_strings():

Description: Dispatches an explicit request to find and translate any missing string definitions for the active target language. It acts as the public hook when deferred translation is configured in init(auto_translate=False).

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • None: Translates missing rows in place and updates internal state.

Raises:

  • Does not raise directly; network or parsing exceptions during translation are absorbed within the translation subsystem.

Example:

from utils.output import init as init_output, translate_missing_strings

# Defer translation during CLI initialization
init_output(language="Vietnamese", auto_translate=False)

# Execute translation after preflight credential checks pass
translate_missing_strings()

This method delegates execution directly to _auto_translate(). It separates CLI argument parsing and LLM authentication validation from API translation calls. This ensures that network requests to external providers occur only after credentials and project configurations are verified.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):

Description: Looks up a localized message from the internal catalog by key, formats it with provided keyword arguments, applies ANSI color coding according to its configured severity level, and routes the formatted string to stdout, the log file, or both.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Catalog key declared in strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER").
  • suffix (str): Optional additional text appended directly to the end of the formatted message prior to emission. Defaults to "".
  • **kwargs (Any): Variable keyword arguments applied to the message template via string formatting.

Returns:

  • None: Emits output to standard streams or files.

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions. If a key cannot be found, it outputs a diagnostic message [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] to prevent silent output drops.

Example:

from utils.output import emit

# Emit a progress event with placeholder variables and token breakdown suffix
emit(
    "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER",
    suffix=" (prompt=1,200, completion=850)",
    chapter_num=1,
    name="flow"
)

The function queries _strings using the provided key. If the key is unregistered, it prints [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] to stdout as a fallback and halts further processing. For registered keys, the string is populated via _format_safe before appending any suffix. Destination flags starting with "D" (such as "DBOTH" or "DSTDOUT") indicate debug gating: if _debug is disabled, the destination downgrades to "LOG", suppressing console noise while maintaining audit traces. ANSI escape sequences are retrieved from COLORS using the record's level and wrapped around the text when writing to console sinks.

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):

Description: Directly routes arbitrary, uncataloged text strings through the formatting and logging pipeline using an explicit severity level and destination target.

Parameters:

  • level (str): Severity identifier (e.g., "PROGRESS", "SUCCESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG").
  • text (str): Pre-formatted string to output.
  • dest (str): Target stream selector; accepts "BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG". Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns:

  • None: Renders output directly to selected destinations.

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Example:

from utils.output import emit_raw

# Output an informational banner to both console and log file
emit_raw("INFO", "Initializing codebase crawler pipeline...")

# Emit diagnostic data only to the log file
emit_raw("DEBUG", "Excluded path matched regex: tests/fixtures/*", dest="LOG")

emit_raw bypasses the strings.csv catalog, providing a direct interface for dynamic CLI displays, generated data tables, and batch processing status counters. If level is set to "DEBUG" while _debug is inactive, dest is reassigned to "LOG" to prevent console clutter. When dest includes stdout, ANSI color codes mapped from level are applied and reset using RESET. If dest includes file logging, execution is dispatched to _write_log.

Description: Resolves and returns a localized, formatted string from the catalog without sending output to standard streams or persistent log files.
